Step 1: Mathematical Form of Instantaneous Power
\[p = v i = (v_m \sin\omega t) [i_m \sin(\omega t + \phi)] = \frac{v_m i_m}{2} [\cos\phi - \cos(2\omega t + \phi)]\]

Step 2: Integration Over a Period
Taking the time-average over a period \(T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\):
\[\langle p \rangle = \frac{v_m i_m}{2} \cos\phi - \frac{v_m i_m}{2} \langle \cos(2\omega t + \phi) \rangle\]
The term \(\cos\phi\) is time-independent, so its average is \(\cos\phi\).

Step 3: Evaluation of the Time-Dependent Harmonic Term
\[\langle \cos(2\omega t + \phi) \rangle = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T \cos(2\omega t + \phi)\,\mathrm{d}t = \frac{1}{T} \left[ \frac{\sin(2\omega t + \phi)}{2\omega} \right]_0^T\]
Since \(2\omega T = 2\omega \left(\frac{2\pi}{\omega}\right) = 4\pi\), we have:
\[\sin(4\pi + \phi) - \sin(\phi) = \sin\phi - \sin\phi = 0\]

Step 4: Final Expression
\[P = \frac{v_m i_m}{2} \cos\phi = \left(\frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \left(\frac{i_m}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \cos\phi = V I \cos\phi\]

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The second term averages to zero over a full period.

चरण 1: तात्कालिक शक्ति का विस्तार
\[p = \frac{v_m i_m}{2} [\cos\phi - \cos(2\omega t + \phi)]\]

चरण 2: आवर्तकाल पर औसत
\[\langle p \rangle = \frac{v_m i_m}{2} \cos\phi - \frac{v_m i_m}{2} \langle \cos(2\omega t + \phi) \rangle\]
पहला पद समय से स्वतंत्र है।

चरण 3: ज्यावक्रीय पद का समाकलन
\(\cos(2\omega t + \phi)\) एक पूर्ण चक्र में समान रूप से धनात्मक और ऋणात्मक मान लेता है, अतः इसका निश्चित समाकलन शून्य होता है:
\[\frac{1}{T} \int_0^T \cos(2\omega t + \phi)\,\mathrm{d}t = 0\]

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
समय पर निर्भर पद का औसत शून्य होने के कारण केवल स्थिर पद बचता है: \(P = V I \cos\phi\)।

answer.text: Because the time-average of \(\cos(2\omega t + \phi)\) over a complete period is identically zero
Because current and voltage vanish at the end of each half cycle
Because the phase angle \(\phi\) is constrained to be zero at all instants

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q47 - Primary current calculation for real non-ideal transformer

questiontext.text:
A transformer with an operating efficiency of \(90.0\%\) delivers \(3.60\text{ kW}\) of electrical power at a secondary voltage of \(240\text{ V}\). If the primary supply voltage is \(1200\text{ V}\), what is the current drawn by the primary winding?

\(90.0\%\) कार्यदक्षता वाला एक ट्रांसफॉर्मर \(240\text{ V}\) की द्वितीयक वोल्टता पर \(3.60\text{ kW}\) विद्युत शक्ति प्रदान करता है। यदि प्राथमिक आपूर्ति वोल्टता \(1200\text{ V}\) है, तो प्राथमिक कुंडली द्वारा ली जाने वाली धारा क्या है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Efficiency \(\eta = 90.0\% = 0.900\); Output power \(P_{\text{out}} = 3.60\text{ kW} = 3600\text{ W}\); Secondary voltage \(V_s = 240\text{ V}\); Primary voltage \(V_p = 1200\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Relation Between Efficiency and Input Power
The efficiency of a transformer is defined as:
\[\eta = \frac{P_{\text{out}}}{P_{\text{in}}} \implies P_{\text{in}} = \frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta}\]

Step 3: Calculate Input Power
\[P_{\text{in}} = \frac{3600\text{ W}}{0.900} = 4000\text{ W}\]

Step 4: Calculate Primary Current
Assuming unity power factor for the input supply (\(P_{\text{in}} = V_p I_p\)):
\[I_p = \frac{P_{\text{in}}}{V_p} = \frac{4000\text{ W}}{1200\text{ V}} = \frac{10}{3}\text{ A} \approx 3.333\text{ A} \approx 3.33\text{ A}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The primary current drawn is \(3.33\text{ A}\).

चरण 1: दिया गया डेटा
दक्षता \(\eta = 90.0\% = 0.90\), निर्गत शक्ति \(P_{\text{out}} = 3600\text{ W}\), प्राथमिक वोल्टता \(V_p = 1200\text{ V}\)।

चरण 2: निवेशी शक्ति सूत्र
\[P_{\text{in}} = \frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta}\]

चरण 3: निवेशी शक्ति की गणना
\[P_{\text{in}} = \frac{3600}{0.90} = 4000\text{ W}\]

चरण 4: प्राथमिक धारा की गणना
\[I_p = \frac{P_{\text{in}}}{V_p} = \frac{4000}{1200} = \frac{10}{3}\text{ A} \approx 3.33\text{ A}\]

चरण 5: अंतिम उत्तर
प्राथमिक कुंडली द्वारा ली जाने वाली धारा \(3.33\text{ A}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q48 - Impedance frequency response in series LCR circuit

questiontext.text:
In a series \(LCR\) circuit, how does the circuit impedance \(Z\) vary as the driving angular frequency \(\omega\) increases continuously from \(\omega \to 0\) towards \(\omega \to \infty\)?

एक श्रेणीबद्ध \(LCR\) परिपथ में, जैसे-जैसे चालक कोणीय आवृत्ति \(\omega\) को \(\omega \to 0\) से \(\omega \to \infty\) तक लगातार बढ़ाया जाता है, परिपथ प्रतिबाधा \(Z\) किस प्रकार परिवर्तित होती है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula for Impedance
The impedance of a series \(LCR\) circuit is:
\[Z(\omega) = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(\omega L - \frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}\]

Step 2: Low-Frequency Limit (\(\omega \to 0\))
As \(\omega \to 0\), the inductive reactance vanishes (\(\omega L \to 0\)) while capacitive reactance diverges (\(\frac{1}{\omega C} \to \infty\)). Thus, \(Z \to \infty\).

Step 3: Resonant Frequency (\(\omega = \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\))
At \(\omega = \omega_0\), \(\omega L = \frac{1}{\omega C}\), making the reactive term zero. The impedance reaches its global minimum value:
\[Z_{\min} = R\]

Step 4: High-Frequency Limit (\(\omega \to \infty\))
As \(\omega \to \infty\), capacitive reactance vanishes (\(\frac{1}{\omega C} \to 0\)) while inductive reactance diverges (\(\omega L \to \infty\)). Thus, \(Z \to \infty\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The impedance starts from infinity, decreases to a minimum value \(R\) at resonance, and then increases without bound towards infinity.

चरण 1: प्रतिबाधा का सूत्र
\[Z(\omega) = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(\omega L - \frac{1}{\omega C}\right)^2}\]

चरण 2: निम्न आवृत्ति सीमा (\(\omega \to 0\))
जब \(\omega \to 0\), तो धारितीय प्रतिघात अनंत की ओर अग्रसर होता है (\(X_C \to \infty\)), अतः \(Z \to \infty\)।

चरण 3: अनुनादी आवृत्ति पर (\(\omega = \omega_0\))
\(X_L = X_C\) होने पर प्रतिघात शून्य हो जाता है और प्रतिबाधा न्यूनतम मान \(Z_{\min} = R\) प्राप्त करती है।

चरण 4: उच्च आवृत्ति सीमा (\(\omega \to \infty\))
जब \(\omega \to \infty\), तो प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात अनंत की ओर अग्रसर होता है (\(X_L \to \infty\)), अतः \(Z \to \infty\)।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
प्रतिबाधा अनंत से घटकर अनुनाद पर न्यूनतम मान \(R\) प्राप्त करती है, और फिर पुनः अनंत की ओर बढ़ती है।

answer.text: Increases monotonically from zero to infinity without reaching any minimum
Decreases continuously from infinity to zero as frequency approaches infinity
Remains constant at value R across the entire frequency range
Decreases from infinity to a minimum value R at resonance, then increases indefinitely towards infinity

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q01 - Phase relationship and power in pure resistor circuit

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a purely resistive alternating current circuit, the alternating voltage across the resistor and the alternating current flowing through it are in phase with each other.

Statement II: The average power dissipated in a purely resistive alternating current circuit over one complete cycle is non-zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक विशुद्ध प्रतिरोधक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा परिपथ में, प्रतिरोधक के सिरों पर प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता और उससे प्रवाहित होने वाली प्रत्यावर्ती धारा एक दूसरे के साथ समान कला में होती हैं।

कथन II: एक पूर्ण चक्र में एक विशुद्ध प्रतिरोधक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा परिपथ में क्षयित औसत शक्ति अशून्य होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When an alternating voltage \(v = v_m \sin\omega t\) is applied across a pure resistor of resistance \(R\), the instantaneous current is given by Ohm's law: \(i = \frac{v_m}{R} \sin\omega t = i_m \sin\omega t\).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
Both voltage \(v\) and current \(i\) reach zero, maximum, and minimum values at the exact same respective instants in time. The phase angle difference between them is \(\phi = 0\), which confirms that alternating voltage and current in a pure resistor are strictly in phase. Thus, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
Although the algebraic sum of the current over a complete period is zero (\(\langle i \rangle = 0\)), electrical energy dissipation depends on Joule heating \(i^2 R\). Because \(i^2\) is positive throughout both half-cycles, the cycle-averaged power is \(\overline{p} = \frac{1}{2} i_m^2 R = I^2 R > 0\). Thus, the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
जब \(R\) प्रतिरोध वाले विशुद्ध प्रतिरोधक पर प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता \(v = v_m \sin\omega t\) लगाई जाती है, तो तात्क्षणिक धारा \(i = i_m \sin\omega t\) होती है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
वोल्टता \(v\) और धारा \(i\) दोनों एक ही समय पर शून्य, अधिकतम और न्यूनतम मान प्राप्त करते हैं। उनके बीच कलान्तर \(\phi = 0\) होता है, अतः वे समान कला में होते हैं। अतः प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
यद्यपि एक चक्र में औसत धारा शून्य होती है, जूल तापन \(i^2 R\) पर निर्भर करता है। चूँकि \(i^2\) सदैव धनात्मक होता है, औसत शक्ति \(\overline{p} = I^2 R > 0\) होती है। अतः द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः दोनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q02 - Average current over cycle and phase in pure inductor

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The average value of a symmetrical sinusoidal alternating current over one complete cycle is equal to its root-mean-square value.

Statement II: In a purely inductive alternating current circuit, the alternating current leads the alternating voltage by a phase angle of \(\pi/2\) radians.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक पूर्ण चक्र में एक सममित ज्यावक्रीय प्रत्यावर्ती धारा का औसत मान इसके वर्ग-माध्य-मूल मान के बराबर होता है।

कथन II: एक विशुद्ध प्रेरकीय प्रत्यावर्ती धारा परिपथ में, प्रत्यावर्ती धारा प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता से \(\pi/2\) रेडियन के कला कोण से अग्रगामी होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A sinusoidal alternating quantity is symmetric about the time axis over its period \(T\). The behavior of current in reactive elements is determined by Faraday's and Kirchhoff's laws.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
Over one complete cycle, the positive half-cycle and negative half-cycle cancel algebraically, yielding an average current of \(\langle i \rangle = \frac{1}{T} \int_0^T i_m \sin\omega t \, \mathrm{d}t = 0\). The root-mean-square current is non-zero and equals \(I = \frac{i_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 i_m\). Hence, the average value is zero, not equal to the rms value. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
In a purely inductive circuit, \(v = L \frac{\mathrm{d}i}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Integrating gives \(i = i_m \sin\left(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). This demonstrates that the current lags behind the voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians (\(90^\circ\)), rather than leading it. Thus, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
ज्यावक्रीय प्रत्यावर्ती राशि अपने आवर्तकाल \(T\) में समय-अक्ष के परितः सममित होती है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
एक पूर्ण चक्र में धनात्मक और ऋणात्मक अर्ध-चक्र परस्पर निरस्त हो जाते हैं, जिससे औसत मान \(\langle i \rangle = 0\) होता है, जबकि rms मान \(I = \frac{i_m}{\sqrt{2}}\) होता है। अतः औसत मान rms मान के बराबर नहीं होता। अतः प्रथम कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
शुद्ध प्रेरकीय परिपथ में धारा \(i = i_m \sin\left(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) होती है, अर्थात धारा वोल्टता से \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) पश्चगामी होती है, अग्रगामी नहीं। अतः द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q03 - Effective current definition and moving coil meter response

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: One ampere of root-mean-square alternating current produces the identical average heating effect in a given resistor as one ampere of steady direct current under identical conditions.

Statement II: Standard direct-current moving-coil meters can directly measure the root-mean-square value of a sinusoidal alternating current because their deflection is proportional to effective current.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक ऐम्पियर वर्ग-माध्य-मूल प्रत्यावर्ती धारा किसी दिए गए प्रतिरोधक में समान परिस्थितियों में एक ऐम्पियर स्थिर दिष्ट धारा के समान ही औसत तापन प्रभाव उत्पन्न करती है।

कथन II: मानक दिष्ट-धारा चल-कुंडली मीटर ज्यावक्रीय प्रत्यावर्ती धारा के वर्ग-माध्य-मूल मान को सीधे माप सकते हैं क्योंकि उनका विक्षेप प्रभावी धारा के अनुक्रमानुपाती होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The root-mean-square (effective) value of alternating current is defined physically through Joule heating: \(P = I^2 R\). Moving-coil dc instruments respond to the time-averaged magnetic force proportional to current: \(\tau \propto i\).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
By standard definition (Section 7.2 and Points to Ponder 4), the rms current \(I\) represents the equivalent direct current that produces the exact same average heating dissipation in a resistor over a full period. Thus, \(1\text{ A}\) rms ac produces the exact same Joule heat as \(1\text{ A}\) dc. Thus, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
A standard moving-coil galvanometer responds to the average current \(\langle i \rangle\). For alternating current, the magnetic force reverses direction every half-cycle, and because mechanical inertia prevents the pointer from following rapid oscillations, the meter reads zero (\(\langle i \rangle = 0\)). Hot-wire instruments, which respond to \(i^2\), must be used instead. Thus, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रत्यावर्ती धारा का वर्ग-माध्य-मूल मान जूल तापन के आधार पर परिभाषित किया जाता है: \(P = I^2 R\)। चल-कुंडली दिष्ट-धारा उपकरण धारा के औसत मान के प्रति अनुक्रिया करते हैं।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
परिभाषा के अनुसार, \(1\text{ A}\) rms ac धारा किसी प्रतिरोधक में ठीक उतना ही औसत तापन प्रभाव उत्पन्न करती है जितना कि \(1\text{ A}\) dc धारा। अतः प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
चल-कुंडली गैल्वेनोमीटर औसत धारा \(\langle i \rangle\) पर प्रतिक्रिया देता है। ac के एक पूर्ण चक्र में औसत मान शून्य होने के कारण इसका पाठ्यांक शून्य होता है, यह rms मान नहीं माप सकता। rms मान मापने के लिए तप्त-तार उपकरणों का उपयोग किया जाता है। अतः द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः प्रथम कथन सही है, लेकिन द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q04 - Frequency dependence of inductive and capacitive reactances

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The inductive reactance of an inductor decreases linearly as the frequency of the alternating voltage source increases.

Statement II: The capacitive reactance of a capacitor decreases inversely as the frequency of the alternating voltage source increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता स्रोत की आवृत्ति बढ़ने पर किसी प्रेरक का प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात रैखिक रूप से घटता है।

कथन II: प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता स्रोत की आवृत्ति बढ़ने पर किसी संधारित्र का धारितीय प्रतिघात व्युत्क्रमानुपाती रूप से घटता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The inductive reactance of an inductor of self-inductance \(L\) is \(X_L = \omega L = 2\pi u L\). The capacitive reactance of a capacitor of capacitance \(C\) is \(X_C = rac{1}{\omega C} = rac{1}{2\pi u C}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
The expression \(X_L = 2\pi u L\) shows that inductive reactance is directly proportional to frequency \( u\). Therefore, as frequency increases, inductive reactance increases linearly, rather than decreasing. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
The expression \(X_C = rac{1}{2\pi u C}\) shows that capacitive reactance is inversely proportional to frequency \( u\). As frequency increases, \(X_C\) decreases towards zero. Thus, the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात \(X_L = 2\pi u L\) तथा धारितीय प्रतिघात \(X_C = rac{1}{2\pi u C}\) होता है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
चूँकि \(X_L \propto u\), आवृत्ति बढ़ने पर प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात रैखिक रूप से बढ़ता है, घटता नहीं। अतः प्रथम कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
चूँकि \(X_C \propto rac{1}{ u}\), आवृत्ति बढ़ने पर धारितीय प्रतिघात व्युत्क्रमानुपाती रूप से घटता है। अतः द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः प्रथम कथन गलत है, लेकिन द्वितीय कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q05 - Dimensions of reactances and wattless power dissipation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The physical dimensions of both inductive reactance and capacitive reactance are identical to the dimension of electrical resistance, and both have the SI unit of ohm (\(\Omega\)).

Statement II: An alternating current flowing through an ideal pure inductor or an ideal pure capacitor consumes zero net power over a complete cycle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात और धारितीय प्रतिघात दोनों की भौतिक विमाएँ विद्युत प्रतिरोध की विमा के समान होती हैं, और दोनों का SI मात्रक ओम (\(\Omega\)) होता है।

कथन II: एक आदर्श शुद्ध प्रेरक या एक आदर्श शुद्ध संधारित्र से प्रवाहित होने वाली प्रत्यावर्ती धारा एक पूर्ण चक्र में शून्य कुल शक्ति का उपभोग करती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reactance represents the opposition to the flow of alternating current offered by inductors and capacitors, defined via current amplitudes: \(X_L = \frac{v_m}{i_m}\) and \(X_C = \frac{v_m}{i_m}\). Average power is \(P = V I \cos\phi\).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
Because both \(X_L\) and \(X_C\) represent voltage amplitude divided by current amplitude, their dimensions are \([\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-3} \text{A}^{-2}]\), which is identical to electrical resistance, and their SI unit is the ohm (\(\Omega\)). Thus, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
In an ideal inductor, current lags voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) (\(\cos\phi = \cos(-90^\circ) = 0\)). In an ideal capacitor, current leads voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) (\(\cos\phi = \cos 90^\circ = 0\)). Consequently, average power \(P = V I \cos\phi = 0\text{ W}\) for both purely reactive elements over a full cycle. Thus, the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रतिघात ac धारा के प्रवाह में विरोध को दर्शाता है: \(X = \frac{v_m}{i_m}\)। औसत शक्ति \(P = V I \cos\phi\) होती है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
चूँकि प्रतिघात वोल्टता और धारा का अनुपात है, इसकी विमा \([\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-3} \text{A}^{-2}]\) प्रतिरोध के समान होती है और SI मात्रक ओम (\(\Omega\)) होता है। अतः प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
शुद्ध प्रेरक और शुद्ध संधारित्र दोनों के लिए कलान्तर \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) होता है, जिससे शक्ति गुणांक \(\cos\phi = 0\) होता है। अतः एक पूर्ण चक्र में दोनों के लिए औसत शक्ति शून्य होती है। अतः द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः दोनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q06 - Voltage summation in series RC and resonance requirements

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In an alternating current series circuit containing a resistor and a capacitor, the total rms voltage across the combination is equal to the simple algebraic sum of the individual rms voltages across the resistor and capacitor.

Statement II: Electrical resonance can occur in an alternating current circuit consisting of only a resistor and a capacitor connected in series to an alternating voltage source.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक प्रतिरोधक और एक संधारित्र वाले प्रत्यावर्ती धारा श्रेणी परिपथ में, संयोजन के सिरों पर कुल rms वोल्टता प्रतिरोधक और संधारित्र के सिरों पर अलग-अलग rms वोल्टताओं के सरल बीजीय योग के बराबर होती है।

कथन II: प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता स्रोत से श्रेणीक्रम में जुड़े केवल एक प्रतिरोधक और एक संधारित्र वाले प्रत्यावर्ती धारा परिपथ में वैद्युत अनुनाद हो सकता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In series ac circuits, voltages across different components differ in phase and must be added vectorially using phasors. Electrical resonance requires cancellation of reactive voltages.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
The voltage across the capacitor \(V_C\) lags the voltage across the resistor \(V_R\) by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians (\(90^\circ\)). Therefore, the total source voltage is given by Pythagorean addition: \(V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + V_C^2}\), which is strictly less than the algebraic sum \(V_R + V_C\). Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
Resonance requires inductive reactance and capacitive reactance to cancel each other (\(X_L = X_C\)), which requires the presence of both an inductor \(L\) and a capacitor \(C\). An \(RC\) circuit lacks an inductor, so reactive cancellation cannot occur and resonance cannot be exhibited. Thus, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
श्रेणीबद्ध ac परिपथ में विभिन्न अवयवों की वोल्टताएँ फेजर रूप में जोड़ी जाती हैं। अनुनाद के लिए प्रतिघातों का परस्पर निरसन आवश्यक है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
\(V_R\) और \(V_C\) के बीच \(90^\circ\) का कलान्तर होने के कारण कुल वोल्टता \(V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + V_C^2}\) होती है, जो बीजीय योग \(V_R + V_C\) के बराबर नहीं होती। अतः प्रथम कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
वैद्युत अनुनाद केवल तभी हो सकता है जब परिपथ में \(L\) और \(C\) दोनों उपस्थित हों ताकि \(X_L = X_C\) पर वोल्टताएँ निरस्त हो सकें। केवल \(RC\) परिपथ में अनुनाद संभव नहीं है। अतः द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q07 - Series resonance impedance minimum and power factor value

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At electrical resonance in a series \(LCR\) circuit, the total circuit impedance attains its minimum possible value equal to the resistance \(R\), resulting in maximum current amplitude.

Statement II: At electrical resonance in a series \(LCR\) circuit, the power factor of the circuit is zero because the inductive reactance completely cancels the capacitive reactance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक श्रेणीबद्ध \(LCR\) परिपथ में वैद्युत अनुनाद की स्थिति में, परिपथ की कुल प्रतिबाधा प्रतिरोध \(R\) के बराबर अपना न्यूनतम संभव मान प्राप्त करती है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप धारा का आयाम अधिकतम होता है।

कथन II: एक श्रेणीबद्ध \(LCR\) परिपथ में वैद्युत अनुनाद की स्थिति में, परिपथ का शक्ति गुणांक शून्य होता है क्योंकि प्रेरकीय प्रतिघात धारितीय प्रतिघात को पूरी तरह से निरस्त कर देता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In a series \(LCR\) circuit, impedance is \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}\), current amplitude is \(i_m = \frac{v_m}{Z}\), and the power factor is \(\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
At resonance (\(\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\)), \(X_L = X_C\), which makes \((X_L - X_C)^2 = 0\). The impedance reaches its absolute minimum, \(Z = R\). Consequently, the current amplitude reaches its peak maximum, \(i_m = \frac{v_m}{R}\). Thus, the first statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
Because \(Z = R\) at resonance, the phase difference is \(\phi = 0\). The power factor is \(\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{R}{R} = 1\), which is unity (maximum possible power factor), not zero. Power dissipation is at its maximum: \(P = I^2 R\). Thus, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
श्रेणीबद्ध \(LCR\) परिपथ में प्रतिबाधा \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}\) तथा शक्ति गुणांक \(\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}\) होता है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
अनुनाद पर \(X_L = X_C\) होने के कारण प्रतिबाधा न्यूनतम \(Z = R\) हो जाती है और धारा आयाम अधिकतम \(i_m = \frac{v_m}{R}\) हो जाता है। अतः प्रथम कथन सही है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
अनुनाद पर \(Z = R\) होने से शक्ति गुणांक \(\cos\phi = \frac{R}{R} = 1\) (इकाई/अधिकतम) होता है, शून्य नहीं। अतः द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः प्रथम कथन सही है, लेकिन द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q08 - Step-up transformer current relationship and transmission losses

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In an ideal step-up transformer, the output voltage across the secondary coil is greater than the input voltage, and consequently the output current in the secondary coil is also greater than the input current.

Statement II: Long-distance transmission of electrical energy is carried out at high alternating voltages because reducing the transmission current substantially cuts down the \(I^2 R\) Joule heating losses in the cables.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक आदर्श उच्चायी ट्रांसफॉर्मर में, द्वितीयक कुंडली पर निर्गत वोल्टता निवेशी वोल्टता से अधिक होती है, और परिणामस्वरूप द्वितीयक कुंडली में निर्गत धारा भी निवेशी धारा से अधिक होती है।

कथन II: विद्युत ऊर्जा का लंबी दूरी का संचरण उच्च प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता पर किया जाता है क्योंकि संचरण धारा को कम करने से केबलों में \(I^2 R\) जूल ऊष्मा हानि काफी कम हो जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
For an ideal transformer, energy conservation requires input power to equal output power: \(V_p I_p = V_s I_s\), yielding \(\frac{I_s}{I_p} = \frac{V_p}{V_s} = \frac{N_p}{N_s}\). Cable Joule loss is \(P_{\text{loss}} = I^2 R_c\).

Step 2: Evaluation of First Statement
In a step-up transformer, \(N_s > N_p\), so \(V_s > V_p\). According to power conservation, current must decrease proportionally: \(I_s = \left(\frac{N_p}{N_s}\right) I_p < I_p\). The secondary current is strictly smaller than the primary current, not greater. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Statement
Transmitting power \(P = V I\) at elevated voltage \(V\) reduces line current \(I = \frac{P}{V}\). The transmission heating dissipation is \(P_{\text{loss}} = I^2 R_c = \frac{P^2 R_c}{V^2}\), which decreases inversely with the square of the voltage. Thus, high-voltage transmission drastically cuts down power loss. Thus, the second statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
आदर्श ट्रांसफॉर्मर के लिए ऊर्जा संरक्षण से \(V_p I_p = V_s I_s\) होता है, जिससे \(\frac{I_s}{I_p} = \frac{V_p}{V_s} = \frac{N_p}{N_s}\)। संचरण हानि \(P_{\text{loss}} = I^2 R_c\) होती है।

चरण 2: प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
उच्चायी ट्रांसफॉर्मर में \(V_s > V_p\) होने पर ऊर्जा संरक्षण के अनुसार द्वितीयक धारा कम होनी चाहिए: \(I_s < I_p\)। अतः द्वितीयक धारा प्राथमिक धारा से कम होती है, अधिक नहीं। अतः प्रथम कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
उच्च वोल्टता \(V\) पर संचरण करने से धारा \(I = \frac{P}{V}\) कम हो जाती है, जिससे केबलों में \(I^2 R_c\) जूल तापन हानि अत्यधिक कम हो जाती है। अतः द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
अतः प्रथम कथन गलत है, लेकिन द्वितीय कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q01 - Phase relationships in pure resistive inductive and capacitive AC circuits

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In a purely resistive alternating current circuit, the phase difference between the alternating voltage and the alternating current is zero.

Statement II: In a purely inductive alternating current circuit, the alternating current lags behind the alternating voltage by a phase angle of \(\pi/2\) radians.

Statement III: In a purely capacitive alternating current circuit, the alternating current lags behind the alternating voltage by a phase angle of \(\pi/2\) radians.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक विशुद्ध प्रतिरोधक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा परिपथ में, प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता और प्रत्यावर्ती धारा के बीच कलान्तर शून्य होता है।

कथन II: एक विशुद्ध प्रेरकीय प्रत्यावर्ती धारा परिपथ में, प्रत्यावर्ती धारा प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता से \(\pi/2\) रेडियन के कला कोण से पश्चगामी होती है।

कथन III: एक विशुद्ध धारितीय प्रत्यावर्ती धारा परिपथ में, प्रत्यावर्ती धारा प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता से \(\pi/2\) रेडियन के कला कोण से पश्चगामी होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles
For an alternating voltage \(v = v_m \sin\omega t\), the current response depends fundamentally on the nature of the circuit element.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement I
For a purely resistive circuit of resistance \(R\), Ohm's law gives \(i = \frac{v_m}{R} \sin\omega t = i_m \sin\omega t\). Both voltage and current reach zero, maximum, and minimum simultaneously. The phase difference is \(\phi = 0\). Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement II
For a purely inductive circuit of self-inductance \(L\), Kirchhoff's loop rule gives \(v - L \frac{\mathrm{d}i}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0\). Integrating gives \(i = i_m \sin\left(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). This indicates that the current lags behind the voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians (\(90^\circ\)). Thus, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Analysis of Statement III
For a purely capacitive circuit of capacitance \(C\), the current is \(i = \frac{\mathrm{d}q}{\mathrm{d}t} = \omega C v_m \cos\omega t = i_m \sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). This indicates that the current leads the voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) radians, rather than lagging behind it. Thus, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement I and Statement II only are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता \(v = v_m \sin\omega t\) के लिए परिपथ में धारा की अनुक्रिया अवयव की प्रकृति पर निर्भर करती है।

चरण 2: कथन I का विश्लेषण
विशुद्ध प्रतिरोधक परिपथ में ओम के नियम से तात्क्षणिक धारा \(i = i_m \sin\omega t\) होती है। वोल्टता और धारा एक ही समय पर अपने चरम मान प्राप्त करते हैं, अतः कलान्तर \(\phi = 0\) होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का विश्लेषण
विशुद्ध प्रेरकीय परिपथ में \(v - L \frac{\mathrm{d}i}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0\) से धारा \(i = i_m \sin\left(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) प्राप्त होती है। यहाँ धारा वोल्टता से \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) रेडियन पश्चगामी होती है। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: कथन III का विश्लेषण
विशुद्ध धारितीय परिपथ में धारा \(i = \frac{\mathrm{d}q}{\mathrm{d}t} = i_m \sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) होती है। यहाँ धारा वोल्टता से \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) रेडियन अग्रगामी होती है, पश्चगामी नहीं। अतः कथन III गलत है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन I और कथन II सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q02 - RMS current relation and cycle-averaged power in reactive elements

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: For a sinusoidal alternating current, the root-mean-square current \(I\) is related to the peak current \(i_m\) by the relation \(I = \frac{i_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707\,i_m\).

Statement II: The average power consumed over a complete cycle by an alternating current in an ideal inductor of inductance \(L\) is non-zero and equals \(\frac{1}{2} L I^2\).

Statement III: The current in a purely capacitive circuit is referred to as a wattless current because the net electrical energy dissipated as heat over a complete cycle is zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक ज्यावक्रीय प्रत्यावर्ती धारा के लिए, वर्ग-माध्य-मूल धारा \(I\) और शिखर धारा \(i_m\) के बीच संबंध \(I = \frac{i_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707\,i_m\) होता है।

कथन II: एक पूर्ण चक्र में प्रेरकत्व \(L\) वाले एक आदर्श प्रेरक में प्रत्यावर्ती धारा द्वारा उपभुक्त औसत शक्ति अशून्य होती है और \(\frac{1}{2} L I^2\) के बराबर होती है।

कथन III: एक विशुद्ध धारितीय परिपथ में धारा को वाटहीन धारा कहा जाता है क्योंकि एक पूर्ण चक्र में ऊष्मा के रूप में क्षयित कुल विद्युत ऊर्जा शून्य होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles
The effective value of an alternating current is defined by root-mean-square calculation, and power dissipation over a complete cycle depends on the circuit's power factor \(\cos\phi\).

Step 2: Analysis of Statement I
The rms current is defined as \(I = \sqrt{\langle i^2 \rangle} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T} \int_0^T i_m^2 \sin^2\omega t \, \mathrm{d}t} = \frac{i_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707\,i_m\). Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement II
The instantaneous power in an inductor is \(p_L = v i = - \frac{i_m v_m}{2} \sin(2\omega t)\). The average value of \(\sin(2\omega t)\) over a full period \(T\) is strictly zero (\(\langle \sin 2\omega t \rangle = 0\)). The quantity \(\frac{1}{2} L I^2\) represents peak stored magnetic energy in the inductor core, not power consumed per second. Hence, the average power dissipated is zero, not non-zero. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Analysis of Statement III
In a purely capacitive circuit, the current leads the voltage by \(\phi = \pi/2\). The power factor is \(\cos(\pi/2) = 0\), so the average power dissipated is \(P = V I \cos\phi = 0\). A current carrying zero average power dissipation is termed a wattless current. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement I and Statement III only are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रत्यावर्ती धारा का प्रभावी मान वर्ग-माध्य-मूल गणना द्वारा निर्धारित होता है तथा चक्र-औसत शक्ति शक्ति गुणांक \(\cos\phi\) पर निर्भर करती है।

चरण 2: कथन I का विश्लेषण
वर्ग-माध्य-मूल धारा की परिभाषा से \(I = \sqrt{\langle i^2 \rangle} = \frac{i_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707\,i_m\) होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का विश्लेषण
प्रेरक में तात्क्षणिक शक्ति \(p_L = -\frac{i_m v_m}{2} \sin(2\omega t)\) होती है। पूर्ण चक्र में \(\langle \sin 2\omega t \rangle = 0\) होने से औसत शक्ति शून्य होती है। राशि \(\frac{1}{2} L I^2\) अधिकतम संचित चुंबकीय ऊर्जा है, उपभुक्त शक्ति नहीं। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन III का विश्लेषण
विशुद्ध धारितीय परिपथ में \(\phi = \pi/2\) होने से शक्ति गुणांक \(\cos(\pi/2) = 0\) होता है, जिससे औसत शक्ति \(P = V I \cos\phi = 0\) होती है। शून्य शक्ति क्षय वाली इस धारा को वाटहीन धारा कहा जाता है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन I और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q03 - Necessary conditions for resonance phase angle and quality factor in series LCR

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Electrical resonance can readily occur in an alternating current circuit consisting of only a pure resistor and a pure inductor connected in series with an ac source.

Statement II: At electrical resonance in a series LCR circuit, the phase angle between the alternating source voltage and the circuit current is zero.

Statement III: The quality factor \(Q\) of a series LCR circuit is given by \(Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}\) and is a dimensionless quantity that measures the sharpness of resonance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा स्रोत के साथ श्रेणीक्रम में जुड़े केवल एक विशुद्ध प्रतिरोधक और एक विशुद्ध प्रेरक वाले परिपथ में विद्युत अनुनाद सुगमता से हो सकता है।

कथन II: एक श्रेणी LCR परिपथ में विद्युत अनुनाद पर, प्रत्यावर्ती स्रोत वोल्टता और परिपथ धारा के बीच कला कोण शून्य होता है।

कथन III: एक श्रेणी LCR परिपथ का विशेषता गुणांक (Quality factor) \(Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}\) द्वारा दिया जाता है और यह एक विमाहीन राशि है जो अनुनाद की तीक्ष्णता को मापती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles
Resonance in an ac circuit requires cancellation of reactive voltages. The sharpness of resonance is parameterized by the quality factor \(Q\).

Step 2: Analysis of Statement I
Electrical resonance occurs when the inductive and capacitive reactances balance each other (\(X_L = X_C\)), which requires both \(L\) and \(C\) elements to be present simultaneously in the circuit. In an RL circuit, capacitance is absent, so the total impedance \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}\) increases monotonically with frequency and voltage cancellation cannot occur. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement II
In a series LCR circuit, the phase angle is given by \(\tan\phi = \frac{X_L - X_C}{R}\). At resonance, \(X_L = X_C\), which gives \(\tan\phi = 0\) and therefore \(\phi = 0\). This means the applied voltage and resulting current are in phase. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Analysis of Statement III
The quality factor is defined as \(Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{1}{\omega_0 C R}\). Since both \(\omega_0 L\) and \(R\) have dimensions of electrical resistance (ohms, \(\Omega\)), their ratio is dimensionless. It describes the selectivity or sharpness of the resonance peak. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement II and Statement III only are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
प्रत्यावर्ती परिपथ में अनुनाद के लिए प्रतिघाती वोल्टताओं का परस्पर निरसन आवश्यक होता है तथा तीक्ष्णता विशेषता गुणांक \(Q\) द्वारा व्यक्त की जाती है।

चरण 2: कथन I का विश्लेषण
अनुनाद परिघटना के लिए \(X_L = X_C\) होना अनिवार्य है, जिसके लिए परिपथ में \(L\) और \(C\) दोनों तत्वों की उपस्थिति आवश्यक है। केवल RL परिपथ में धारिता अनुपस्थित होने के कारण वोल्टता निरसन संभव नहीं है, अतः अनुनाद नहीं हो सकता। अतः कथन I गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन II का विश्लेषण
श्रेणी LCR परिपथ में कलान्तर \(\tan\phi = \frac{X_L - X_C}{R}\) होता है। अनुनाद पर \(X_L = X_C\) होने से \(\tan\phi = 0\) अर्थात \(\phi = 0\) होता है, जिससे वोल्टता और धारा समान कला में होते हैं। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: कथन III का विश्लेषण
विशेषता गुणांक \(Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}\) होता है। चूँकि अंश और हर दोनों का मात्रक ओम (\(\Omega\)) है, यह एक विमाहीन राशि है जो अनुनाद वक्र की तीक्ष्णता को दर्शाती है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन II और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q04 - Transformation ratios conservation of energy and eddy current mitigation in transformers

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In an ideal transformer, the ratio of secondary voltage to primary voltage equals the turns ratio: \(\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}\).

Statement II: In an ideal step-up transformer where \(N_s > N_p\), the secondary alternating current is less than the primary alternating current in accordance with the law of conservation of energy.

Statement III: In practical transformers, energy dissipation caused by eddy currents induced in the iron core is minimized by constructing the core from thin, electrically insulated laminations.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक आदर्श ट्रांसफार्मर में, द्वितीयक वोल्टता और प्राथमिक वोल्टता का अनुपात फेरों के अनुपात के बराबर होता है: \(\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}\)।

कथन II: एक आदर्श उच्चायी (step-up) ट्रांसफार्मर में जहाँ \(N_s > N_p\) होता है, ऊर्जा संरक्षण के नियमानुसार द्वितीयक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा प्राथमिक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा से कम होती है।

कथन III: व्यावहारिक ट्रांसफार्मरों में, लोहे के क्रोड में प्रेरित भंवर धाराओं के कारण होने वाले ऊर्जा क्षय को क्रोड को पतली, विद्युत-रोधी पट्टिकाओं (laminations) से बनाकर न्यूनतम किया जाता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles
Transformers operate on mutual induction. For an ideal transformer, complete magnetic flux linkage and energy conservation govern voltage and current transformations.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement I
By Faraday's law of induction, the induced emf per turn in the iron core is identical: \(\frac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Hence, \(V_s = -N_s \frac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t}\) and \(V_p = -N_p \frac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Taking the ratio gives \(\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}\). Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement II
By the law of conservation of energy, for an ideal transformer with zero power loss, the input electrical power equals the output electrical power: \(V_p I_p = V_s I_s\). In a step-up transformer, \(V_s > V_p\), which mathematically mandates that \(I_s = \left(\frac{V_p}{V_s}\right) I_p < I_p\). Therefore, stepping up the voltage proportionally steps down the current. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Analysis of Statement III
The time-varying magnetic flux induces closed circular circulating currents (eddy currents) within the bulk conductive iron core, generating unwanted Joule heat. Using thin laminations stacked with insulating varnish breaks the broad conduction loops into narrow paths of much higher electrical resistance, significantly diminishing eddy current amplitude and power dissipation. Thus, Statement III is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
ट्रांसफार्मर अन्योन्य प्रेरण के सिद्धांत पर कार्य करता है। आदर्श ट्रांसफार्मर में पूर्ण फ्लक्स युग्मन और ऊर्जा संरक्षण लागू होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का विश्लेषण
फैराडे के प्रेरण नियम के अनुसार, क्रोड में प्रति फेरा प्रेरित वि.वा.बल समान होता है। अतः \(V_s = -N_s \frac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t}\) और \(V_p = -N_p \frac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t}\) से अनुपात \(\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का विश्लेषण
ऊर्जा संरक्षण के नियमानुसार, शून्य शक्ति हानि वाले आदर्श ट्रांसफार्मर में निवेशी शक्ति निर्गत शक्ति के बराबर होती है (\(V_p I_p = V_s I_s\))। उच्चायी ट्रांसफार्मर में \(V_s > V_p\) होने से द्वितीयक धारा \(I_s = \frac{V_p}{V_s} I_p < I_p\) होती है। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: कथन III का विश्लेषण
समय-परिवर्ती चुंबकीय फ्लक्स लोहे के ठोस क्रोड में भंवर धाराएं प्रेरित करता है जिससे जूल ऊष्मा के रूप में ऊर्जा हानि होती है। विद्युत-रोधी वार्निश युक्त पतली पटलित (laminated) पत्तियों का उपयोग करने से धारा के संवहन पथ का प्रतिरोध बढ़ जाता है और भंवर धारा हानि न्यूनतम हो जाती है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I, कथन II और कथन III तीनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_AC_MATCH_Q01 - Circuit elements and phase differences

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Circuit Configuration) List II (Phase Difference Between Current and Voltage)
A. Purely resistive ac circuit I. Current lags voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\)
B. Purely inductive ac circuit II. Current and voltage are in phase (\(\phi = 0\)) with maximum current
C. Purely capacitive ac circuit III. Current and voltage are in phase (\(\phi = 0\))
D. Series LCR circuit at resonance IV. Current leads voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The phase relationship between alternating voltage \(v(t) = v_m \sin(\omega t)\) and alternating current \(i(t) = i_m \sin(\omega t + \phi)\) is governed by the reactive and resistive properties of the components in the circuit.

Step 2: Analysis of Each Circuit Configuration
1. In a purely resistive ac circuit, Ohm's law \(v(t) = i(t) R\) holds at every instant, so the current and voltage pass through zero and peak values together. The phase angle is \(\phi = 0\). This pairs with the condition where current and voltage are in phase.
2. In a purely inductive ac circuit, Faraday's back emf requires \(v(t) = L \frac{\mathrm{d}i}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Integrating gives \(i(t) = i_m \sin\left(\omega t - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), meaning current lags behind voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). This pairs with current lagging voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).
3. In a purely capacitive ac circuit, the charge relation \(q(t) = C v(t)\) yields current \(i(t) = \frac{\mathrm{d}q}{\mathrm{d}t} = i_m \sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\), meaning current leads voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). This pairs with current leading voltage by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\).
4. In a series LCR circuit at electrical resonance, the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel each other (\(X_L = X_C\)), making the circuit purely resistive with minimum impedance \(Z = R\). Current and voltage are in phase (\(\phi = 0\)) and the current achieves its maximum amplitude. This pairs with current and voltage in phase with maximum current.

Final Conclusion
The correct pairs correspond to matching the purely resistive circuit to in phase (\(\phi=0\)), the purely inductive circuit to current lagging by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), the purely capacitive circuit to current leading by \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), and series resonance to in phase with maximum current: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_AC_MATCH_Q02 - Transformer energy loss mechanisms and remedies

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Energy Loss Mechanism in Transformer) List II (Primary Minimization Technique)
A. Flux leakage between windings I. Using magnetic core material with a narrow hysteresis loop
B. Resistance heating in coil windings II. Winding primary and secondary coils directly one over the other
C. Magnetic hysteresis loss in core III. Using a laminated iron core separated by insulating varnish
D. Eddy current circulation in iron core IV. Using thick copper wire with large cross-sectional area

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Transformers experience four principal physical sources of energy loss: imperfect magnetic flux linkage, ohmic resistance of wire windings, cyclic ferromagnetic domain reorientation, and induced bulk circulating currents.

Step 2: Analysis of Each Loss Mechanism and its Remedy
1. Flux leakage arises when magnetic field lines generated by the primary do not completely pass through the secondary turns. This loss is minimized by winding the primary and secondary coils concentrically directly one on top of the other on the same limb of the soft-iron core.
2. Resistance of the windings causes Joule heating loss (\(I^2 R\)). This loss is minimized by lowering winding resistance, which is accomplished by using thick copper wire having a large cross-sectional area in high-current coils.
3. Hysteresis loss represents energy dissipated per cycle during the continuous magnetization reversal of ferromagnetic core domains. This expenditure is minimized by selecting a soft ferromagnetic material, such as silicon steel or soft iron, having a narrow magnetic hysteresis loop area.
4. Eddy currents are closed circulating loops induced within the conducting iron core by the alternating flux. This heating is minimized by building the core from thin laminated sheets coated with insulating varnish to interrupt conducting paths.

Final Conclusion
Matching each loss mechanism with its appropriate design remedy yields: flux leakage paired with winding coils one over the other, winding resistance paired with thick copper wire, hysteresis loss paired with narrow hysteresis loop material, and eddy current loss paired with laminated core construction: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_AC_MATCH_Q03 - Ac circuit parameters and their mathematical expressions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Physical Quantity / Characteristic) List II (Standard Mathematical Formula)
A. Resonant angular frequency of series LCR circuit I. \(\frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}}\)
B. Quality factor (\(Q\)) of series LCR circuit II. \(\sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2}\)
C. Impedance (\(Z\)) of series LCR circuit III. \(\frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}\)
D. Power factor (\(\cos\phi\)) of series LCR circuit IV. \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A series LCR circuit is governed by its inductive reactance \(X_L = \omega L\), capacitive reactance \(X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C}\), and resistance \(R\).

Step 2: Derivation and Evaluation of Formulae
1. Electrical resonance occurs when \(X_L = X_C\), which gives \(\omega_0 L = \frac{1}{\omega_0 C}\) or \(\omega_0^2 = \frac{1}{LC}\). Hence, the resonant angular frequency is \(\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\).
2. The quality factor of the resonant circuit represents the ratio of inductive reactance to resistance at resonance, \(Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}\). Substituting \(\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\) gives \(Q = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\frac{L}{R} = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}\).
3. From the impedance triangle, total circuit impedance is the hypotenuse combining resistance and net reactance: \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2}\).
4. The power factor is defined as the cosine of the phase angle between voltage and current: \(\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z} = \frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}}\).

Final Conclusion
Matching each quantity to its formula gives resonant frequency to \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\), quality factor to \(\frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}\), impedance to \(\sqrt{R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2}\), and power factor to \(\frac{R}{Z}\): A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_AC_MATCH_Q04 - Physical dimensions and SI units of ac circuit quantities

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Physical Quantity) List II (Dimensional Formula / Character)
A. Root-mean-square voltage (\(V_{\text{rms}}\)) I. Dimensionless with value between 0 and 1
B. Inductive reactance (\(X_L\)) II. \([\text{T}^{-1}]\)
C. Resonant angular frequency (\(\omega_0\)) III. \([\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-1}]\)
D. Power factor (\(\cos\phi\)) IV. \([\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-2}]\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Dimensional analysis of alternating current parameters is established from base electromagnetic definitions in SI base units: mass \([\text{M}]\), length \([\text{L}]\), time \([\text{T}]\), and electric current \([\text{A}]\).

Step 2: Dimensional Derivations for Each Quantity
1. Electric potential (rms voltage) is work done per unit charge: \(V = \frac{W}{q} = \frac{[\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-2}]}{[\text{A}\,\text{T}]} = [\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-1}]\).
2. Inductive reactance has the dimension of resistance: \(R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{[\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-1}]}{[\text{A}]} = [\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-2}]\).
3. Resonant angular frequency is defined as \(\omega_0 = \frac{2\pi}{T}\). Its dimension is reciprocal time: \([\text{T}^{-1}]\).
4. Power factor is \(\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}\), which is a pure trigonometric ratio of two quantities with identical dimensions of resistance (ohms), making it completely dimensionless with values constrained in \([0, 1]\).

Final Conclusion
Matching each physical quantity to its dimensional nature gives rms voltage to \([\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-1}]\), inductive reactance to \([\text{M}\,\text{L}^2\,\text{T}^{-3}\,\text{A}^{-2}]\), resonant angular frequency to \([\text{T}^{-1}]\), and power factor to dimensionless: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q01 - Peak voltage calculation from domestic rms voltage

questiontext.text: A household alternating voltage supply has a root-mean-square value of \(220\text{ V}\). What is the peak value of this alternating voltage?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The voltage varies sinusoidally with time according to \(v = v_m \sin \omega t\), where \(v_m\) represents the peak voltage.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The root-mean-square voltage and peak voltage for a sinusoidal wave are related by \(V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}}\), which gives \(v_m = \sqrt{2} V\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given root-mean-square voltage into the relation:
\[ v_m = \sqrt{2} \times 220\text{ V} \approx 1.4142 \times 220\text{ V} = 311.12\text{ V} \approx 311\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Because the peak value represents the maximum amplitude of oscillation, it must exceed the effective root-mean-square value by a factor of \(\sqrt{2}\). The calculated peak voltage is \(311\text{ V}\).

Final Answer: \(311\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q02 - Root mean square voltage from peak supply

questiontext.text: The peak voltage of an alternating current supply is \(300\text{ V}\). What is the root-mean-square voltage of this supply?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Peak voltage \(v_m = 300\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The ac supply produces a symmetric sinusoidal waveform.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The root-mean-square voltage is defined as \(V = \frac{v_m}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 v_m\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the root-mean-square voltage:
\[ V = \frac{300\text{ V}}{\sqrt{2}} \approx \frac{300}{1.4142}\text{ V} \approx 212.13\text{ V} \approx 212\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The effective value is roughly \(70.7\%\) of the peak amplitude. Dividing \(300\) by \(1.4142\) yields \(212\text{ V}\).

Final Answer: \(212\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q03 - Peak current from root mean square value

questiontext.text: The root-mean-square value of current in an alternating circuit is \(10\text{ A}\). What is the peak current flowing in this circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Root-mean-square current \(I = 10\text{ A}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The current varies sinusoidally as \(i = i_m \sin \omega t\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The relation connecting peak current and root-mean-square current is \(i_m = \sqrt{2} I\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Multiply the root-mean-square value by \(\sqrt{2}\):
\[ i_m = \sqrt{2} \times 10\text{ A} \approx 1.4142 \times 10\text{ A} = 14.14\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The peak current exceeds the root-mean-square current by a factor of \(1.4142\). The result is \(14.14\text{ A}\).

Final Answer: \(14.14\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q04 - Resistance of rated incandescent electric light bulb

questiontext.text: An electric bulb is rated at \(100\text{ W}\) for a \(220\text{ V}\) ac supply. What is the resistance of the bulb filament at its operating temperature?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Power rating \(P = 100\text{ W}\), rated root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The bulb filament acts as a purely resistive load obeying Ohm's law.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Power dissipated in a resistor under root-mean-square voltage \(V\) is \(P = \frac{V^2}{R}\), which gives \(R = \frac{V^2}{P}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute the resistance by substituting the given values:
\[ R = \frac{(220\text{ V})^2}{100\text{ W}} = \frac{48400}{100}\ \Omega = 484\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking power: \(P = \frac{(220)^2}{484} = 100\text{ W}\), confirming the resistance is \(484\ \Omega\).

Final Answer: \(484\ \Omega\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q05 - Root mean square current in purely resistive

questiontext.text: A \(100\ \Omega\) resistor is connected across a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) ac supply. What is the root-mean-square current in the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance \(R = 100\ \Omega\), supply root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\), frequency \(\nu = 50\text{ Hz}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The circuit consists exclusively of an ideal ohmic resistor with negligible inductance and capacitance.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Ohm's law for alternating current across a pure resistor states \(I = \frac{V}{R}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the root-mean-square voltage and resistance:
\[ I = \frac{220\text{ V}}{100\ \Omega} = 2.2\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units and magnitude verify correctly: \(220 / 100 = 2.2\text{ A}\).

Final Answer: \(2.2\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q06 - Average power consumed by pure resistor circuit

questiontext.text: A \(100\ \Omega\) resistor is connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) alternating voltage source. What is the net power consumed over a complete cycle?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance \(R = 100\ \Omega\), root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In a purely resistive circuit, current and voltage are in phase, so the power factor is \(\cos\phi = 1\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Average power consumed is given by \(P = \frac{V^2}{R} = I^2 R = V I\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the power dissipation:
\[ P = \frac{V^2}{R} = \frac{(220\text{ V})^2}{100\ \Omega} = \frac{48400}{100}\text{ W} = 484\text{ W} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Alternatively, using root-mean-square current \(I = 2.2\text{ A}\): \(P = (2.2)^2 \times 100 = 4.84 \times 100 = 484\text{ W}\).

Final Answer: \(484\text{ W}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q07 - Amplitude of alternating voltage for domestic outlet

questiontext.text: The voltage across the terminals of an electrical wall outlet is specified as \(240\text{ V}\). What is the amplitude (peak value) of this voltage?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Specified wall outlet voltage \(V = 240\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard commercial specifications denote the root-mean-square value of voltage.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The amplitude of sinusoidal alternating voltage is \(v_m = \sqrt{2} V\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the peak amplitude:
\[ v_m = \sqrt{2} \times 240\text{ V} \approx 1.4142 \times 240\text{ V} = 339.4\text{ V} \approx 340\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Rounding to the nearest significant whole number gives \(340\text{ V}\).

Final Answer: \(340\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q08 - Inductive reactance calculation of pure inductor coil

questiontext.text: A pure inductor of self-inductance \(25.0\text{ mH}\) is connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) ac source. What is the inductive reactance of the inductor? (Take \(\pi = 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Inductance \(L = 25.0\text{ mH} = 25.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H}\), frequency \(\nu = 50\text{ Hz}\), root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The inductor possesses zero winding resistance.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Inductive reactance is defined as \(X_L = \omega L = 2 \pi \nu L\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical values:
\[ X_L = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50\text{ s}^{-1} \times 25.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H} = 314 \times 0.025\ \Omega = 7.85\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The unit of \(2\pi\nu L\) is \(\text{s}^{-1} \times \text{H} = \Omega\). The calculated reactance is \(7.85\ \Omega\).

Final Answer: \(7.85\ \Omega\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q09 - Root mean square current in pure inductor

questiontext.text: A pure inductor of self-inductance \(25.0\text{ mH}\) having an inductive reactance of \(7.85\ \Omega\) is connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) source. What is the root-mean-square current in the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Inductive reactance \(X_L = 7.85\ \Omega\), supply root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Ideal inductive circuit with zero internal resistance.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The root-mean-square current through a pure inductor is \(I = \frac{V}{X_L}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute the current:
\[ I = \frac{220\text{ V}}{7.85\ \Omega} \approx 28.025\text{ A} \approx 28\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Multiplying \(28\text{ A} \times 7.85\ \Omega \approx 219.8\text{ V}\), matching the supply voltage of \(220\text{ V}\).

Final Answer: \(28\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q10 - Current calculation for forty four millihenry inductor

questiontext.text: A \(44\text{ mH}\) inductor is connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) ac supply. Determine the root-mean-square value of the current in the circuit. (Take \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Inductance \(L = 44\text{ mH} = 44 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H}\), voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\), frequency \(\nu = 50\text{ Hz}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The inductor is ideal and resistance is negligible.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Inductive reactance is \(X_L = 2\pi\nu L\), and root-mean-square current is \(I = \frac{V}{X_L}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate inductive reactance:
\[ X_L = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 50 \times 44 \times 10^{-3} = \frac{44 \times 50 \times 44 \times 10^{-3}}{7} = \frac{96.8}{7} \approx 13.83\ \Omega \]
Calculate the current:
\[ I = \frac{220\text{ V}}{13.83\ \Omega} \approx 15.91\text{ A} \approx 15.9\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The inductive reactance of \(13.83\ \Omega\) limits the \(220\text{ V}\) supply to \(15.9\text{ A}\).

Final Answer: \(15.9\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q11 - Inductive reactance at sixty hertz frequency

questiontext.text: An inductor of self-inductance \(0.50\text{ H}\) is operated in an alternating circuit of frequency \(60\text{ Hz}\). What is its inductive reactance? (Take \(\pi = 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Inductance \(L = 0.50\text{ H}\), frequency \(\nu = 60\text{ Hz}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Resistance of the coil is taken to be zero.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Inductive reactance is \(X_L = 2 \pi \nu L\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Evaluate the expression:
\[ X_L = 2 \times 3.14 \times 60\text{ s}^{-1} \times 0.50\text{ H} = 3.14 \times 60\ \Omega = 188.4\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Dimensionally, angular frequency multiplied by inductance gives resistance in ohms (\(188.4\ \Omega\)).

Final Answer: \(188.4\ \Omega\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q12 - Inductance required to limit alternating current

questiontext.text: An alternating voltage source of \(100\text{ V}\) and frequency \(50\text{ Hz}\) is applied across a pure inductor. If the desired root-mean-square current in the circuit is \(2.0\text{ A}\), what must be the self-inductance of the coil? (Take \(\pi = 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Supply voltage \(V = 100\text{ V}\), frequency \(\nu = 50\text{ Hz}\), desired current \(I = 2.0\text{ A}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Pure inductive circuit with no resistive or capacitive effects.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Required inductive reactance is \(X_L = \frac{V}{I}\). Since \(X_L = 2 \pi \nu L\), inductance is \(L = \frac{V}{2 \pi \nu I}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the required reactance:
\[ X_L = \frac{100\text{ V}}{2.0\text{ A}} = 50\ \Omega \]
Calculate inductance \(L\):
\[ L = \frac{50\ \Omega}{2 \times 3.14 \times 50\text{ s}^{-1}} = \frac{50}{314}\text{ H} \approx 0.1592\text{ H} \approx 0.159\text{ H} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: \(X_L = 2 \times 3.14 \times 50 \times 0.1592 \approx 50\ \Omega\), giving \(I = 100/50 = 2\text{ A}\). The inductance is \(0.159\text{ H}\) (\(159\text{ mH}\)).

Final Answer: \(0.159\text{ H}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q13 - Capacitive reactance of fifteen microfarad capacitor

questiontext.text: A \(15.0\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor is connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) source. What is the capacitive reactance of the capacitor? (Take \(\pi = 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Capacitance \(C = 15.0\ \mu\text{F} = 15.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}\), frequency \(\nu = 50\text{ Hz}\), supply voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Ideal capacitor with negligible equivalent series resistance.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Capacitive reactance is \(X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{2 \pi \nu C}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values into the formula:
\[ X_C = \frac{1}{2 \times 3.14 \times 50\text{ s}^{-1} \times 15.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}} = \frac{1}{314 \times 15.0 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{1}{4.71 \times 10^{-3}}\ \Omega \approx 212.3\ \Omega \approx 212\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units of \(\frac{1}{\text{s}^{-1} \times \text{F}} = \Omega\). Rounded to three significant digits, the reactance is \(212\ \Omega\).

Final Answer: \(212\ \Omega\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q14 - Root mean square current in purely capacitive

questiontext.text: A \(15.0\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor having a capacitive reactance of \(212\ \Omega\) is connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) source. What is the root-mean-square current in the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Capacitive reactance \(X_C = 212\ \Omega\), supply root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Capacitor is purely reactive with zero dielectric leakage.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Ohm's law relation for a capacitive circuit is \(I = \frac{V}{X_C}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the current:
\[ I = \frac{220\text{ V}}{212\ \Omega} \approx 1.0377\text{ A} \approx 1.04\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: \(1.0377\text{ A} \times 212\ \Omega \approx 220\text{ V}\). The root-mean-square current is \(1.04\text{ A}\).

Final Answer: \(1.04\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q15 - Peak current through fifteen microfarad capacitor

questiontext.text: A \(15.0\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor carries a root-mean-square alternating current of \(1.04\text{ A}\) when connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) supply. What is the peak current in the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Root-mean-square current \(I = 1.04\text{ A}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The current alternates sinusoidally with time.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The peak current amplitude is related to the root-mean-square current by \(i_m = \sqrt{2} I\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the peak value:
\[ i_m = \sqrt{2} \times 1.04\text{ A} \approx 1.4142 \times 1.04\text{ A} = 1.4708\text{ A} \approx 1.47\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The peak amplitude oscillates between \(+1.47\text{ A}\) and \(-1.47\text{ A}\).

Final Answer: \(1.47\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q16 - Current through sixty microfarad capacitor at sixty hertz

questiontext.text: A \(60\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor is connected to a \(110\text{ V}\), \(60\text{ Hz}\) ac supply. Determine the root-mean-square current flowing in the circuit. (Take \(\pi = 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Capacitance \(C = 60\ \mu\text{F} = 60 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}\), voltage \(V = 110\text{ V}\), frequency \(\nu = 60\text{ Hz}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The capacitor is ideal with zero resistance.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Capacitive reactance is \(X_C = \frac{1}{2 \pi \nu C}\), and current is \(I = \frac{V}{X_C} = 2 \pi \nu C V\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate capacitive reactance:
\[ X_C = \frac{1}{2 \times 3.14 \times 60 \times 60 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{1}{0.022608}\ \Omega \approx 44.23\ \Omega \]
Calculate root-mean-square current:
\[ I = \frac{110\text{ V}}{44.23\ \Omega} \approx 2.487\text{ A} \approx 2.49\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Direct multiplication \(I = 2 \times 3.1416 \times 60 \times 60 \times 10^{-6} \times 110 = 2.488\text{ A} \approx 2.49\text{ A}\).

Final Answer: \(2.49\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q17 - Capacitance required for specified capacitive reactance

questiontext.text: What capacitance is required to provide a capacitive reactance of \(100\ \Omega\) in a \(50\text{ Hz}\) alternating circuit? (Take \(\pi = 3.14\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Desired reactance \(X_C = 100\ \Omega\), operating frequency \(\nu = 50\text{ Hz}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Ideal capacitance without parasitic resistance.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From \(X_C = \frac{1}{2 \pi \nu C}\), the capacitance is given by \(C = \frac{1}{2 \pi \nu X_C}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[ C = \frac{1}{2 \times 3.14 \times 50\text{ s}^{-1} \times 100\ \Omega} = \frac{1}{31400}\text{ F} \approx 3.1847 \times 10^{-5}\text{ F} = 31.8\ \mu\text{F} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Check: \(X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi \times 50 \times 31.85 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{10^6}{10006} \approx 100\ \Omega\).

Final Answer: \(31.8\ \mu\text{F}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q18 - Total impedance of series resistor capacitor circuit

questiontext.text: A resistor of \(200\ \Omega\) and a capacitor of capacitive reactance \(212.3\ \Omega\) are connected in series across an alternating supply. What is the total impedance of the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance \(R = 200\ \Omega\), capacitive reactance \(X_C = 212.3\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The series RC combination has voltage phasor across \(R\) in phase with current, and across \(C\) lagging by \(90^\circ\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The impedance of a series RC circuit is \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Evaluate the square root:
\[ Z = \sqrt{(200\ \Omega)^2 + (212.3\ \Omega)^2} = \sqrt{40000 + 45071.29} = \sqrt{85071.29}\ \Omega \approx 291.67\ \Omega \approx 291.7\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Impedance is bounded: \(212.3 < Z < 200 + 212.3\). The value \(291.7\ \Omega\) is correct.

Final Answer: \(291.7\ \Omega\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q19 - Current calculation in series resistor capacitor circuit

questiontext.text: A series RC circuit with total impedance \(Z = 291.5\ \Omega\) is connected to a \(220\text{ V}\), \(50\text{ Hz}\) source. What is the root-mean-square current flowing in the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Impedance \(Z = 291.5\ \Omega\), supply root-mean-square voltage \(V = 220\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Series circuit with uniform instantaneous current through both components.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Root-mean-square current is given by \(I = \frac{V}{Z}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate current:
\[ I = \frac{220\text{ V}}{291.5\ \Omega} \approx 0.7547\text{ A} \approx 0.755\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Multiplying \(0.7547\text{ A} \times 291.5\ \Omega = 220.0\text{ V}\), which matches the source voltage.

Final Answer: \(0.755\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q20 - Component voltages across resistor and capacitor

questiontext.text: A current of \(0.755\text{ A}\) flows through a series RC circuit having \(R = 200\ \Omega\) and \(X_C = 212.3\ \Omega\). What are the root-mean-square voltages \(V_R\) across the resistor and \(V_C\) across the capacitor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Current \(I = 0.755\text{ A}\), resistance \(R = 200\ \Omega\), capacitive reactance \(X_C = 212.3\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Current is identical in both series elements; voltages are \(90^\circ\) out of phase.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Ohmic potential drops are \(V_R = I R\) and \(V_C = I X_C\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate voltage across resistor:
\[ V_R = 0.755\text{ A} \times 200\ \Omega = 151.0\text{ V} \]
Calculate voltage across capacitor:
\[ V_C = 0.755\text{ A} \times 212.3\ \Omega \approx 160.29\text{ V} \approx 160.3\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Vector sum: \(\sqrt{151^2 + 160.3^2} = \sqrt{22801 + 25696.09} = \sqrt{48497.09} \approx 220.2\text{ V}\), in agreement with source voltage.

Final Answer: \(V_R = 151\text{ V}\) and \(V_C = 160.3\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q21 - Impedance and current in series inductor resistor

questiontext.text: A series RL circuit contains a resistance of \(30\ \Omega\) and an inductive reactance of \(40\ \Omega\) connected to a \(100\text{ V}\) ac source. What are the impedance and the root-mean-square current in the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance \(R = 30\ \Omega\), inductive reactance \(X_L = 40\ \Omega\), supply voltage \(V = 100\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Capacitance is absent from the circuit.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Circuit impedance is \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}\), and root-mean-square current is \(I = \frac{V}{Z}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate impedance:
\[ Z = \sqrt{30^2 + 40^2}\ \Omega = \sqrt{900 + 1600}\ \Omega = \sqrt{2500}\ \Omega = 50\ \Omega \]
Calculate root-mean-square current:
\[ I = \frac{100\text{ V}}{50\ \Omega} = 2.0\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Pythagorean triple (30-40-50) yields \(Z = 50\ \Omega\) and \(I = 2.0\text{ A}\).

Final Answer: \(Z = 50\ \Omega\) and \(I = 2.0\text{ A}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q22 - Phase angle calculation in series inductor resistor

questiontext.text: A series RL circuit has a resistance of \(30\ \Omega\) and an inductive reactance of \(40\ \Omega\). What is the phase angle by which the applied voltage leads the current?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance \(R = 30\ \Omega\), inductive reactance \(X_L = 40\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In an RL circuit, voltage leads current by phase angle \(\phi > 0\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The tangent of the phase angle is given by \(\tan\phi = \frac{X_L}{R}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute \(\tan\phi\):
\[ \tan\phi = \frac{40\ \Omega}{30\ \Omega} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.333 \]
Take the inverse tangent:
\[ \phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \approx 53.13^\circ \approx 53.1^\circ \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Because \(X_L > R\), the phase angle must exceed \(45^\circ\). The angle is \(53.1^\circ\).

Final Answer: \(53.1^\circ\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q23 - Total impedance calculation of series LCR circuit

questiontext.text: A series LCR circuit contains a resistor \(R = 3\ \Omega\), an inductor with inductive reactance \(X_L = 8\ \Omega\), and a capacitor with capacitive reactance \(X_C = 4\ \Omega\). What is the total impedance of this circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(R = 3\ \Omega\), \(X_L = 8\ \Omega\), \(X_C = 4\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Series LCR circuit under sinusoidal steady-state excitation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Total impedance is \(Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate net reactance:
\[ X = X_L - X_C = 8\ \Omega - 4\ \Omega = 4\ \Omega \]
Calculate impedance:
\[ Z = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}\ \Omega = \sqrt{9 + 16}\ \Omega = \sqrt{25}\ \Omega = 5\ \Omega \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The net reactance of \(4\ \Omega\) with resistance \(3\ \Omega\) yields hypotenuse \(5\ \Omega\).

Final Answer: \(5\ \Omega\)

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CH07_MCQ_Q24 - Phase angle calculation in series LCR circuit

questiontext.text: In a series LCR circuit with \(R = 3\ \Omega\), \(X_L = 8\ \Omega\), and \(X_C = 4\ \Omega\), what is the phase difference \(\phi\) between the source voltage and current where \(i = i_m \sin(\omega t + \phi)\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance \(R = 3\ \Omega\), \(X_L = 8\ \Omega\), \(X_C = 4\ \Omega\).
