जे. जे. थॉमसन के प्रायोगिक अनुसंधानों ने यह सिद्ध किया कि कैथोड किरण कणों के लिए आवेश और द्रव्यमान का अनुपात \(e/m\) लगभग \(1.76 \times 10^{11}\text{ C/kg}\) पर स्थिर रहता है, चाहे कैथोड किसी भी धातु का बना हो अथवा नलिका में कोई भी गैस भरी गई हो। इसने सिद्ध किया कि ये कण (इलेक्ट्रॉन) पदार्थ के सार्वत्रिक घटक हैं।

चरण 2: प्रायोगिक वेग वरण विधि का विश्लेषण
थॉमसन ने विसर्जन नलिका में परस्पर लंबवत विद्युत और चुंबकीय क्षेत्रों का उपयोग करके स्थिरवैद्युत और चुंबकीय लोरेंत्ज़ बलों को संतुलित किया, जिससे कैथोड किरणों का वेग तथा विशिष्ट आवेश \(e/m\) सफलतापूर्वक मापा गया।

चरण 3: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
विशिष्ट आवेश की स्वतंत्रता से संबंधित पहला कथन भौतिक रूप से सत्य है। इसी प्रकार, परस्पर लंबवत क्षेत्रों की सहायता से मापन का दूसरा कथन भी भौतिक रूप से सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST2_Q02 - Minimum energy requirement for electron emission process

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The minimum energy required by an electron to escape from a metal surface is called the work function of that metal.

Statement II: The work function is identical for all metals and is completely independent of the nature of the surface.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन को धातु की सतह से बाहर निकलने के लिए आवश्यक न्यूनतम ऊर्जा को उस धातु का कार्यफलन कहा जाता है।

कथन II: कार्यफलन सभी धातुओं के लिए एक समान होता है और सतह की प्रकृति पर बिल्कुल निर्भर नहीं करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of Metal Work Function
Free electrons are bound within a metal surface by the attractive electrostatic pull of positive ionic cores. The threshold energy barrier that an electron must overcome to escape into the vacuum is defined as the work function, usually denoted by \(\phi_0\) and measured in electron-volts (\(\text{eV}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of Surface and Material Dependence
The work function depends strongly on the specific chemical element, atomic lattice structure, impurities, and the surface condition of the material. For example, alkali metals like caesium have a low work function (\(2.14\text{ eV}\)), whereas platinum has a much higher work function (\(5.65\text{ eV}\)). Thus, the claim of identical work functions across all metals is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Propositions
The first definition is factually correct, whereas the second claim stating that work function is invariant across all metals is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: धातु कार्यफलन की परिभाषा
मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन धातु की सतह के भीतर धनायनों के स्थिरवैद्युत आकर्षण बल से बंधे रहते हैं। इलेक्ट्रॉन को सतह से बाहर निकलने हेतु आवश्यक न्यूनतम ऊर्जा को कार्यफलन (\(\phi_0\)) कहा जाता है, जिसे प्रायः इलेक्ट्रॉन वोल्ट (\(\text{eV}\)) में मापा जाता है।

चरण 2: सतह एवं पदार्थ निर्भरता का मूल्यांकन
कार्यफलन का मान धातु के प्रकार, क्रिस्टल जालक तथा सतह की प्रकृति पर दृढ़ता से निर्भर करता है। उदाहरण के लिए, सीज़ियम का कार्यफलन \(2.14\text{ eV}\) है, जबकि प्लेटिनम का कार्यफलन \(5.65\text{ eV}\) होता है। अतः सभी धातुओं के लिए इसे समान बताना असत्य है।

चरण 3: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
पहला कथन पूर्णतः सही है, जबकि सभी धातुओं के लिए समान कार्यफलन बताने वाला दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I सही है लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST2_Q03 - Photoelectric current dependence on collector plate potential

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a photoelectric experiment, once the saturation current is attained, further increasing the accelerating potential on the collector plate causes the photocurrent to increase continuously.

Statement II: Saturation current corresponds to the operating condition where all the photoelectrons emitted per second by the photosensitive plate are collected by the collector plate.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: प्रकाश-विद्युत प्रयोग में, एक बार संतृप्त धारा प्राप्त हो जाने के बाद, संग्राहक प्लेट पर त्वरक विभव को और बढ़ाने से प्रकाश-विद्युत धारा निरंतर बढ़ती जाती है।

कथन II: संतृप्त धारा उस स्थिति से संबंधित होती है जब प्रकाश-संवेदी प्लेट द्वारा प्रति सेकंड उत्सर्जित सभी फोटोइलेक्ट्रॉन संग्राहक प्लेट द्वारा एकत्रित कर लिए जाते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Physical Meaning of Saturation Current
When monochromatic light of constant intensity and frequency illuminates the emitter cathode, a fixed number of electrons are ejected per second. As the accelerating positive potential on the collector anode is increased, it collects a progressively larger fraction of these emitted electrons.

Step 2: Behavior at High Accelerating Potentials
When the potential is sufficiently positive, all photoelectrons emitted per unit time reach the collector plate. Beyond this point, increasing the voltage further cannot draw any additional electrons because the emission rate is governed solely by the light intensity, not by the collector voltage. Consequently, the photocurrent remains flat and saturated, making the first claim incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Saturation Definition
The definition that saturation current corresponds to the collection of every emitted photoelectron per second is physically exact and correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: संतृप्त धारा का भौतिक अर्थ
जब निश्चित आवृत्ति और तीव्रता का प्रकाश उत्सर्जक पर आपतित होता है, तो प्रति सेकंड उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या नियत होती है। संग्राहक प्लेट का धनात्मक विभव बढ़ाने पर वह उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉनों के बड़े हिस्से को एकत्रित करता है।

चरण 2: उच्च त्वरक विभव पर व्यवहार
एक पर्याप्त धनात्मक विभव पर, प्रति सेकंड उत्सर्जित सभी इलेक्ट्रॉन संग्राहक प्लेट पर पहुँच जाते हैं। इसके बाद विभव को और बढ़ाने पर धारा में कोई वृद्धि नहीं होती क्योंकि उत्सर्जन दर केवल प्रकाश की तीव्रता पर निर्भर करती है। अतः पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 3: संतृप्त अवस्था की परिभाषा का मूल्यांकन
यह परिभाषा पूर्णतः सत्य है कि संतृप्त धारा वह अवस्था है जहाँ प्रति सेकंड उत्सर्जित सभी फोटोइलेक्ट्रॉनों को संग्राहक प्लेट द्वारा एकत्र कर लिया जाता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST2_Q04 - Stopping potential variation with radiation intensity frequency

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For incident light of a given frequency exceeding the threshold frequency, the stopping potential increases in direct proportion to the intensity of the incident radiation.

Statement II: The threshold frequency of a photosensitive metal decreases when the intensity of the incident beam is made extremely high.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: देहली आवृत्ति से अधिक किसी निश्चित आवृत्ति के आपतित प्रकाश के लिए, निरोधी विभव आपतित विकिरण की तीव्रता के सीधे अनुक्रमानुपाती होकर बढ़ता है।

कथन II: आपतित पुंज की तीव्रता अत्यंत उच्च कर देने पर प्रकाश-संवेदी धातु की देहली आवृत्ति कम हो जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Stopping Potential vs Intensity
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, \(e V_0 = K_{\max} = h\nu - \phi_0\). The stopping potential \(V_0\) depends solely on the photon frequency \(\nu\) and the metal work function \(\phi_0\). Experimental measurements confirm that changing the intensity at constant frequency changes only the saturation current, while \(V_0\) remains completely unchanged. Therefore, the first statement is false.

Step 2: Analysis of Threshold Frequency vs Intensity
The threshold frequency is defined by \(\nu_0 = \phi_0 / h\), which is an inherent, characteristic property of the metal determined strictly by the binding energy of the surface electrons. It does not depend on the intensity, brightness, or exposure time of the incident radiation. Therefore, the second statement is also false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Propositions
Both propositions describe incorrect dependencies that contradict fundamental photoelectric laws.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

चरण 1: निरोधी विभव बनाम तीव्रता का विश्लेषण
आइंस्टाइन के प्रकाश-विद्युत समीकरण \(e V_0 = h\nu - \phi_0\) के अनुसार, निरोधी विभव \(V_0\) केवल आवृत्ति \(\nu\) और कार्यफलन \(\phi_0\) पर निर्भर करता है। नियत आवृत्ति पर तीव्रता बदलने से केवल संतृप्त धारा बदलती है, निरोधी विभव नहीं। अतः पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 2: देहली आवृत्ति बनाम तीव्रता का विश्लेषण
देहली आवृत्ति \(\nu_0 = \phi_0 / h\) धातु का एक अंतर्निहित विशिष्ट गुण है जो केवल सतह के कार्यफलन पर निर्भर करती है। यह आपतित प्रकाश की तीव्रता अथवा दीप्ति पर बिल्कुल निर्भर नहीं करती। अतः दूसरा कथन भी असत्य है।

चरण 3: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
दोनों कथन भौतिक नियमों के विपरीत और असत्य हैं।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST2_Q05 - Photon momentum and energy in radiation interaction

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Every photon of electromagnetic radiation of frequency \(\nu\) and wavelength \(\lambda\) carries energy \(E = h\nu\) and momentum \(p = h/\lambda\), regardless of the beam intensity.

Statement II: Increasing the intensity of monochromatic light of a given wavelength increases the photon flux per unit area per second without altering the energy or momentum of individual photons.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: \(\nu\) आवृत्ति और \(\lambda\) तरंगदैर्घ्य वाले विद्युत चुंबकीय विकिरण का प्रत्येक फोटॉन, पुंज की तीव्रता पर ध्यान दिए बिना, \(E = h\nu\) ऊर्जा और \(p = h/\lambda\) संवेग वहन करता है।

कथन II: किसी दी गई तरंगदैर्घ्य के एकवर्णी प्रकाश की तीव्रता बढ़ाने से प्रति इकाई क्षेत्रफल प्रति सेकंड गुजरने वाले फोटॉनों का फ्लक्स बढ़ता है, जबकि व्यक्तिगत फोटॉनों की ऊर्जा या संवेग में कोई परिवर्तन नहीं होता।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Photon Energy and Momentum Relations
Einstein's photon hypothesis and relativistic mechanics establish that a light quantum with frequency \(\nu\) possesses energy \(E = h\nu = hc/\lambda\) and linear momentum \(p = E/c = h/\lambda\). These particle attributes depend strictly on the radiation frequency/wavelength.

Step 2: Interpretation of Beam Intensity
Intensity \(I\) of a monochromatic beam is given by \(I = n E = n h\nu\), where \(n\) is the number of photons crossing unit area perpendicular to the beam per second. Increasing the intensity multiplies the number of photons, but each photon retains the exact same quantum of energy and momentum.

Step 3: Evaluation of Propositions
The mathematical expressions for photon energy and momentum are accurate. The deduction that higher intensity increases photon flux rather than photon energy is also accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

चरण 1: फोटॉन ऊर्जा एवं संवेग संबंध
आइंस्टाइन के फोटॉन सिद्धांत तथा आपेक्षिकीय यांत्रिकी के अनुसार, \(\nu\) आवृत्ति वाले प्रकाश क्वांटम की ऊर्जा \(E = h\nu = hc/\lambda\) तथा संवेग \(p = h/\lambda\) होता है। ये दोनों मान केवल आवृत्ति अथवा तरंगदैर्घ्य पर निर्भर करते हैं।

चरण 2: प्रकाश तीव्रता की व्याख्या
एकवर्णी पुंज की तीव्रता \(I = n h\nu\) होती है, जहाँ \(n\) प्रति सेकंड प्रति इकाई क्षेत्रफल से गुजरने वाले फोटॉनों की संख्या है। तीव्रता बढ़ाने से केवल फोटॉन फ्लक्स \(n\) बढ़ता है, व्यक्तिगत फोटॉन की ऊर्जा या संवेग अपरिवर्तित रहते हैं।

चरण 3: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
फोटॉन की ऊर्जा और संवेग से संबंधित पहला कथन सत्य है, तथा तीव्रता का फोटॉन फ्लक्स से संबंध बताने वाला दूसरा कथन भी सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I और कथन II दोनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST2_Q06 - De Broglie wavelength independence from electric charge

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = h/p\) associated with a moving material particle depends only on Planck's constant and the momentum of the particle, and is independent of whether the particle carries an electric charge.

Statement II: If a proton and a neutron move with identical velocities, the proton will have a significantly larger de Broglie wavelength because it carries a positive electric charge.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी गतिमान पदार्थ कण से संबद्ध दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य \(\lambda = h/p\) केवल प्लांक नियतांक तथा कण के संवेग पर निर्भर करती है, और इस बात से स्वतंत्र होती है कि कण पर कोई विद्युत आवेश है या नहीं।

कथन II: यदि एक प्रोटॉन और एक न्यूट्रॉन समान वेग से गति करते हैं, तो प्रोटॉन की दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य काफी बड़ी होगी क्योंकि वह धनात्मक विद्युत आवेश वहन करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of the de Broglie Relation
De Broglie's hypothesis posits that any moving material body exhibits wave behavior with wavelength \(\lambda = h/p = h/(mv)\). The formula contains only Planck's constant \(h\), inertial mass \(m\), and velocity \(v\). It contains no charge parameter \(q\), meaning the matter wave relation holds identically for charged particles (electrons, protons) and uncharged particles (neutrons, atoms). Thus, the first statement is correct.

Step 2: Comparison of Proton and Neutron
A proton (mass \(m_p \approx 1.6726 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\)) and a neutron (mass \(m_n \approx 1.6749 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\)) have nearly identical masses. If both travel at the exact same velocity \(v\), their momenta \(p = mv\) are virtually identical, yielding essentially equal de Broglie wavelengths (with the slightly heavier neutron having an infinitesimally smaller wavelength). The presence of electric charge on the proton confers no additional wavelength. Thus, the second statement is false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Propositions
The general statement regarding charge independence is valid, whereas the claim that charge increases the proton's matter wavelength is invalid.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: दे ब्रॉग्ली संबंध का विश्लेषण
दे ब्रॉग्ली संबंध \(\lambda = h/p = h/(mv)\) में केवल प्लांक नियतांक, द्रव्यमान तथा वेग आते हैं। इसमें आवेश \(q\) का कोई पद नहीं होता, अतः द्रव्य तरंगें आवेशित एवं अनावेशित दोनों प्रकार के कणों पर समान रूप से लागू होती हैं। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन की तुलना
प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन के द्रव्यमान लगभग समान होते हैं। यदि दोनों समान वेग \(v\) से गति कर रहे हैं, तो उनके संवेग \(p = mv\) लगभग समान होंगे और उनकी दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य भी लगभग बराबर होगी। प्रोटॉन का धन आवेश उसकी तरंगदैर्घ्य को नहीं बढ़ाता। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
पहला कथन सत्य है जबकि दूसरा कथन असत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I सही है लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST2_Q07 - Continuous X ray spectrum cutoff wavelength dependence

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In an X-ray tube operated at accelerating voltage \(V\), the minimum (cutoff) wavelength \(\lambda_{\min}\) of the continuous X-ray spectrum increases linearly with the accelerating voltage.

Statement II: The maximum kinetic energy of electrons striking the target anode in an X-ray tube depends on the atomic number of the target material rather than the accelerating voltage.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: \(V\) त्वरित वोल्टता पर संचालित एक एक्स-किरण नलिका में, सतत एक्स-किरण स्पेक्ट्रम की न्यूनतम (अंतक) तरंगदैर्घ्य \(\lambda_{\min}\) त्वरित वोल्टता के साथ रैखिक रूप से बढ़ती है।

कथन II: एक्स-किरण नलिका में लक्ष्य एनोड से टकराने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा त्वरित वोल्टता के बजाय लक्ष्य पदार्थ की परमाणु संख्या पर निर्भर करती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Duane-Hunt Law for Minimum Wavelength
In an X-ray tube, energetic electrons accelerated through potential difference \(V\) possess kinetic energy \(K = e V\). The maximum photon energy emitted when an electron loses all its energy in a single collision is \(h\nu_{\max} = \frac{hc}{\lambda_{\min}} = e V\). Rearranging gives \(\lambda_{\min} = \frac{hc}{eV}\). This demonstrates that \(\lambda_{\min}\) is inversely proportional to \(V\), not directly proportional. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Dependence of Electron Kinetic Energy
The kinetic energy acquired by an electron of charge \(e\) falling across accelerating potential \(V\) from cathode to anode is \(K = e V\). This depends strictly on the accelerating voltage \(V\) established between the electrodes. It is completely independent of the atomic number \(Z\) or composition of the target material. Therefore, the second statement is also incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Propositions
Both statements make erroneous physical claims about X-ray generation mechanics.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

चरण 1: न्यूनतम तरंगदैर्घ्य हेतु ड्वेन-हंट नियम
\(V\) विभवांतर से त्वरित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा \(K = e V\) होती है। सतत एक्स-किरणों की अधिकतम ऊर्जा \(h\nu_{\max} = \frac{hc}{\lambda_{\min}} = e V\) होती है, जिससे \(\lambda_{\min} = \frac{hc}{eV}\) प्राप्त होता है। स्पष्ट है कि \(\lambda_{\min}\) वोल्टता \(V\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है, अनुक्रमानुपाती नहीं। अतः पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 2: इलेक्ट्रॉन की गतिज ऊर्जा की निर्भरता
एनोड से टकराने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉन की गतिज ऊर्जा \(K = e V\) केवल इलेक्ट्रोडों के बीच प्रयुक्त त्वरित वोल्टता \(V\) पर निर्भर करती है। यह लक्ष्य पदार्थ के परमाणु क्रमांक \(Z\) पर बिल्कुल निर्भर नहीं करती। अतः दूसरा कथन भी असत्य है।

चरण 3: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
दोनों कथन भौतिक रूप से त्रुटिपूर्ण और असत्य हैं।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I और कथन II दोनों गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST2_Q08 - De Broglie phase velocity and group velocity

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The phase velocity \(v_p\) of a de Broglie matter wave associated with a moving particle carries direct physical significance and is always equal to the particle speed.

Statement II: The group velocity of a matter wave packet has direct physical meaning and equals the actual physical velocity of the moving particle.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी गतिमान कण से संबद्ध दे ब्रॉग्ली द्रव्य तरंग का कला वेग \(v_p\) प्रत्यक्ष भौतिक महत्व रखता है और हमेशा कण की चाल के बराबर होता है।

कथन II: द्रव्य तरंग पैकेट का समूह वेग प्रत्यक्ष भौतिक अर्थ रखता है और गतिमान कण के वास्तविक भौतिक वेग के बराबर होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनें:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examination of Phase Velocity of Matter Waves
For a relativistic free particle of rest mass \(m\) moving with velocity \(v\), its energy is \(E = \hbar\omega = \gamma mc^2\) and momentum is \(p = \hbar k = \gamma mv\). The phase velocity of the matter wave is \(v_p = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{E}{p} = \frac{c^2}{v}\). Since a material particle always travels slower than light (\(v < c\)), the phase velocity satisfies \(v_p > c\). A phase velocity exceeding the speed of light cannot transport information or matter and possesses no direct physical significance. Thus, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Examination of Group Velocity of Matter Waves
A localized material particle is physically represented by a wave packet composed of a group of frequencies. The group velocity is given by \(v_g = \frac{d\omega}{dk} = \frac{dE}{dp}\). Differentiating relativistic energy \(E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4\) yields \(2E \, dE = 2p c^2 \, dp\), which gives \(\frac{dE}{dp} = \frac{p c^2}{E} = \frac{(\gamma m v) c^2}{\gamma m c^2} = v\). Hence, the group velocity of the wave packet precisely equals the physical velocity of the particle and carries full physical significance. Thus, the second statement is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Propositions
The first proposition incorrectly attributes physical significance and particle speed to phase velocity, whereas the second proposition correctly identifies group velocity with particle speed.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: द्रव्य तरंगों के कला वेग का परीक्षण
\(v\) वेग से गतिमान कण के लिए ऊर्जा \(E = \gamma mc^2\) तथा संवेग \(p = \gamma mv\) होता है। कला वेग \(v_p = \frac{E}{p} = \frac{c^2}{v}\) प्राप्त होता है। चूंकि कण की चाल प्रकाश की चाल से कम होती है (\(v < c\)), अतः कला वेग प्रकाश की चाल से अधिक (\(v_p > c\)) होता है। यह कोई प्रत्यक्ष भौतिक महत्व नहीं रखता और कण की चाल के बराबर नहीं होता। अतः पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 2: द्रव्य तरंगों के समूह वेग का परीक्षण
एक स्थानिक कण को तरंग पैकेट द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है। समूह वेग \(v_g = \frac{dE}{dp}\) होता है। आपेक्षिकीय ऊर्जा संबंध \(E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m^2 c^4\) का अवकलन करने पर \(\frac{dE}{dp} = \frac{p c^2}{E} = v\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः समूह वेग वास्तविक भौतिक वेग के बराबर होता है और भौतिक सार्थकता रखता है। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
पहला कथन कला वेग के संबंध में असत्य है, जबकि समूह वेग से संबंधित दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST3_Q01 - Physical processes imparting energy for electron emission

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the dual nature of radiation and matter:

Statement I: Thermionic emission occurs when sufficient thermal energy is imparted to free electrons by heating to enable them to overcome the attractive pull of ions.

Statement II: Field emission can be achieved by applying a very strong electric field of the order of \(10^8\text{ V m}^{-1}\) to pull electrons out of the metal.

Statement III: In photoelectric emission, electron emission occurs at any arbitrary incident light frequency provided the electric field amplitude is non-zero.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

विकिरण तथा द्रव्य की द्वैत प्रकृति के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: तापीय उत्सर्जन तब होता है जब गर्म करके मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉनों को पर्याप्त ऊष्मीय ऊर्जा प्रदान की जाती है ताकि वे धनायनों के आकर्षण बल को पार कर सकें।

कथन II: क्षेत्रीय उत्सर्जन धातु पर लगभग \(10^8\text{ V m}^{-1}\) कोटि का अत्यंत प्रबल विद्युत क्षेत्र लगाकर इलेक्ट्रॉनों को बाहर खींचकर प्राप्त किया जा सकता है।

कथन III: प्रकाश-विद्युत उत्सर्जन में, आपतित प्रकाश की किसी भी स्वेच्छ आवृत्ति पर इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्सर्जन होता है, बशर्ते विद्युत क्षेत्र का आयाम अशून्य हो।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Thermionic Emission Process
By suitably heating a metal, thermal energy is imparted to the free conduction electrons. When this thermal kinetic energy exceeds the work function \(\phi_0\), electrons escape from the metal surface. Hence, the description of thermionic emission is physically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Field Emission Process
By applying an exceptionally strong electric field of the order of \(10^8\text{ V m}^{-1}\) (as found in sharp tips or spark plugs), the surface potential barrier is sufficiently narrowed and lowered to pull electrons out directly. Hence, the description of field emission is physically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Photoelectric Emission Requirement
Photoelectric emission does not occur at arbitrary frequencies. There exists a strict characteristic threshold frequency \(\nu_0 = \phi_0/h\) below which no photoelectrons are ejected, regardless of the electric field amplitude, intensity, or exposure time. Hence, the claim of emission at any arbitrary frequency is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements I and II only are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.

चरण 1: तापीय उत्सर्जन प्रक्रिया का मूल्यांकन
धातु को उपयुक्त रूप से गर्म करने पर मुक्त चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों को ऊष्मीय ऊर्जा मिलती है। जब यह ऊर्जा कार्यफलन \(\phi_0\) से अधिक हो जाती है, तो इलेक्ट्रॉन धातु की सतह से बाहर निकल जाते हैं। अतः तापीय उत्सर्जन का विवरण भौतिक रूप से सत्य है।

चरण 2: क्षेत्रीय उत्सर्जन प्रक्रिया का मूल्यांकन
लगभग \(10^8\text{ V m}^{-1}\) की कोटि का अत्यधिक प्रबल विद्युत क्षेत्र लगाने पर विभव प्राचीर संकीर्ण हो जाती है और इलेक्ट्रॉन धातु से बाहर खिंच आते हैं। अतः क्षेत्रीय उत्सर्जन का विवरण भौतिक रूप से सत्य है।

चरण 3: प्रकाश-विद्युत उत्सर्जन की आवश्यकता का मूल्यांकन
प्रकाश-विद्युत उत्सर्जन किसी भी स्वेच्छ आवृत्ति पर नहीं होता। प्रत्येक धातु के लिए एक विशिष्ट देहली आवृत्ति \(\nu_0 = \phi_0/h\) होती है, जिससे कम आवृत्ति पर कोई उत्सर्जन संभव नहीं है, चाहे विद्युत क्षेत्र का आयाम कितना भी अधिक क्यों न हो। अतः तीसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I and II only are correct.
Statements II and III only are correct.
Statements I, II and III are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST3_Q02 - Experimental characteristics of photoelectric emission phenomenon

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the dual nature of radiation and matter:

Statement I: Photoelectric emission starts instantaneously without any measurable time lag (within \(10^{-9}\text{ s}\) or less), even when the incident light is exceedingly dim.

Statement II: At a constant frequency above the threshold frequency, doubling the intensity of the incident radiation doubles the stopping potential.

Statement III: For different photosensitive metals, plots of stopping potential versus incident radiation frequency yield parallel straight lines having identical slopes equal to \(h/e\).

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

विकिरण तथा द्रव्य की द्वैत प्रकृति के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: प्रकाश-विद्युत उत्सर्जन बिना किसी मापने योग्य समयांतराल (\(10^{-9}\text{ s}\) या उससे कम समय) के तात्कालिक रूप से प्रारंभ होता है, भले ही आपतित प्रकाश अत्यधिक मंद क्यों न हो।

कथन II: देहली आवृत्ति से अधिक नियत आवृत्ति पर, आपतित विकिरण की तीव्रता दोगुनी करने पर निरोधी विभव दोगुना हो जाता है।

कथन III: विभिन्न प्रकाश-संवेदी धातुओं के लिए, निरोधी विभव बनाम आपतित विकिरण की आवृत्ति के ग्राफ \(h/e\) के बराबर समान ढलान वाली समानांतर सरल रेखाएं होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Emission Time Lag
Experimental observations establish that photoelectric emission begins within \(10^{-9}\text{ s}\) or less upon illumination, because the process involves an instantaneous one-to-one collision between a photon and an electron. Hence, the description of instantaneous emission is physically accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Stopping Potential Independence
Einstein's photoelectric equation gives \(e V_0 = h\nu - \phi_0\), showing that the stopping potential \(V_0\) depends solely on the incident frequency \(\nu\) and work function \(\phi_0\). Doubling the intensity doubles the number of photons and hence the saturation current, but leaves the stopping potential entirely unchanged. Hence, the claim that stopping potential doubles with intensity is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Linear Slope Universality
The relation \(V_0 = \left(\frac{h}{e}\right)\nu - \frac{\phi_0}{e}\) represents a straight line whose slope is \(h/e\). Because Planck's constant \(h\) and elementary charge \(e\) are universal physical constants, the slope is identical for all emitter metals, producing parallel straight lines. Hence, the statement regarding parallel lines and universal slope is physically accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements I and III only are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: उत्सर्जन समयांतराल का मूल्यांकन
प्रायोगिक प्रेक्षण यह स्थापित करते हैं कि प्रकाश-विद्युत उत्सर्जन \(10^{-9}\text{ s}\) या उससे कम समय में प्रारंभ हो जाता है, क्योंकि यह फोटॉन और इलेक्ट्रॉन के बीच तात्कालिक संघट्ट है। अतः तात्कालिक उत्सर्जन का कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: निरोधी विभव की स्वतंत्रता का मूल्यांकन
आइंस्टाइन के समीकरण \(e V_0 = h\nu - \phi_0\) के अनुसार, निरोधी विभव \(V_0\) केवल आवृत्ति और कार्यफलन पर निर्भर करता है। तीव्रता दोगुनी करने पर संतृप्त धारा दोगुनी होती है, निरोधी विभव नहीं बदलता। अतः निरोधी विभव के दोगुने होने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: रैखिक ढलान की सार्वभौमिकता का मूल्यांकन
\(V_0 = \left(\frac{h}{e}\right)\nu - \frac{\phi_0}{e}\) एक सरल रेखा का समीकरण है जिसका ढलान \(h/e\) होता है। चूंकि \(h\) और \(e\) सार्वत्रिक नियतांक हैं, अतः सभी धातुओं के लिए रेखाओं के ढलान समान होते हैं और वे परस्पर समानांतर होती हैं। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन I और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I, II and III are all correct.
Statements I and III only are correct.
Statements II and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST3_Q03 - Photon particle model and energy distribution features

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the dual nature of radiation and matter:

Statement I: According to Einstein's photoelectric theory, all photoelectrons ejected from a metal surface emerge with identical kinetic energy equal to \(K_{\max}\Defaultgrade>.

Statement II: A photon of frequency \(\nu\) travels in vacuum with speed \(c\) and carries a linear momentum \(p = h\nu/c = h/\lambda\), despite having zero rest mass.

Statement III: Photons are electrically neutral entities and do not experience any deflection when propagating through external electric or magnetic fields.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

विकिरण तथा द्रव्य की द्वैत प्रकृति के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: आइंस्टाइन के प्रकाश-विद्युत सिद्धांत के अनुसार, धातु की सतह से उत्सर्जित सभी फोटोइलेक्ट्रॉन \(K_{\max}\) के बराबर समान गतिज ऊर्जा के साथ बाहर निकलते हैं।

कथन II: \(\nu\) आवृत्ति का एक फोटॉन निर्वात में \(c\) चाल से गति करता है और शून्य विराम द्रव्यमान होने के बावजूद \(p = h\nu/c = h/\lambda\) रैखिक संवेग वहन करता है।

कथन III: फोटॉन विद्युत रूप से उदासीन होते हैं और बाह्य विद्युत या चुंबकीय क्षेत्रों से गुजरने पर किसी भी प्रकार का विक्षेपण अनुभव नहीं करते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Kinetic Energy Distribution
Electrons in a metal have a distribution of binding energies. Only those electrons closest to the Fermi level that absorb a photon without suffering internal inelastic scattering emerge with the maximum kinetic energy \(K_{\max} = h\nu - \phi_0\). More tightly bound electrons or electrons that collide with ions lose energy and emerge with kinetic energies ranging from zero up to \(K_{\max}\). Hence, the assertion that all photoelectrons have energy \(K_{\max}\) is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of Photon Linear Momentum
In Einstein's photon picture and relativistic kinematics, electromagnetic radiation of wavelength \(\lambda\) is composed of quanta travelling at speed \(c\). Even though a photon has zero invariant rest mass (\(m_0 = 0\)), its relativistic momentum is strictly non-zero and given by \(p = E/c = h\nu/c = h/\lambda\). Hence, this statement is physically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Photon Neutrality in Fields
Photons carry zero electric charge. The Lorentz force \(\vec{F} = q(\vec{E} + \vec{v} \times \vec{B})\) exerted on a photon is identically zero for all field configurations, so photon beams propagate undeflected through electrostatic and magnetostatic fields. Hence, this statement is physically accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements II and III only are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.

चरण 1: गतिज ऊर्जा वितरण का मूल्यांकन
धातु में इलेक्ट्रॉनों की ऊर्जा का एक वितरण होता है। केवल वही इलेक्ट्रॉन जो सतह पर होते हैं और बिना किसी संघट्ट के बाहर निकलते हैं, अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा \(K_{\max} = h\nu - \phi_0\) प्राप्त करते हैं। आंतरिक परतों से निकलने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉन ऊर्जा खोकर \(0\) से लेकर \(K_{\max}\) के बीच किसी भी ऊर्जा के साथ निकलते हैं। अतः सभी इलेक्ट्रॉनों की ऊर्जा \(K_{\max}\) बताना गलत है।

चरण 2: फोटॉन के रैखिक संवेग का मूल्यांकन
फोटॉन मॉडल के अनुसार, शून्य विराम द्रव्यमान होने के बावजूद फोटॉन का आपेक्षिकीय संवेग अशून्य होता है और \(p = h\nu/c = h/\lambda\) होता है। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: क्षेत्रों में फोटॉन की उदासीनता का मूल्यांकन
फोटॉन पर कोई विद्युत आवेश नहीं होता (\(q = 0\))। अतः लोरेंत्ज़ बल शून्य होने के कारण विद्युत या चुंबकीय क्षेत्रों से गुजरने पर इसका कोई विक्षेपण नहीं होता। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन II और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन I गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I and II only are correct.
Statements II and III only are correct.
Statements I, II and III are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_DUAL_NATURE_ST3_Q04 - De Broglie matter waves and relativistic velocities

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the dual nature of radiation and matter:

Statement I: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated from rest across a potential difference \(V\) is inversely proportional to the accelerating potential \(V\).

Statement II: A macroscopic ball of mass \(0.12\text{ kg}\) travelling at \(20\text{ m s}^{-1}\) has a de Broglie wavelength of the order of \(10^{-34}\text{ m}\), which is vastly smaller than atomic dimensions and undetectable experimentally.

Statement III: For a relativistic free particle with non-zero rest mass, the phase velocity of the associated de Broglie wave exceeds the speed of light in vacuum, while its group velocity equals the particle velocity.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

विकिरण तथा द्रव्य की द्वैत प्रकृति के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: विभवांतर \(V\) से विरामावस्था से त्वरित एक इलेक्ट्रॉन की दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य त्वरित विभव \(V\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।

कथन II: \(20\text{ m s}^{-1}\) की चाल से गतिमान \(0.12\text{ kg}\) द्रव्यमान की स्थूल गेंद की दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य लगभग \(10^{-34}\text{ m}\) कोटि की होती है, जो परमाणुक आकार से बहुत छोटी और प्रायोगिक रूप से अप्रेक्षणीय है।

कथन III: अशून्य विराम द्रव्यमान वाले आपेक्षिकीय मुक्त कण के लिए, संबद्ध दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंग का कला वेग निर्वात में प्रकाश की चाल से अधिक होता है, जबकि इसका समूह वेग कण के वेग के बराबर होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Accelerating Voltage Dependence
For an electron of charge \(e\) and mass \(m\) accelerated through potential \(V\), its kinetic energy is \(K = e V\) and momentum is \(p = \sqrt{2m e V}\). The de Broglie wavelength is \(\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m e V}} = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ nm}\). Therefore, \(\lambda\) is inversely proportional to the square root of \(V\) (\(\lambda \propto V^{-1/2}\)), not inversely proportional to \(V\). Hence, this statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Calculation of Macroscopic Matter Wavelength
The momentum of the ball is \(p = mv = (0.12\text{ kg})(20\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 2.4\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\). The de Broglie wavelength is \(\lambda = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{2.4\text{ kg m s}^{-1}} = 2.76 \times 10^{-34}\text{ m}\). This wavelength is about \(10^{-19}\) times the diameter of a proton and far below the dimension of any conceivable obstacle or aperture. Thus, macroscopic objects do not exhibit wave behavior. Hence, this statement is physically accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Phase and Group Velocity for Matter Waves
For a relativistic particle, \(E = \hbar\omega = \gamma mc^2\) and \(p = \hbar k = \gamma mv\). The phase velocity is \(v_p = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{E}{p} = \frac{c^2}{v}\). Since \(v < c\) for any massive particle, \(v_p > c\). The group velocity of the wave packet is \(v_g = \frac{d\omega}{dk} = \frac{dE}{dp} = \frac{p c^2}{E} = v\), which identically equals the particle speed and carries information. Hence, this statement is physically accurate.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements II and III only are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.

चरण 1: त्वरित विभव पर निर्भरता का मूल्यांकन
\(V\) विभवांतर से त्वरित इलेक्ट्रॉन की गतिज ऊर्जा \(K = e V\) और संवेग \(p = \sqrt{2m e V}\) होता है। दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य \(\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2m e V}} = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ nm}\) होती है। अतः \(\lambda\) त्वरित विभव के वर्गमूल के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है (\(\lambda \propto 1/\sqrt{V}\)), \(V\) के नहीं। अतः पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: स्थूल द्रव्य तरंगदैर्घ्य की गणना
गेंद का संवेग \(p = mv = (0.12)(20) = 2.4\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\) है। दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य \(\lambda = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{2.4} = 2.76 \times 10^{-34}\text{ m}\) प्राप्त होती है। यह अतिसूक्ष्म मान किसी भी भौतिक अवरोधक से अत्यधिक छोटा है जिससे विवर्तन संभव नहीं है। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: द्रव्य तरंगों के कला एवं समूह वेग का मूल्यांकन
आपेक्षिकीय कण के लिए कला वेग \(v_p = \frac{E}{p} = \frac{c^2}{v}\) होता है। चूंकि \(v < c\), अतः \(v_p > c\) होता है। समूह वेग \(v_g = \frac{dE}{dp} = v\) होता है जो सीधे कण के वेग के बराबर होता है। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन II और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन I गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I and II only are correct.
Statements I and III only are correct.
Statements I, II and III are all correct.
Statements II and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Historical pioneers and key discoveries in modern physics

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. J. J. Thomson I. Hypothesis of wave nature of matter
B. Heinrich Hertz II. Discovery of photoelectric effect in spark discharge
C. R. A. Millikan III. Determination of specific charge of cathode ray particles
D. Louis de Broglie IV. Precision measurement of elementary charge on electron

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Historical investigations established the corpuscular nature of electrons, quantized charge, photoelectric emission, and matter waves.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Scientist
In 1897, J. J. Thomson applied mutually perpendicular electric and magnetic fields to cathode rays to determine the specific charge (\(e/m\)) of electrons, proving their universality. Thus, Thomson associates with determination of specific charge of cathode ray particles.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Scientist
In 1887, Heinrich Hertz discovered the photoelectric effect by observing that high-voltage spark discharges across a detector loop were enhanced when illuminated by ultraviolet light. Thus, Hertz associates with discovery of photoelectric effect in spark discharge.

Step 4: Evaluation of Third Scientist
In 1913, R. A. Millikan performed the oil-drop experiment to demonstrate charge quantization and measure the elementary charge \(e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\). Thus, Millikan associates with precision measurement of elementary charge on electron.

Step 5: Evaluation of Fourth Scientist
In 1924, Louis de Broglie proposed that moving material particles exhibit wave properties with wavelength \(\lambda = h/p\). Thus, de Broglie associates with hypothesis of wave nature of matter.

Step 6: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Matching each historical scientist with the corresponding breakthrough yields: J. J. Thomson with specific charge determination, Heinrich Hertz with photoelectric discovery, R. A. Millikan with oil-drop charge measurement, and Louis de Broglie with the wave nature of matter.

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct match is J. J. Thomson with specific charge determination, Heinrich Hertz with spark discharge photoelectric discovery, R. A. Millikan with elementary charge measurement, and Louis de Broglie with wave nature of matter (A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Photoelectric physical quantities and defining mathematical relations

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Planck's constant (\(h\)) I. \(\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}\)
B. Stopping potential (\(V_0\)) II. \(\frac{K_{\max}}{e}\)
C. Work function (\(\phi_0\)) III. \([\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-1}]\) with SI unit \(\text{J s}\)
D. de Broglie wavelength (\(\lambda\)) IV. \(h\nu_0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fundamental quantities in radiation and matter interactions possess characteristic dimensional structures and governing equations.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Quantity
Planck's constant \(h\) connects wave frequency to photon energy via \(E = h u\), giving dimensions \([ ext{M L}^2 ext{T}^{-1}]\) and the SI unit \( ext{J s}\). Thus, Planck's constant associates with unit \( ext{J s}\).

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Quantity
The stopping potential \(V_0\) is the retarding potential that brings the most energetic photoelectrons to rest, defined by \(e V_0 = K_{\max}\), or \(V_0 = rac{K_{\max}}{e}\). Thus, stopping potential associates with \( rac{K_{\max}}{e}\).

Step 4: Evaluation of Third Quantity
The work function \(\phi_0\) is the minimum energy required to liberate an electron from the metal surface, related to threshold frequency by \(\phi_0 = h u_0\). Thus, work function associates with \(h u_0\).

Step 5: Evaluation of Fourth Quantity
The de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda\) for a particle of mass \(m\) and kinetic energy \(K\) with momentum \(p = \sqrt{2mK}\) is given by \(\lambda = rac{h}{p} = rac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}\). Thus, de Broglie wavelength associates with \( rac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}\).

Step 6: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Matching each physical quantity with its defining relation yields: Planck's constant with \( ext{J s}\), stopping potential with \(K_{\max}/e\), work function with \(h u_0\), and de Broglie wavelength with \(h/\sqrt{2mK}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct match is Planck's constant with unit \( ext{J s}\), stopping potential with \(K_{\max}/e\), work function with \(h u_0\), and de Broglie wavelength with \(h/\sqrt{2mK}\) (A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Experimental parameters and photoelectric response variations

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Increasing incident light intensity at constant frequency (\(\nu > \nu_0\)) I. Increases stopping potential magnitude and maximum kinetic energy
B. Increasing incident radiation frequency at constant intensity II. Increases threshold frequency and shifts emission threshold to shorter wavelengths
C. Increasing accelerating potential of collector plate III. Increases saturation photocurrent linearly without altering stopping potential
D. Using photosensitive metal with a larger work function IV. Increases photocurrent gradually until saturation current is reached

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The photoelectric apparatus responds distinctly to intensity, frequency, accelerating voltage, and emitter surface properties.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Parameter
Increasing light intensity increases photon flux (photons per second), thereby ejecting more electrons per second and increasing the saturation photocurrent linearly, while leaving individual photon energy and stopping potential unchanged. Thus, intensity increase associates with linear saturation current increase.

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Parameter
Increasing frequency increases individual photon energy \(E = h u\), which elevates maximum kinetic energy \(K_{\max} = h u - \phi_0\) and requires a larger stopping potential \(V_0\). Thus, frequency increase associates with increase in stopping potential and maximum kinetic energy.

Step 4: Evaluation of Third Parameter
Increasing the positive collector potential attracts more emitted electrons towards the collector plate, causing photocurrent to rise gradually until reaching a constant saturation value where all emitted electrons are collected. Thus, accelerating potential associates with photocurrent rise up to saturation.

Step 5: Evaluation of Fourth Parameter
A metal with a larger work function \(\phi_0\) requires higher threshold energy \(h u_0 = \phi_0\), shifting the cut-off frequency higher (shorter threshold wavelength). Thus, larger work function associates with increased threshold frequency.

Step 6: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Matching each experimental change with its physical consequence yields: intensity increase with linear saturation current increase, frequency increase with increased stopping potential, accelerating potential with current rise to saturation, and larger work function with increased threshold frequency.

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct match is intensity increase with linear saturation current increase, frequency increase with higher stopping potential, accelerating voltage with current rise to saturation, and higher work function with increased threshold frequency (A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q04 - Graphical features of photoelectric equations and physical significance

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Slope of stopping potential (\(V_0\)) versus frequency (\(\nu\)) graph I. Universal constant \(h\) (Planck's constant)
B. Intercept on frequency axis of \(V_0\) versus \(\nu\) graph II. Universal ratio \(h/e\) identical for all emitter metals
C. Intercept on potential axis of \(V_0\) versus \(\nu\) graph III. Negative work function potential ratio \(-\phi_0/e\)
D. Slope of maximum kinetic energy (\(K_{\max}\)) versus frequency (\(\nu\)) graph IV. Material-specific threshold frequency \(\nu_0 = \phi_0/h\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Einstein's photoelectric equation relates kinetic energy and stopping potential to radiation frequency through linear equations.

Step 2: Evaluation of First Graphical Feature
Expressing the photoelectric law as \(V_0 = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi_0}{e}\), the slope with respect to frequency \( u\) is \(h/e\), which consists purely of fundamental universal constants and is identical for every photosensitive metal. Thus, the slope of \(V_0\) versus \( u\) associates with universal ratio \(h/e\).

Step 3: Evaluation of Second Graphical Feature
Setting \(V_0 = 0\) in \(V_0 = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi_0}{e}\) gives \( u = \phi_0/h = u_0\), which is the material-specific threshold frequency. Thus, the frequency intercept associates with \( u_0 = \phi_0/h\).

Step 4: Evaluation of Third Graphical Feature
Evaluating \(V_0\) at \( u = 0\) gives an intercept on the potential axis of \(-\phi_0/e\), directly measuring the negative of the metal's work function divided by elementary charge. Thus, the potential intercept associates with \(-\phi_0/e\).

Step 5: Evaluation of Fourth Graphical Feature
In Einstein's relation \(K_{\max} = h u - \phi_0\), plotting \(K_{\max}\) versus frequency \( u\) gives a straight line with slope equal to Planck's constant \(h\). Thus, the slope of \(K_{\max}\) versus \( u\) associates with Planck's constant \(h\).

Step 6: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Matching each graphical parameter with its physical significance yields: slope of \(V_0\) versus \( u\) with \(h/e\), frequency intercept with \( u_0\), potential intercept with \(-\phi_0/e\), and slope of \(K_{\max}\) versus \( u\) with \(h\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct match is slope of stopping potential graph with universal ratio \(h/e\), frequency-axis intercept with threshold frequency \( u_0\), potential-axis intercept with \(-\phi_0/e\), and slope of kinetic energy graph with Planck's constant \(h\) (A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q01 - Mass of electron from specific charge and elementary charge

questiontext.text: In a cathode ray discharge tube experiment, the specific charge of an electron was determined to be \(1.76 \times 10^{11}\text{ C kg}^{-1}\). If the elementary charge of an electron measured in Millikan's oil-drop experiment is \(1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\), what is the mass of the electron?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Specific charge \(e/m = 1.76 \times 10^{11}\text{ C kg}^{-1}\), elementary charge \(e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The electron is treated as a fundamental particle of rest mass \(m\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(m = \frac{e}{e/m}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(m = \frac{1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}}{1.76 \times 10^{11}\text{ C kg}^{-1}} = 0.9102 \times 10^{-30}\text{ kg} = 9.10 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated mass is \(9.10 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\), which matches standard physical data.

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(9.10 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q02 - Conversion of cesium work function from electron volts to joules

questiontext.text: The work function of cesium is \(2.14\text{ eV}\). What is this work function expressed in joules? (Take \(1\text{ eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Work function \(\phi_0 = 2.14\text{ eV}\), conversion factor \(1\text{ eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Energy conversion between atomic units and SI units is linear.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\phi_0(\text{J}) = \phi_0(\text{eV}) \times 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J/eV}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\phi_0 = 2.14 \times 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} = 3.428 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} \approx 3.43 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The work function in SI units is \(3.43 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(3.43 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q03 - Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons from stopping voltage

questiontext.text: In a photoelectric effect experiment, the cut-off (stopping) potential is measured to be \(1.50\text{ V}\). What is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons in joules? (Take \(e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Stopping potential \(V_0 = 1.50\text{ V}\), elementary charge \(e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The maximum kinetic energy is completely converted into electrostatic potential energy at cut-off.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(K_{\max} = e V_0\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(K_{\max} = (1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (1.50\text{ V}) = 2.40 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The maximum kinetic energy is \(2.40 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(2.40 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q04 - Energy of photon of given optical frequency

questiontext.text: A laser produces monochromatic light of frequency \(6.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\). What is the energy of a single photon in this light beam? (Use Planck's constant \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Frequency \(\nu = 6.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\), Planck's constant \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Each photon carries energy given by Planck's quantum hypothesis.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(E = h\nu\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(E = (6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}) \times (6.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ s}^{-1}) = 3.98 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The energy of each photon is \(3.98 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(3.98 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q05 - de Broglie wavelength of moving macroscopic ball

questiontext.text: A ball of mass \(0.120\text{ kg}\) moves with a speed of \(20.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\). What is the de Broglie wavelength associated with the ball? (Use \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass \(m = 0.120\text{ kg}\), velocity \(v = 20.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Motion is non-relativistic.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Linear momentum \(p = mv\), de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = \frac{h}{p}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Momentum: \(p = 0.120\text{ kg} \times 20.0\text{ m s}^{-1} = 2.40\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\). Wavelength: \(\lambda = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{2.40\text{ kg m s}^{-1}} = 2.76 \times 10^{-34}\text{ m}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The de Broglie wavelength is \(2.76 \times 10^{-34}\text{ m}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(2.76 \times 10^{-34}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q06 - Saturation photocurrent ratio on doubling source distance

questiontext.text: A small isotropic point light source placed at a distance of \(1.0\text{ m}\) from a photocell produces a saturation current of \(16.0\ \mu\text{A}\). If the source is moved to a distance of \(2.0\text{ m}\) from the photocell, what will be the new saturation photocurrent?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial distance \(r_1 = 1.0\text{ m}\), initial saturation current \(I_1 = 16.0\ \mu\text{A}\). Final distance \(r_2 = 2.0\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The source radiates uniformly in all directions; the inverse-square law of intensity applies.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(I \propto \text{Intensity} \propto \frac{1}{r^2} \implies \frac{I_2}{I_1} = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(I_2 = I_1 \left(\frac{1.0}{2.0}\right)^2 = 16.0\ \mu\text{A} \times \frac{1}{4} = 4.0\ \mu\text{A}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The new saturation current is \(4.0\ \mu\text{A}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(4.0\ \mu\text{A}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q07 - Linear momentum of photon of red light

questiontext.text: What is the linear momentum of a photon of wavelength \(663\text{ nm}\)? (Take \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Wavelength \(\lambda = 663\text{ nm} = 6.63 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\), Planck's constant \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Photon momentum relates to wavelength via de Broglie-Einstein relation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(p = \frac{h}{\lambda}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(p = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{6.63 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}} = 1.00 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The photon momentum is \(1.00 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(1.00 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q08 - Threshold frequency from metal work function

questiontext.text: The work function of a certain metal is \(3.315\text{ eV}\). What is the threshold frequency for photoelectric emission from this metal? (Take \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\) and \(1\text{ eV} = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Work function \(\phi_0 = 3.315\text{ eV} = 3.315 \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} = 5.304 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Photoelectric emission occurs when photon energy equals or exceeds the work function.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\nu_0 = \frac{\phi_0}{h}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\nu_0 = \frac{5.304 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}}{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}} = 8.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The threshold frequency is \(8.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(8.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q09 - Threshold wavelength from work function of metal

questiontext.text: The work function of a photosensitive metal is \(2.48\text{ eV}\). What is the threshold wavelength of the incident light required for photoemission? (Use \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Work function \(\phi_0 = 2.48\text{ eV}\), Planck product \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The threshold wavelength corresponds to the minimum photon energy needed to eject an electron.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\lambda_0 = \frac{hc}{\phi_0}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\lambda_0 = \frac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{2.48\text{ eV}} = 500\text{ nm}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The threshold wavelength is \(500\text{ nm}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(500\text{ nm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q10 - Calculation of stopping potential from frequencies

questiontext.text: Light of frequency \(8.20 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\) illuminates a metal having a threshold frequency of \(3.30 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\). What is the cut-off (stopping) potential for photoelectric emission? (Use \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\) and \(e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Incident frequency \( u = 8.20 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\), threshold frequency \( u_0 = 3.30 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\), \(e = 1.60 imes 10^{-19} ext{ C}\), \(h = 6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The maximum kinetic energy equals the electrostatic stopping work: \(e V_0 = K_{\max}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(e V_0 = h( u - u_0) \implies V_0 = rac{h}{e}( u - u_0)\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Frequency difference: \( u - u_0 = (8.20 - 3.30) imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz} = 4.90 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\). Ratio \( rac{h}{e} = rac{6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}}{1.60 imes 10^{-19} ext{ C}} \approx 4.144 imes 10^{-15} ext{ V s}\). Then \(V_0 = (4.144 imes 10^{-15} ext{ V s}) imes (4.90 imes 10^{14} ext{ s}^{-1}) \approx 2.03 ext{ V}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The stopping potential is \(2.03 ext{ V}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(2.03 ext{ V}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q11 - Photon emission rate from monochromatic laser beam

questiontext.text: A laser emits monochromatic light of frequency \(6.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\) with an output power of \(2.00 \times 10^{-3}\text{ W}\). How many photons per second on average are emitted by the source? (Take \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Laser power \(P = 2.00 imes 10^{-3} ext{ W}\), frequency \( u = 6.00 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\), \(h = 6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All emitted radiant power consists of individual photons of energy \(E = h u\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(P = N E = N h u \implies N = \frac{P}{h u}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Energy per photon: \(E = (6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}) imes (6.00 imes 10^{14} ext{ s}^{-1}) = 3.978 imes 10^{-19} ext{ J}\). Rate: \(N = rac{2.00 imes 10^{-3} ext{ W}}{3.978 imes 10^{-19} ext{ J}} \approx 5.03 imes 10^{15} ext{ photons s}^{-1} \approx 5.0 imes 10^{15} ext{ s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The emission rate is \(5.0 imes 10^{15} ext{ photons s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(5.0 imes 10^{15} ext{ s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q12 - Rate of photons arriving from helium neon laser

questiontext.text: A helium-neon laser produces monochromatic light of wavelength \(632.8\text{ nm}\) with a beam power of \(9.42\text{ mW}\). How many photons per second on average arrive at a target fully intercepting this beam? (Use \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\), \(c = 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Power \(P = 9.42 \times 10^{-3}\text{ W}\), \(\lambda = 6.328 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\), \(c = 3.00 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Target area fully intercepts the uniform beam without loss.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Photon energy \(E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}\), arrival rate \(N = \frac{P}{E} = \frac{P\lambda}{hc}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(E = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.00 \times 10^8}{6.328 \times 10^{-7}} = 3.143 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}\). Then \(N = \frac{9.42 \times 10^{-3}\text{ W}}{3.143 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}} = 2.997 \times 10^{16}\text{ s}^{-1} \approx 3.00 \times 10^{16}\text{ s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The arrival rate is \(3.00 \times 10^{16}\text{ photons per second}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(3.00 \times 10^{16}\text{ s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q13 - Maximum speed of photoelectrons from given frequencies

questiontext.text: Light of frequency \(7.21 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\) is incident on a metal surface. If the threshold frequency of the metal is \(4.73 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\), what is the maximum speed of the ejected photoelectrons? (Take \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\), \(m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Incident frequency \( u = 7.21 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\), threshold frequency \( u_0 = 4.73 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\), \(m_e = 9.11 imes 10^{-31} ext{ kg}\), \(h = 6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Photoelectrons with maximum speed correspond to least bound surface electrons.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(K_{\max} = h( u - u_0) = rac{1}{2} m_e v_{\max}^2 \implies v_{\max} = \sqrt{ rac{2h( u - u_0)}{m_e}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\Delta u = (7.21 - 4.73) imes 10^{14} = 2.48 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\). \(K_{\max} = (6.63 imes 10^{-34}) imes (2.48 imes 10^{14}) = 1.644 imes 10^{-19} ext{ J}\). Then \(v_{\max} = \sqrt{ rac{2 imes 1.644 imes 10^{-19} ext{ J}}{9.11 imes 10^{-31} ext{ kg}}} = \sqrt{3.609 imes 10^{11}} \approx 6.01 imes 10^5 ext{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The maximum speed is \(6.01 imes 10^5 ext{ m s}^{-1}\) (or approximately \(6.0 imes 10^5 ext{ m s}^{-1}\)).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(6.0 imes 10^5 ext{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q14 - Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons from cesium metal

questiontext.text: The work function of cesium is \(2.14\text{ eV}\). When light of frequency \(6.00 \times 10^{14}\text{ Hz}\) is incident on the cesium surface, what is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons? (Take \(h = 4.14 \times 10^{-15}\text{ eV s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Work function \(\phi_0 = 2.14 ext{ eV}\), frequency \( u = 6.00 imes 10^{14} ext{ Hz}\), \(h = 4.14 imes 10^{-15} ext{ eV s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Photoelectric equation: \(K_{\max} = h u - \phi_0\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(E = h u\), \(K_{\max} = E - \phi_0\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(E = (4.14 imes 10^{-15} ext{ eV s}) imes (6.00 imes 10^{14} ext{ s}^{-1}) = 2.484 ext{ eV}\). Then \(K_{\max} = 2.484 ext{ eV} - 2.140 ext{ eV} = 0.344 ext{ eV} \approx 0.34 ext{ eV}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The maximum kinetic energy is \(0.34 ext{ eV}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(0.34 ext{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q15 - Maximum frequency of continuous X rays at thirty kilovolts

questiontext.text: Electrons in an X-ray tube are accelerated by an operating potential difference of \(30.0\text{ kV}\). What is the maximum frequency of the continuous X-rays produced? (Use \(e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Accelerating potential \(V = 30.0 ext{ kV} = 30,000 ext{ V}\), \(e = 1.60 imes 10^{-19} ext{ C}\), \(h = 6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Maximum photon energy equals total kinetic energy gained by an electron: \(h u_{\max} = eV\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\( u_{\max} = rac{eV}{h}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\( u_{\max} = rac{(1.60 imes 10^{-19} ext{ C}) imes (30,000 ext{ V})}{6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}} = rac{4.80 imes 10^{-15} ext{ J}}{6.63 imes 10^{-34} ext{ J s}} = 7.24 imes 10^{18} ext{ Hz}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The maximum frequency of the continuous X-rays is \(7.24 imes 10^{18} ext{ Hz}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(7.24 imes 10^{18} ext{ Hz}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q16 - Minimum wavelength of continuous X rays from thirty kilovolt tube

questiontext.text: What is the minimum wavelength \(\lambda_{\min}\) of the continuous X-ray spectrum produced by an X-ray tube operating at \(30.0\text{ kV}\)? (Take \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Operating potential \(V = 30.0\text{ kV} = 30,000\text{ V}\), \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The cut-off wavelength corresponds to complete conversion of electron kinetic energy into a single photon.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\lambda_{\min} = \frac{hc}{eV}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\lambda_{\min} = \frac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{30,000\text{ eV}} = 0.04133\text{ nm} = 41.3\text{ pm}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The minimum wavelength is \(0.0413\text{ nm}\) (or \(41.3\text{ pm}\)).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(0.0413\text{ nm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q17 - de Broglie wavelength of electron moving at given speed

questiontext.text: An electron is moving with a speed of \(5.40 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\). What is its associated de Broglie wavelength? (Take \(m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass \(m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}\), velocity \(v = 5.40 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Velocity is well below \(c\); non-relativistic mechanics is valid.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
Linear momentum \(p = m_e v\), de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = \frac{h}{p}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(p = (9.11 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}) \times (5.40 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 4.919 \times 10^{-24}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\). Then \(\lambda = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{4.919 \times 10^{-24}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}} = 0.1348 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m} \approx 0.135\text{ nm}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The de Broglie wavelength is \(0.135\text{ nm}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(0.135\text{ nm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q18 - de Broglie wavelength of electron accelerated through hundred volts

questiontext.text: An electron initially at rest is accelerated through an electric potential difference of \(100\text{ V}\). What is its associated de Broglie wavelength?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Accelerating potential \(V = 100\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard simplified formula for an electron accelerated through potential \(V\) applies.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\lambda = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ nm}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\lambda = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{100}}\text{ nm} = \frac{1.227}{10}\text{ nm} = 0.1227\text{ nm} \approx 0.123\text{ nm}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The de Broglie wavelength is \(0.123\text{ nm}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(0.123\text{ nm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q19 - Ratio of de Broglie wavelength of proton to alpha particle

questiontext.text: A proton and an \(\alpha\)-particle are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. If the mass of an \(\alpha\)-particle is \(4\) times that of a proton and its charge is \(2\) times that of a proton, the ratio \(\lambda_p / \lambda_\alpha\) is approximately:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Accelerating potential \(V\) is identical for both particles. \(m_\alpha = 4m_p\), \(q_\alpha = 2q_p\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both particles acquire kinetic energy \(K = qV\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}} \implies \frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha} = \sqrt{\frac{m_\alpha q_\alpha}{m_p q_p}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_\alpha} = \sqrt{\frac{(4m_p)(2q_p)}{(m_p)(q_p)}} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.83\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is \(2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.83\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(2.83\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q20 - Ratio of de Broglie wavelength of proton to deuteron

questiontext.text: A proton and a deuteron (mass \(m_d \approx 2m_p\), charge \(q_d = q_p\)) are accelerated from rest through the same potential difference \(V\). What is the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths \(\lambda_p / \lambda_d\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Accelerating potential = \(V\), \(m_d = 2m_p\), \(q_d = q_p\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Kinetic energy \(K = qV\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}} \implies \frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_d} = \sqrt{\frac{m_d q_d}{m_p q_p}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(\frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_d} = \sqrt{\frac{(2m_p)(q_p)}{(m_p)(q_p)}} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is \(\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(\sqrt{2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q21 - Cathode work function from argon laser stopping potential

questiontext.text: Light of wavelength \(488\text{ nm}\) from an argon laser is incident on the emitter of a photoelectric cell. If the stopping potential is \(0.38\text{ V}\), what is the work function of the emitter material? (Take \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(\lambda = 488\text{ nm}\), \(V_0 = 0.38\text{ V}\) (so \(e V_0 = 0.38\text{ eV}\)), \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Einstein's photoelectric equation applies: \(e V_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi_0\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\phi_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda} - e V_0\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Photon energy: \(E = \frac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{488\text{ nm}} = 2.541\text{ eV}\). Then \(\phi_0 = 2.541\text{ eV} - 0.380\text{ eV} = 2.161\text{ eV} \approx 2.16\text{ eV}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The work function is \(2.16\text{ eV}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(2.16\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q22 - Speed of hydrogen atom possessing photon momentum

questiontext.text: A photon has a wavelength of \(632.8\text{ nm}\). At what speed must a neutral hydrogen atom of mass \(1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\) travel in order to possess momentum equal to that of the photon? (Take \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Wavelength \(\lambda = 6.328 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\), \(m_H = 1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Momentum of photon equals momentum of atom: \(p = \frac{h}{\lambda} = m_H v\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(v = \frac{h}{m_H \lambda}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Photon momentum: \(p = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{6.328 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}} = 1.0477 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\). Speed of atom: \(v = \frac{1.0477 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}}{1.67 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}} \approx 0.627\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 0.63\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The speed of the hydrogen atom is \(0.63\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(0.63\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q23 - Calculation of Planck constant from stopping voltage slope

questiontext.text: In an experiment on the photoelectric effect, the slope of the cut-off potential \(V_0\) versus frequency \(\nu\) of incident radiation is determined to be \(4.12 \times 10^{-15}\text{ V s}\). What is the calculated value of Planck's constant? (Take \(e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Slope \(S = 4.12 \times 10^{-15}\text{ V s}\), \(e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Einstein's relation \(V_0 = \frac{h}{e}\nu - \frac{\phi_0}{e}\) gives slope \(S = \frac{h}{e}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(h = e \times S\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\(h = (1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (4.12 \times 10^{-15}\text{ V s}) = 6.592 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated Planck constant is \(6.59 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(6.59 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q24 - Thermal neutron de Broglie wavelength at room temperature

questiontext.text: A thermal neutron of mass \(1.675 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\) is in thermal equilibrium at a temperature of \(300\text{ K}\). If its average kinetic energy is \(K = \frac{3}{2} k_B T\), what is its de Broglie wavelength? (Use Boltzmann constant \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J K}^{-1}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(m = 1.675 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}\), \(T = 300\text{ K}\), \(k_B = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J K}^{-1}\), \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Thermal motion gives average momentum \(p = \sqrt{3 m k_B T}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{3 m k_B T}}\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Denominator term: \(3 m k_B T = 3 \times (1.675 \times 10^{-27}) \times (1.38 \times 10^{-23}) \times 300 = 2.080 \times 10^{-47}\text{ kg}^2\text{ m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}\). Momentum: \(p = \sqrt{2.080 \times 10^{-47}} \approx 4.561 \times 10^{-24}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}\). Wavelength: \(\lambda = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}}{4.561 \times 10^{-24}\text{ kg m s}^{-1}} = 0.1454 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m} \approx 0.145\text{ nm}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The de Broglie wavelength is \(0.145\text{ nm}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(0.145\text{ nm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q25 - Work function from stopping potential and incident wavelength

questiontext.text: When monochromatic light of wavelength \(454\text{ nm}\) illuminates a photosensitive plate, the photocurrent is brought to zero by a stopping potential of \(0.60\text{ V}\). What is the work function of the metal? (Use \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Incident wavelength \(\lambda = 454\text{ nm}\), stopping potential \(V_0 = 0.60\text{ V}\) (so \(e V_0 = 0.60\text{ eV}\)), \(hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Photoelectrons are retarded by potential \(V_0\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(e V_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi_0 \implies \phi_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda} - e V_0\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Photon energy: \(E = \frac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{454\text{ nm}} \approx 2.731\text{ eV}\). Then \(\phi_0 = 2.731\text{ eV} - 0.600\text{ eV} = 2.131\text{ eV} \approx 2.14\text{ eV}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The work function of the metal is \(2.14\text{ eV}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(2.14\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q26 - Work function from stopping potentials upon frequency doubling

questiontext.text: Light of frequency \(\nu\) falling on a metallic surface produces photoelectrons with a stopping potential of \(1.20\text{ V}\). When light of frequency \(2\nu\) is incident on the same surface, the stopping potential is found to be \(3.60\text{ V}\). What is the work function of the metal?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial stopping potential \(V_1 = 1.20 ext{ V}\), final stopping potential \(V_2 = 3.60 ext{ V}\) when frequency is doubled to \(2 u\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Einstein's photoelectric equation governs both conditions.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\(e V_1 = h u - \phi_0\) and \(e V_2 = 2h u - \phi_0\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
From the first equation: \(h u = e V_1 + \phi_0\). Substitute into the second equation: \(e V_2 = 2(e V_1 + \phi_0) - \phi_0 = 2e V_1 + \phi_0\). Rearranging for \(\phi_0\): \(\phi_0 = e(V_2 - 2V_1)\). Substituting numerical values: \(\phi_0 = e(3.60 ext{ V} - 2 imes 1.20 ext{ V}) = e(3.60 ext{ V} - 2.40 ext{ V}) = 1.20 ext{ eV}\).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The work function is \(1.20 ext{ eV}\).

Final Conceptual Conclusion:
Therefore, the correct numerical value is: \(1.20 ext{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_MCQ_Q27 - Work function determination from speeds at different wavelengths

questiontext.text: When radiation of wavelength \(\lambda\) is incident on a metal surface, the maximum speed of emitted photoelectrons is \(v\). When radiation of wavelength \(\lambda / 3\) is incident on the same metal surface, the maximum speed of photoelectrons is \(2v\).
