Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The speed of the electron in the first excited state is \(1.09 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

चरण 1: बोर मॉडल में कक्षीय चाल का सूत्र
हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर सिद्धांत में, \(n^{\text{वीं}}\) स्थायी कक्षा में कक्षीय चाल निम्न है: \[v_n = \frac{v_1}{n}\] जहाँ \(v_1 = 2.18 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\) मूल अवस्था (\(n = 1\)) में चाल है।

चरण 2: क्वांटम संख्या की पहचान
प्रथम उत्तेजित अवस्था मुख्य क्वांटम संख्या \(n = 2\) के संगत होती है।

चरण 3: n = 2 के लिए गणना
\[v_2 = \frac{v_1}{2} = \frac{2.18 \times 10^6}{2} = 1.09 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

चरण 4: अंतिम उत्तर
प्रथम उत्तेजित अवस्था में इलेक्ट्रॉन की चाल \(1.09 \times 10^6\text{ m s}^{-1}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q46 - Lyman series wavelength range from series limit to first line

questiontext.text:
In the emission spectrum of atomic hydrogen, what are the wavelengths of the first line (longest wavelength, \(n = 2 \to 1\)) and the series limit (shortest wavelength, \(n = \infty \to 1\)) of the Lyman series? (Take Rydberg constant \(R = 1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}\))

परमाण्विक हाइड्रोजन के उत्सर्जन स्पेक्ट्रम में, लाइमन श्रेणी की प्रथम रेखा (अधिकतम तरंगदैर्घ्य, \(n = 2 \to 1\)) और श्रेणी सीमा (न्यूनतम तरंगदैर्घ्य, \(n = \infty \to 1\)) की तरंगदैर्घ्य क्या हैं? (रिडबर्ग नियतांक \(R = 1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}\) मानिए)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula for Lyman Series Wavelengths
The Rydberg formula for the Lyman series (\(n_f = 1\)) is: \[\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{n_i^2} \right) \quad (n_i = 2, 3, 4, \dots)\]

Step 2: First Line (Longest Wavelength)
For the first line, \(n_i = 2\): \[\frac{1}{\lambda_{\text{max}}} = R \left( 1 - \frac{1}{4} \right) = \frac{3}{4} R\] \[\lambda_{\text{max}} = \frac{4}{3R} = \frac{4}{3 \times (1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1})} = 1.2156 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \approx 121.6\text{ nm}\]

Step 3: Series Limit (Shortest Wavelength)
For the series limit, \(n_i = \infty\): \[\frac{1}{\lambda_{\text{min}}} = R \left( 1 - 0 \right) = R\] \[\lambda_{\text{min}} = \frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{1.097 \times 10^7\text{ m}^{-1}} = 9.116 \times 10^{-8}\text{ m} \approx 91.2\text{ nm}\]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The wavelength range of the Lyman series is from \(91.2\text{ nm}\) to \(121.6\text{ nm}\).

चरण 1: लाइमन श्रेणी की तरंगदैर्घ्य का सूत्र
लाइमन श्रेणी (\(n_f = 1\)) के लिए रिडबर्ग सूत्र: \[\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( 1 - \frac{1}{n_i^2} \right)\]

चरण 2: प्रथम रेखा (अधिकतम तरंगदैर्घ्य)
\(n_i = 2\) के लिए: \[\lambda_{\text{max}} = \frac{4}{3R} = \frac{4}{3 \times 1.097 \times 10^7} \approx 121.6\text{ nm}\]

चरण 3: श्रेणी सीमा (न्यूनतम तरंगदैर्घ्य)
\(n_i = \infty\) के लिए: \[\lambda_{\text{min}} = \frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{1.097 \times 10^7} \approx 91.2\text{ nm}\]

चरण 4: अंतिम उत्तर
लाइमन श्रेणी की प्रथम रेखा की तरंगदैर्घ्य \(121.6\text{ nm}\) तथा श्रेणी सीमा की तरंगदैर्घ्य \(91.2\text{ nm}\) है।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q47 - Bohr correspondence principle for large quantum numbers

questiontext.text:
According to the correspondence principle in Bohr's model of the atom, under what limiting condition does the quantum transition frequency of emitted radiation coincide with the classical orbital revolution frequency of the electron?

परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में संगतता सिद्धांत के अनुसार, किस सीमांत स्थिति के अंतर्गत उत्सर्जित विकिरण की क्वांटम संक्रमण आवृत्ति इलेक्ट्रॉन के चिरप्रतिष्ठित कक्षीय परिक्रमण की आवृत्ति से मेल खाती है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classical Orbital Frequency
Classically, the frequency of revolution is: \[ u_{ ext{classical}} = rac{v_n}{2\pi r_n} = rac{m e^4}{4\varepsilon_0^2 h^3 n^3}\]

Step 2: Quantum Transition Frequency
In Bohr's theory, the frequency of a photon emitted during a transition from state \(n\) to \(n - 1\) is: \[ u_{ ext{quantum}} = rac{E_n - E_{n-1}}{h} = rac{m e^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^3} \left( rac{1}{(n-1)^2} - rac{1}{n^2} ight) = rac{m e^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^3} rac{2n - 1}{n^2(n-1)^2}\]

Step 3: Limiting Behavior for Very Large n
For very large \(n\) (\(n \gg 1\)), we can approximate: \[2n - 1 \approx 2n \quad ext{and} \quad (n-1)^2 \approx n^2\] Thus: \[ u_{ ext{quantum}} \approx rac{m e^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^3} rac{2n}{n^4} = rac{m e^4}{4\varepsilon_0^2 h^3 n^3} = u_{ ext{classical}}\]

Step 4: Correspondence Principle
Thus, quantum predictions smoothly merge with classical predictions in the domain of large quantum numbers (\(n \gg 1\)).

Step 5: Final Answer
The frequencies coincide for transitions between adjacent states with very large quantum numbers (\(n o n - 1\) with \(n \gg 1\)).

चरण 1: चिरप्रतिष्ठित कक्षीय आवृत्ति
चिरप्रतिष्ठित रूप से, परिक्रमण की आवृत्ति है: \[ u_{ ext{classical}} = rac{m e^4}{4\varepsilon_0^2 h^3 n^3}\]

चरण 2: क्वांटम संक्रमण आवृत्ति
\(n\) से \(n - 1\) में संक्रमण के लिए: \[ u_{ ext{quantum}} = rac{m e^4}{8\varepsilon_0^2 h^3} rac{2n - 1}{n^2(n-1)^2}\]

चरण 3: अत्यधिक बड़े n के लिए सीमांत व्यवहार
अत्यधिक बड़े \(n\) (\(n \gg 1\)) के लिए, \(2n - 1 \approx 2n\) तथा \(n-1 \approx n\): \[ u_{ ext{quantum}} \approx rac{m e^4}{4\varepsilon_0^2 h^3 n^3} = u_{ ext{classical}}\]

चरण 4: संगतता सिद्धांत
इस प्रकार, उच्च क्वांटम संख्याओं (\(n \gg 1\)) की सीमा में क्वांटम यांत्रिकी के परिणाम चिरप्रतिष्ठित भौतिकी के परिणामों के समरूप हो जाते हैं।

चरण 5: अंतिम उत्तर
अत्यधिक बड़ी क्वांटम संख्याओं वाले निकटवर्ती स्तरों (\(n \gg 1\) के लिए \(n o n - 1\)) के बीच संक्रमण के लिए आवृत्तियाँ संपाती होती हैं।

answer.text: For transitions directly to the ground state from any level (\(n \to 1\)).
Only when the principal quantum number \(n = 1\) and the radius approaches the Bohr radius.
For transitions between adjacent states with very large quantum numbers (\(n \to n - 1\) with \(n \gg 1\)).
When the electron is completely detached and at rest at infinity (\(E = 0\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q48 - Physical reason for discrepancy in gold nuclear radius estimate

questiontext.text:
The distance of closest approach of a \(7.7\text{ MeV}\) \(\alpha\)-particle to a gold nucleus is computed to be approximately \(30\text{ fm}\), whereas the actual measured radius of the gold nucleus is about \(6\text{ fm}\). What is the physical cause of this discrepancy?

सोने के नाभिक के लिए \(7.7\text{ MeV}\) वाले \(\alpha\)-कण की निकटतम पहुँच की दूरी लगभग \(30\text{ fm}\) परिकलित की जाती है, जबकि सोने के नाभिक की वास्तविक मापी गई त्रिज्या लगभग \(6\text{ fm}\) है। इस विसंगति का भौतिक कारण क्या है?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Concept of Distance of Closest Approach
In Geiger-Marsden scattering, the distance of closest approach \(d\) is the turning point where the incoming alpha particle's kinetic energy \(K = 7.7\text{ MeV}\) is entirely converted into electrostatic potential energy in the gold nucleus's Coulomb field: \[d = \frac{2 Z e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K} \approx 30\text{ fm}\]

Step 2: Comparison with Actual Nuclear Radius
The actual physical radius of the gold nucleus (determined by higher-energy electron and neutron scattering) is \(R_{\text{Au}} \approx 6\text{ fm}\).

Step 3: Cause of Discrepancy
Because \(d \approx 30\text{ fm} > R_{\text{Au}} \approx 6\text{ fm}\), the alpha particle lacks sufficient kinetic energy to penetrate close enough to make direct physical contact with the nucleus. The intense Coulomb repulsive force halts and turns the alpha particle around while it is still several nuclear radii away from the nuclear surface.

Step 4: Final Answer
The alpha particle reverses its motion due to Coulomb repulsion without ever actually touching the nuclear surface.

चरण 1: निकटतम पहुँच की दूरी की संकल्पना
गाइगर-मार्सडेन प्रकीर्णन में, निकटतम पहुँच की दूरी \(d\) वह मोड़ बिंदु है जहाँ आपतित अल्फा कण की गतिज ऊर्जा \(K = 7.7\text{ MeV}\) पूरी तरह से कूलॉम क्षेत्र में स्थिरवैद्युत स्थितिज ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित हो जाती है: \[d \approx 30\text{ fm}\]

चरण 2: वास्तविक नाभिकीय त्रिज्या से तुलना
सोने के नाभिक की वास्तविक भौतिक त्रिज्या लगभग \(R_{\text{Au}} \approx 6\text{ fm}\) है।

चरण 3: विसंगति का कारण
चूँकि \(d \approx 30\text{ fm} > R_{\text{Au}} \approx 6\text{ fm}\), अतः \(7.7\text{ MeV}\) ऊर्जा वाले अल्फा कण में नाभिक की सतह को स्पर्श करने के लिए पर्याप्त ऊर्जा नहीं होती। तीव्र कूलॉम प्रतिकर्षण बल अल्फा कण को नाभिक की सतह से काफी दूर ही रोककर वापस मोड़ देता है।

चरण 4: अंतिम उत्तर
कूलॉम प्रतिकर्षण के कारण \(\alpha\)-कण वास्तविक नाभिकीय सतह को स्पर्श किए बिना ही काफी पहले रुककर वापस लौट जाता है।

answer.text: Strong nuclear attractive forces repel the \(\alpha\)-particle at large distances.
The atomic electrons shield the gold nucleus completely, doubling the apparent barrier radius.
Relativistic increase in the mass of the \(\alpha\)-particle stops it prematurely.
The electrostatic Coulomb repulsion brings the \(\alpha\)-particle to rest and reverses its motion well before it ever touches the nuclear surface.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q01 - Electrostatic equilibrium and net force in Thomson and Rutherford models

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the ground state of Thomson's model, the electrons are in stable electrostatic equilibrium, whereas in Rutherford's model, the revolving electrons always experience a net centripetal force.

Statement II: An atom has a nearly continuous mass distribution in Thomson's model, but has a highly non-uniform mass distribution in Rutherford's model.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: थॉमसन मॉडल की मूल अवस्था में, इलेक्ट्रॉन स्थायी स्थिरवैद्युत साम्यावस्था में होते हैं, जबकि रदरफोर्ड मॉडल में, परिक्रमण करने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉन सदैव एक नेट अभिकेंद्रीय बल का अनुभव करते हैं।

कथन II: थॉमसन मॉडल में परमाणु का द्रव्यमान वितरण लगभग सतत होता है, लेकिन रदरफोर्ड मॉडल में द्रव्यमान वितरण अत्यधिक असमान होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
In Thomson's plum pudding model, electrons are embedded in a uniform positive charge cloud and settle in static equilibrium positions where the net electrostatic force on each is zero. In Rutherford's nuclear model, electrons revolve in circular planetary orbits around the nucleus, constantly experiencing a net inward electrostatic Coulomb force that acts as the requisite centripetal force (\(F_c = \frac{m v^2}{r}\)). Therefore, the first statement is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
Thomson assumed that both mass and positive charge are uniformly distributed throughout the entire sphere of the atom of diameter approximately \(10^{-10}\text{ m}\). In contrast, Rutherford's scattering experiments proved that virtually all the mass and positive charge reside in a tiny central nucleus of size \(10^{-15}\text{ m}\) to \(10^{-14}\text{ m}\), leaving the surrounding atomic space largely empty. Thus, the mass distribution is highly concentrated and non-uniform. Therefore, the second statement is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the first statement and the second statement are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
थॉमसन के प्लम पुडिंग मॉडल में, इलेक्ट्रॉन एकसमान धनावेशित बादल में अंतःस्थापित होते हैं और स्थिर साम्यावस्था में रहते हैं जहाँ उन पर नेट स्थिरवैद्युत बल शून्य होता है। रदरफोर्ड के नाभिकीय मॉडल में, इलेक्ट्रॉन वृत्ताकार कक्षाओं में परिक्रमण करते हैं और निरंतर एक नेट कूलॉम आकर्षण बल का अनुभव करते हैं जो अभिकेंद्रीय बल (\(F_c = \frac{m v^2}{r}\)) का कार्य करता है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
थॉमसन मॉडल में परमाणु का द्रव्यमान लगभग \(10^{-10}\text{ m}\) के पूरे आयतन में एकसमान रूप से वितरित माना गया था। इसके विपरीत, रदरफोर्ड के प्रकीर्णन प्रयोगों ने सिद्ध किया कि लगभग संपूर्ण द्रव्यमान \(10^{-15}\text{ m}\) से \(10^{-14}\text{ m}\) के सूक्ष्म नाभिक में केंद्रित होता है और शेष परमाणु मुख्यतः रिक्त होता है। अतः द्रव्यमान वितरण अत्यधिक असमान है। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन और दूसरा कथन दोनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q02 - Alpha scattering fraction and nature of classical atomic collapse

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the Geiger-Marsden scattering experiment, more than 50% of the incident \(\alpha\)-particles are deflected by angles greater than \(90^\circ\).

Statement II: Classical electromagnetic theory predicts that an atom based on Thomson's model is doomed to collapse due to continuous radiation of orbital energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: गाइगर-मार्सडेन प्रकीर्णन प्रयोग में, आपतित \(\alpha\)-कणों में से 50% से अधिक कण \(90^\circ\) से अधिक कोणों पर विक्षेपित होते हैं।

कथन II: चिरप्रतिष्ठित विद्युतचुंबकीय सिद्धांत यह भविष्यवाणी करता है कि थॉमसन मॉडल पर आधारित परमाणु कक्षीय ऊर्जा के निरंतर विकिरण के कारण नष्ट होने के लिए अभिशप्त है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
The Geiger-Marsden scattering measurements established that most \(\alpha\)-particles pass through the thin gold foil undeviated; only about \(0.14\%\) scatter by more than \(1^\circ\), and merely about 1 in 8000 (approximately \(0.0125\%\)) deflects by more than \(90^\circ\). The claim that more than \(50\%\) deflect by more than \(90^\circ\) is factually incorrect. Therefore, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
In classical physics, an accelerating charge continuously radiates electromagnetic energy and spirals into the center; this classical instability and collapse applies strictly to Rutherford's planetary model, not Thomson's model. In Thomson's model, electrons are at rest in static positions, so orbital radiative spiralling does not occur. Therefore, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the first statement and the second statement are incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
गाइगर-मार्सडेन प्रयोग के आंकड़ों के अनुसार अधिकांश \(\alpha\)-कण बिना किसी विक्षेपण के सीधे निकल जाते हैं; केवल लगभग \(0.14\%\) कण \(1^\circ\) से अधिक विक्षेपित होते हैं, और लगभग 8000 में से केवल 1 कण (लगभग \(0.0125\%\)) ही \(90^\circ\) से अधिक कोण पर विक्षेपित होता है। 50% से अधिक कणों के विक्षेपित होने का दावा असत्य है। अतः पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
चिरप्रतिष्ठित विद्युतचुंबकीय सिद्धांत के अनुसार त्वरित आवेश विकिरण उत्सर्जित करता है और सर्पिलाकार गति करते हुए केंद्र में गिर जाता है; यह शास्त्रीय अस्थायित्व और पतन रदरफोर्ड के ग्रहीय मॉडल पर लागू होता है, थॉमसन मॉडल पर नहीं। थॉमसन मॉडल में इलेक्ट्रॉन स्थिर होते हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन और दूसरा कथन दोनों गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q03 - Impact parameter relation to deflection angle and target nucleus mass assumption

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Rutherford scattering, an \(\alpha\)-particle with a smaller impact parameter experiences a larger electrostatic deflection angle.

Statement II: During alpha scattering by a gold foil, the gold nucleus recoils rapidly at a speed greater than that of the incident \(\alpha\)-particle.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: रदरफोर्ड प्रकीर्णन में, छोटे संघट्ट प्राचल वाला \(\alpha\)-कण एक बड़ा स्थिरवैद्युत विक्षेपण कोण अनुभव करता है।

कथन II: सोने की पन्नी द्वारा अल्फा प्रकीर्णन के दौरान, सोने का नाभिक आपतित \(\alpha\)-कण की तुलना में अधिक तीव्र चाल से पीछे हटता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
The impact parameter \(b\) is defined as the perpendicular distance between the initial velocity vector of the incoming \(\alpha\)-particle and the center of the nucleus. A trajectory with a smaller impact parameter approaches closer to the concentrated positive charge, thereby experiencing an intensely stronger Coulomb repulsive force (\(F \propto \frac{1}{r^2}\)) and undergoing a significantly larger deflection angle \(\theta\). At minimum impact parameter (head-on collision), the particle rebounds back (\(\theta \cong 180^\circ\)). Therefore, the first statement is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
The atomic mass of a gold nucleus (\(Z = 79, A \approx 197\)) is about 50 times heavier than that of an \(\alpha\)-particle (\(A = 4\)). Because the target gold nucleus is so massive in comparison, it remains essentially stationary throughout the scattering collision, rather than recoiling with a speed greater than the projectile. Therefore, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
संघट्ट प्राचल \(b\) नाभिक के केंद्र से \(\alpha\)-कण के प्रारंभिक वेग सदिश की लंबवत दूरी है। छोटा संघट्ट प्राचल कण को नाभिक के अधिक निकट लाता है, जहाँ वह अत्यंत तीव्र कूलॉम प्रतिकर्षण बल का अनुभव करता है और उसका विक्षेपण कोण \(\theta\) अधिक होता है। सम्मुख संघट्ट (\(b \to 0\)) में कण लगभग पीछे लौट आता है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
सोने के नाभिक का द्रव्यमान (\(A \approx 197\)) \(\alpha\)-कण (\(A = 4\)) की तुलना में लगभग 50 गुना भारी होता है। इतना भारी होने के कारण प्रकीर्णन प्रक्रिया के दौरान सोने का नाभिक लगभग स्थिर रहता है, न कि आपतित कण से तीव्र चाल से पीछे हटता है। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन सही है, लेकिन दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q04 - Solid hydrogen target substitution and alpha particle mass comparison

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If the alpha-particle scattering experiment is repeated using a thin sheet of solid hydrogen instead of gold foil, large-angle scattering and backward rebounding of \(\alpha\)-particles will still be observed.

Statement II: An \(\alpha\)-particle is roughly four times more massive than a hydrogen nucleus (proton), so in an elastic collision the target proton is knocked forward while the \(\alpha\)-particle continues forward with only small deflections.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: यदि सोने की पन्नी के स्थान पर ठोस हाइड्रोजन की पतली शीट का उपयोग करके अल्फा-कण प्रकीर्णन प्रयोग दोहराया जाए, तो भी \(\alpha\)-कणों का बड़े कोण पर प्रकीर्णन और पीछे की ओर लौटना देखा जाएगा।

कथन II: एक \(\alpha\)-कण एक हाइड्रोजन नाभिक (प्रोटॉन) की तुलना में लगभग चार गुना भारी होता है, इसलिए एक प्रत्यास्थ संघट्ट में लक्ष्य प्रोटॉन आगे की ओर धकेल दिया जाता है जबकि \(\alpha\)-कण केवल सूक्ष्म विक्षेपण के साथ आगे बढ़ता रहता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
When an incident particle strikes a target that is significantly lighter than itself, classical mechanics dictates that the heavier projectile cannot bounce backwards in an elastic collision. In solid hydrogen, the target nucleus is a single proton of mass \(m_p\), whereas the \(\alpha\)-particle has mass \(4m_p\). Therefore, the \(\alpha\)-particle will never rebound or scatter at large angles exceeding \(90^\circ\). The claim that large-angle backward rebounding would be observed is false. Therefore, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
Because the \(\alpha\)-particle has mass \(m_\alpha \approx 4\text{ u}\) and the hydrogen nucleus has mass \(m_H \approx 1\text{ u}\), conservation of linear momentum and energy in head-on elastic collision shows that the target proton is projected forward at high speed while the incoming \(\alpha\)-particle maintains forward motion. Therefore, the second statement is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
जब एक भारी कण अपने से बहुत हल्के स्थिर कण से टकराता है, तो यांत्रिकी के नियमानुसार भारी प्रक्षेप्य कभी भी पीछे की ओर नहीं लौट सकता। ठोस हाइड्रोजन में लक्ष्य प्रोटॉन (\(1\text{ u}\)) होता है जबकि \(\alpha\)-कण का द्रव्यमान \(4\text{ u}\) होता है। अतः \(\alpha\)-कण कभी भी \(90^\circ\) से अधिक के बड़े कोणों पर विक्षेपित नहीं हो सकता। अतः पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
\(\alpha\)-कण का द्रव्यमान (\(4\text{ u}\)) हाइड्रोजन नाभिक (प्रोटॉन, \(1\text{ u}\)) से चार गुना अधिक होता है। प्रत्यास्थ संघट्ट में संवेग और ऊर्जा संरक्षण के अनुसार हल्का लक्ष्य प्रोटॉन तीव्र गति से आगे की ओर प्रक्षिप्त हो जाता है और भारी \(\alpha\)-कण सूक्ष्म विक्षेपण के साथ आगे बढ़ता रहता है। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन गलत है, लेकिन दूसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q05 - Bohr orbit radius and velocity scaling laws with principal quantum number

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, the radius of the stationary orbit is directly proportional to the square of the principal quantum number (\(r_n \propto n^2\)).

Statement II: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, the orbital speed of the electron is inversely proportional to the principal quantum number (\(v_n \propto \frac{1}{n}\)).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में, स्थायी कक्षा की त्रिज्या मुख्य क्वांटम संख्या के वर्ग के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है (\(r_n \propto n^2\))।

कथन II: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में, इलेक्ट्रॉन की कक्षीय चाल मुख्य क्वांटम संख्या के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है (\(v_n \propto \frac{1}{n}\))।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
Combining Bohr's quantisation condition \(m v_n r_n = \frac{n h}{2\pi}\) with the centripetal Coulomb balance \(\frac{m v_n^2}{r_n} = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r_n^2}\) yields the radius expression \(r_n = \left(\frac{h^2 \varepsilon_0}{\pi m e^2}\right) n^2 = n^2 a_0\). Hence, the orbital radius is strictly proportional to \(n^2\). Therefore, the first statement is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
Eliminating the radius from the same equations yields the orbital velocity \(v_n = \frac{e^2}{2\varepsilon_0 h} \cdot \frac{1}{n} = \frac{v_1}{n}\). Hence, the orbital speed decreases as \(\frac{1}{n}\) as the electron occupies higher principal quantum levels. Therefore, the second statement is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the first statement and the second statement are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
बोर की क्वांटीकरण शर्त \(m v_n r_n = \frac{n h}{2\pi}\) तथा अभिकेंद्रीय संतुलन समीकरण \(\frac{m v_n^2}{r_n} = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r_n^2}\) को संयोजित करने पर त्रिज्या \(r_n = n^2 a_0\) प्राप्त होती है। अतः कक्षा की त्रिज्या \(n^2\) के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
इन्हीं समीकरणों से वेग का व्यंजक \(v_n = \frac{v_1}{n}\) प्राप्त होता है। जैसे-जैसे मुख्य क्वांटम संख्या \(n\) बढ़ती है, इलेक्ट्रॉन की कक्षीय चाल \(\frac{1}{n}\) के अनुपात में घटती जाती है। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन और दूसरा कथन दोनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q06 - Hydrogen energy level spacing and ionisation energy comparison from excited states

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: As the principal quantum number \(n\) increases in a hydrogen atom, the energy separation between consecutive stationary levels increases continuously.

Statement II: The minimum energy required to liberate an electron from an excited state (\(n > 1\)) of a hydrogen atom is greater than the ground state ionisation energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जैसे-जैसे हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में मुख्य क्वांटम संख्या \(n\) बढ़ती है, क्रमागत स्थायी स्तरों के बीच ऊर्जा अंतराल निरंतर बढ़ता जाता है।

कथन II: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की किसी उत्तेजित अवस्था (\(n > 1\)) से एक इलेक्ट्रॉन को मुक्त करने के लिए आवश्यक न्यूनतम ऊर्जा मूल अवस्था की आयनन ऊर्जा से अधिक होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
The energy of the \(n^{\text{th}}\) level is given by \(E_n = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2}\). The energy gap between adjacent levels is \(\Delta E = E_{n+1} - E_n = 13.6 \left(\frac{1}{n^2} - \frac{1}{(n+1)^2}\right) = 13.6 \frac{2n+1}{n^2(n+1)^2}\). For \(n=1 \to 2\), the gap is \(10.2\text{ eV}\); for \(n=2 \to 3\), it is \(1.89\text{ eV}\); for \(n=3 \to 4\), it is \(0.66\text{ eV}\). Thus, the levels come closer and closer together as \(n\) increases, meaning the energy separation decreases, not increases. Therefore, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
The energy required to free an electron from state \(n\) to infinity is the binding energy \(|E_n| = \frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2}\). For the ground state (\(n = 1\)), this is \(13.6\text{ eV}\). For any excited state (\(n \ge 2\)), the required energy is at most \(\frac{13.6}{4} = 3.4\text{ eV}\), which is strictly less than \(13.6\text{ eV}\). As excitation increases, the energy needed to ionise the atom decreases. Therefore, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both the first statement and the second statement are incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
ऊर्जा स्तर का सूत्र \(E_n = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2}\) होता है। क्रमागत स्तरों के बीच ऊर्जा अंतर: \(n=1\) से 2 के लिए \(10.2\text{ eV}\), \(n=2\) से 3 के लिए \(1.89\text{ eV}\), तथा \(n=3\) से 4 के लिए \(0.66\text{ eV}\) है। जैसे-जैसे \(n\) बढ़ता है, ऊर्जा स्तर एक-दूसरे के निकट आते जाते हैं और ऊर्जा अंतराल घटता जाता है, बढ़ता नहीं। अतः पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
किसी अवस्था \(n\) से इलेक्ट्रॉन को मुक्त करने के लिए आवश्यक ऊर्जा \(|E_n| = \frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2}\) होती है। मूल अवस्था (\(n = 1\)) के लिए यह \(13.6\text{ eV}\) है, जबकि किसी उत्तेजित अवस्था (\(n \ge 2\)) के लिए यह अधिकतम \(3.4\text{ eV}\) होती है, जो स्पष्ट रूप से कम है। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन और दूसरा कथन दोनों गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q07 - de Broglie standing wave quantization condition and multi-electron atom limitations

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Louis de Broglie explained Bohr's angular momentum quantisation postulate by demonstrating that stationary electron orbits correspond to circular standing waves where the orbital circumference equals an integral number of de Broglie wavelengths (\(2\pi r_n = n\lambda\)).

Statement II: Bohr's model successfully explains the relative spectral intensities of emitted lines and accurately predicts the energy levels of multi-electron atoms like neutral helium and lithium.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: लुई डी ब्रॉग्ली ने यह प्रदर्शित करके बोर के कोणीय संवेग क्वांटीकरण अभिगृहीत की व्याख्या की कि स्थायी इलेक्ट्रॉन कक्षाएँ वृत्ताकार अप्रगामी तरंगों के संगत होती हैं जहाँ कक्षा की परिधि डी ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य की पूर्ण संख्या के बराबर होती है (\(2\pi r_n = n\lambda\))।

कथन II: बोर का मॉडल उत्सर्जित रेखाओं की आपेक्षिक स्पेक्ट्रमी तीव्रताओं की सफलतापूर्वक व्याख्या करता है तथा उदासीन हीलियम और लिथियम जैसे बहु-इलेक्ट्रॉन परमाणुओं के ऊर्जा स्तरों की सटीक भविष्यवाणी करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
De Broglie proposed that an orbiting electron behaves as a particle wave that forms stationary resonant standing waves around the circular orbit, satisfying \(2\pi r_n = n \lambda\). Substituting \(\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{m v_n}\) directly yields \(m v_n r_n = \frac{n h}{2\pi}\), precisely justifying Bohr's second postulate. Therefore, the first statement is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
Bohr's model suffers from critical limitations: it cannot be extended to multi-electron atoms (such as neutral helium or lithium) because it ignores electron-electron electrostatic repulsions, and it is completely unable to explain why certain spectral transition frequencies are intense while others are weak (variation of spectral line intensities). Therefore, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is correct, but the second statement is incorrect.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
डी ब्रॉग्ली ने प्रतिपादित किया कि परिक्रमण करता हुआ इलेक्ट्रॉन एक द्रव्य तरंग की तरह व्यवहार करता है और कक्षा में अप्रगामी तरंग अनुनाद शर्त \(2\pi r_n = n \lambda\) को संतुष्ट करता है। \(\lambda = \frac{h}{m v_n}\) रखने पर बोर का दूसरा अभिगृहीत \(m v_n r_n = \frac{n h}{2\pi}\) प्राप्त होता है। अतः पहला कथन सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
बोर मॉडल की मुख्य कमियाँ यह हैं कि यह बहु-इलेक्ट्रॉन परमाणुओं (जैसे उदासीन हीलियम या लिथियम) पर लागू नहीं होता क्योंकि यह इलेक्ट्रॉन-इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रतिकर्षण की उपेक्षा करता है, और यह स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखाओं की आपेक्षिक तीव्रताओं की भिन्नता को समझाने में पूरी तरह असमर्थ है। अतः दूसरा कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन सही है, लेकिन दूसरा कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST2_Q08 - Orbital period scaling and correspondence between orbital and radiation frequencies

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Bohr's hydrogen atom, the orbital period of revolution of the electron scales with the principal quantum number as \(T_n \propto n^2\).

Statement II: Although the orbital revolution frequency and emitted radiation frequency differ for low quantum states, they coincide asymptotically for transitions between very large adjacent quantum numbers (\(n \to n - 1\) with \(n \gg 1\)).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: बोर के हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में, इलेक्ट्रॉन के परिक्रमण का कक्षीय आवर्तकाल मुख्य क्वांटम संख्या के साथ \(T_n \propto n^2\) के रूप में परिवर्तित होता है।

कथन II: यद्यपि निम्न क्वांटम अवस्थाओं के लिए कक्षीय परिक्रमण आवृत्ति और उत्सर्जित विकिरण आवृत्ति भिन्न होती हैं, फिर भी अत्यधिक बड़ी निकटवर्ती क्वांटम संख्याओं के बीच संक्रमण (\(n \to n - 1\) जहाँ \(n \gg 1\)) के लिए वे स्पर्शोन्मुख रूप से समान हो जाती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
The orbital period is given by \(T_n = \frac{2\pi r_n}{v_n}\). In Bohr's model, \(r_n \propto n^2\) and \(v_n \propto \frac{1}{n}\). Substituting these relations yields \(T_n \propto \frac{n^2}{1/n} = n^3\). Therefore, the orbital period scales as \(n^3\), not \(n^2\). Therefore, the first statement is incorrect.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
The transition radiation frequency between \(n\) and \(n-1\) is \(\nu = \frac{E_n - E_{n-1}}{h} \propto \left(\frac{1}{(n-1)^2} - \frac{1}{n^2}\right) = \frac{2n - 1}{n^2 (n-1)^2} \approx \frac{2}{n^3}\) for \(n \gg 1\). The orbital revolution frequency is \(f_{\text{orb}} = \frac{1}{T_n} \propto \frac{1}{n^3}\). In accordance with Bohr's correspondence principle, as stated in the textbook Points to Ponder, for very large quantum numbers the frequency of revolution and the frequency of the emitted spectral line coincide exactly. Therefore, the second statement is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, but the second statement is correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
कक्षीय आवर्तकाल \(T_n = \frac{2\pi r_n}{v_n}\) होता है। चूँकि \(r_n \propto n^2\) तथा \(v_n \propto \frac{1}{n}\) है, अतः \(T_n \propto \frac{n^2}{1/n} = n^3\) होता है। आवर्तकाल \(n^3\) के समानुपाती होता है, \(n^2\) के नहीं। अतः पहला कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
\(n\) और \(n-1\) के बीच संक्रमण आवृत्ति \(\nu \propto \left(\frac{1}{(n-1)^2} - \frac{1}{n^2}\right) \approx \frac{2}{n^3}\) (जहाँ \(n \gg 1\)) होती है। कक्षीय आवृत्ति भी \(f_{\text{orb}} \propto \frac{1}{n^3}\) होती है। पाठ्यपुस्तक के 'विचारणीय बिंदु' के अनुसार, अत्यधिक बड़ी क्वांटम संख्याओं के लिए परिक्रमण की आवृत्ति और उत्सर्जित स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखा की आवृत्ति परस्पर संपाती (समान) हो जाती हैं। अतः दूसरा कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन गलत है, लेकिन दूसरा कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST3_Q01 - Observations of Geiger-Marsden alpha particle scattering experiment

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the atom:

Statement I: Most of the incident \(\alpha\)-particles pass through the thin gold foil without suffering any appreciable collision or deflection.

Statement II: Only about 0.14% of the incident \(\alpha\)-particles scatter by more than \(1^\circ\).

Statement III: More than 10% of the incident \(\alpha\)-particles deflect by large angles exceeding \(90^\circ\).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

परमाणु के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: अधिकांश आपतित \(\alpha\)-कण बिना किसी उल्लेखनीय संघट्ट या विक्षेपण के पतली सोने की पन्नी से सीधे निकल जाते हैं।

कथन II: आपतित \(\alpha\)-कणों में से केवल लगभग 0.14% कण ही \(1^\circ\) से अधिक कोण पर प्रकीर्णित होते हैं।

कथन III: आपतित \(\alpha\)-कणों में से 10% से अधिक कण \(90^\circ\) से अधिक के बड़े कोणों पर विक्षेपित होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
In the Geiger-Marsden scattering experiment, the overwhelming majority of incident \(\alpha\)-particles travel straight through the foil undeviated, proving that most of an atom is empty space. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
The experimental data points plotted by Geiger and Marsden demonstrate that only about \(0.14\%\) of the incident \(\alpha\)-particles are deflected by an angle greater than \(1^\circ\). Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement III
The experimental measurements established that only about 1 in 8000 incident \(\alpha\)-particles (approximately \(0.0125\%\)) deflects by more than \(90^\circ\). The claim that more than \(10\%\) deflect by more than \(90^\circ\) is factually false. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements I and II only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
गाइगर-मार्सडेन प्रकीर्णन प्रयोग में, अधिकांश आपतित \(\alpha\)-कण बिना किसी विक्षेपण के सीधे निकल जाते हैं, जिससे यह सिद्ध होता है कि परमाणु का अधिकांश भाग रिक्त स्थान है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
गाइगर और मार्सडेन द्वारा प्राप्त प्रयोगात्मक आँकड़ों के अनुसार आपतित \(\alpha\)-कणों में से केवल लगभग \(0.14\%\) कण ही \(1^\circ\) से अधिक कोण पर विक्षेपित होते हैं। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का विश्लेषण
प्रयोगात्मक माप यह दर्शाते हैं कि लगभग 8000 में से केवल 1 कण (लगभग \(0.0125\%\)) ही \(90^\circ\) से अधिक कोण पर विक्षेपित होता है। 10% से अधिक कणों के विक्षेपित होने का दावा असत्य है। अतः कथन III गलत है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन I और II सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST3_Q02 - Postulates of Bohr model of hydrogen atom

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the atom:

Statement I: An electron revolving in any arbitrary orbit constantly radiates electromagnetic waves of continuously changing frequency.

Statement II: An electron revolves around the nucleus without radiating energy only in stationary orbits for which its orbital angular momentum is an integral multiple of \(\frac{h}{2\pi}\).

Statement III: When an electron makes a transition from an orbit of higher energy \(E_i\) to one of lower energy \(E_f\), the frequency of the emitted photon is given by \(h\nu = E_i - E_f\).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

परमाणु के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: किसी भी यादृच्छिक कक्षा में परिक्रमण करने वाला इलेक्ट्रॉन निरंतर बदलते हुए आवृत्ति की विद्युतचुंबकीय तरंगें उत्सर्जित करता रहता है।

कथन II: एक इलेक्ट्रॉन ऊर्जा उत्सर्जित किए बिना केवल उन्हीं स्थायी कक्षाओं में नाभिक के चारों ओर परिक्रमण करता है जिनके लिए उसका कक्षीय कोणीय संवेग \(\frac{h}{2\pi}\) का पूर्ण गुणज होता है।

कथन III: जब कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन उच्च ऊर्जा \(E_i\) वाली कक्षा से निम्न ऊर्जा \(E_f\) वाली कक्षा में संक्रमण करता है, तो उत्सर्जित फोटॉन की आवृत्ति \(h\nu = E_i - E_f\) द्वारा दी जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
Continuous radiation of energy from arbitrary orbits is the prediction of classical electrodynamics, which Bohr specifically rejected in his first postulate by asserting the existence of stable, non-radiating stationary orbits. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect as a postulate of Bohr's model.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
Bohr's second postulate explicitly defines stationary orbits by the quantum condition that the electron's orbital angular momentum is quantised as \(L = m v r = \frac{n h}{2\pi}\) (where \(n = 1, 2, 3, \dots\)). Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement III
Bohr's third postulate states that radiation is emitted in discrete quanta (photons) only during transitions between stationary states, with photon frequency determined by the Bohr frequency condition \(h\nu = E_i - E_f\). Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements II and III only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
यादृच्छिक कक्षाओं से निरंतर ऊर्जा विकिरण चिरप्रतिष्ठित विद्युतचुंबकीय सिद्धांत की भविष्यवाणी थी, जिसे बोर ने अपने पहले अभिगृहीत में गैर-विकिरणी स्थायी अवस्थाओं की अवधारणा देकर अस्वीकार किया था। अतः कथन I गलत है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
बोर का दूसरा अभिगृहीत यह स्पष्ट करता है कि इलेक्ट्रॉन केवल उन्हीं कक्षाओं में परिक्रमण करता है जिनका कक्षीय कोणीय संवेग \(L = \frac{n h}{2\pi}\) होता है। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का विश्लेषण
बोर का तीसरा अभिगृहीत बताता है कि उच्च ऊर्जा स्तर से निम्न ऊर्जा स्तर में संक्रमण के दौरान उत्सर्जित फोटॉन की आवृत्ति \(h\nu = E_i - E_f\) होती है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन II और III सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST3_Q03 - Hydrogen spectral series characteristics and electromagnetic wavelength regions

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the atom:

Statement I: The Lyman spectral series corresponds to electron transitions terminating on the ground state (\(n = 1\)) and lies entirely in the ultraviolet region.

Statement II: The Balmer spectral series corresponds to electron transitions terminating on the \(n = 3\) level and lies entirely in the infrared region.

Statement III: The Paschen spectral series corresponds to electron transitions terminating on the \(n = 3\) level and lies in the infrared region.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

परमाणु के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: लाइमन स्पेक्ट्रमी श्रेणी मूल अवस्था (\(n = 1\)) पर समाप्त होने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉन संक्रमणों के संगत होती है तथा पूरी तरह पराबैंगनी क्षेत्र में स्थित होती है।

कथन II: बामर स्पेक्ट्रमी श्रेणी \(n = 3\) स्तर पर समाप्त होने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉन संक्रमणों के संगत होती है तथा पूरी तरह अवरक्त क्षेत्र में स्थित होती है।

कथन III: पाशन स्पेक्ट्रमी श्रेणी \(n = 3\) स्तर पर समाप्त होने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉन संक्रमणों के संगत होती है तथा अवरक्त क्षेत्र में स्थित होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
In atomic hydrogen, transitions from excited states (\(n = 2, 3, 4, \dots\)) down to \(n = 1\) form the Lyman series. Its wavelengths range from \(121.6\text{ nm}\) down to the series limit at \(91.2\text{ nm}\), placing it entirely in the ultraviolet portion of the spectrum. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
The Balmer series corresponds to transitions terminating on the first excited state (\(n = 2\)), and its visible lines span from \(656.3\text{ nm}\) down to \(364.6\text{ nm}\). It does not terminate on \(n = 3\) nor does it lie in the infrared region. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement III
The Paschen series corresponds to transitions terminating on the second excited state (\(n = 3\)) from levels \(n = 4, 5, \dots\), with lines (such as \(1875\text{ nm}\) and series limit at \(820\text{ nm}\)) lying in the infrared region. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements I and III only are correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में उत्तेजित अवस्थाओं से \(n = 1\) पर होने वाले संक्रमण लाइमन श्रेणी बनाते हैं। इसकी तरंगदैर्घ्य \(121.6\text{ nm}\) से \(91.2\text{ nm}\) तक होती है, जो पराबैंगनी क्षेत्र में आती है। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
बामर श्रेणी \(n = 2\) स्तर पर समाप्त होने वाले संक्रमणों के संगत होती है और यह दृश्य प्रकाश क्षेत्र में स्थित होती है, न कि \(n = 3\) या अवरक्त क्षेत्र में। अतः कथन II गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन III का विश्लेषण
पाशन श्रेणी \(n = 3\) स्तर पर समाप्त होने वाले संक्रमणों के संगत होती है और इसकी रेखाएँ (जैसे \(1875\text{ nm}\)) अवरक्त क्षेत्र में आती हैं। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
केवल कथन I और III सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_ST3_Q04 - Inadequacies and physical limitations of Bohr atomic model

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the atom:

Statement I: Bohr's model cannot be generalised even to two-electron atoms such as neutral helium because it does not account for electron-electron electrostatic interactions.

Statement II: Bohr's model is unable to explain the relative intensities of the frequencies in the emission line spectrum of hydrogen.

Statement III: The well-defined planar circular orbital trajectories depicted in Bohr's model are inconsistent with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

परमाणु के संबंध में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: बोर मॉडल को उदासीन हीलियम जैसे दो-इलेक्ट्रॉन परमाणुओं पर भी लागू नहीं किया जा सकता क्योंकि यह इलेक्ट्रॉन-इलेक्ट्रॉन स्थिरवैद्युत अन्योन्यक्रियाओं को शामिल नहीं करता है।

कथन II: बोर मॉडल हाइड्रोजन के उत्सर्जन रेखा स्पेक्ट्रम में आवृत्तियों की आपेक्षिक तीव्रताओं की व्याख्या करने में असमर्थ है।

कथन III: बोर मॉडल में दर्शाए गए सुस्पष्ट समतलीय वृत्ताकार कक्षीय प्रक्षेप-पथ हाइजेनबर्ग के अनिश्चितता सिद्धांत के असंगत हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Statement I
As detailed in Section 12.6 of the textbook, the formulation of Bohr's model accounts only for the electrical force between the nucleus and a single electron. In multi-electron atoms, electron-electron repulsions are comparable in magnitude to the nuclear attraction, causing Bohr's model to fail completely for neutral helium and larger atoms. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: Analysis of Statement II
Experimental spectroscopy shows that some spectral emission lines are significantly more intense than others because certain transitions have higher transition probabilities. Bohr's model predicts only the frequencies of transitions and cannot account for line intensity variations. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 3: Analysis of Statement III
As highlighted in the Points to Ponder, Bohr's model depicts electrons following sharply defined circular orbits with simultaneously precise coordinates and momenta. This classical trajectory picture contradicts the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, which requires replacing definite orbits with quantum mechanical probability distributions. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statements I, II and III are all correct.

चरण 1: कथन I का विश्लेषण
पाठ्यपुस्तक के अनुसार, बोर मॉडल केवल एकल-इलेक्ट्रॉन और नाभिक के बीच के आकर्षण बल पर आधारित है। बहु-इलेक्ट्रॉन परमाणुओं में इलेक्ट्रॉन-इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रतिकर्षण की उपेक्षा के कारण यह हीलियम पर भी लागू नहीं हो सकता। अतः कथन I सही है।

चरण 2: कथन II का विश्लेषण
प्रयोगों से ज्ञात होता है कि कुछ स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखाएँ अधिक तीव्र होती हैं क्योंकि कुछ संक्रमण अधिक अनुकूल होते हैं। बोर मॉडल केवल आवृत्तियों की भविष्यवाणी करता है किंतु तीव्रताओं की भिन्नता को नहीं समझा सकता। अतः कथन II सही है।

चरण 3: कथन III का विश्लेषण
'विचारणीय बिंदु' के अनुसार, बोर मॉडल में इलेक्ट्रॉन की निश्चित स्थिति और संवेग वाली सुस्पष्ट वृत्ताकार कक्षाएँ हाइजेनबर्ग के अनिश्चितता सिद्धांत के विपरीत हैं, जहाँ कक्षाओं को प्रायिकता क्षेत्रों से प्रतिस्थापित किया जाता है। अतः कथन III सही है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I, II और III सभी सही हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q01 - Matching hydrogen spectral series to regions

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Spectral Series (Column I) Spectral Region / Lower Level (Column II)
A. Lyman seriesI. Visible / \(n = 2\)
B. Balmer seriesII. Ultraviolet / \(n = 1\)
C. Paschen seriesIV. Infrared / \(n = 3\)
D. Brackett seriesIII. Far infrared / \(n = 4\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The spectral line series of hydrogen are classified by their terminal stationary level \(n_f\) in the Rydberg formula: Lyman (\(n_f = 1\)), Balmer (\(n_f = 2\)), Paschen (\(n_f = 3\)), and Brackett (\(n_f = 4\)).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Item Matching
1. For the Lyman series, transitions terminate at \(n = 1\), yielding high-energy photons in the ultraviolet region. Thus, A matches II.
2. For the Balmer series, transitions terminate at \(n = 2\), yielding four prominent emission lines in the visible region. Thus, B matches I.
3. For the Paschen series, transitions terminate at \(n = 3\), yielding photons in the infrared region. Thus, C matches IV.
4. For the Brackett series, transitions terminate at \(n = 4\), yielding photons in the far infrared region. Thus, D matches III.

Step 3: Application and Final Conclusion
Combining these pairings yields A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III as the correct match.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q02 - Historical atomic models and discoveries matching

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Scientist / Model (Column I) Key Discovery / Concept (Column II)
A. J. J. ThomsonI. Discovery of dense atomic nucleus
B. Ernst RutherfordII. Plum pudding model of uniform positive sphere
C. Niels BohrIII. Standing wave explanation of quantized orbits
D. Louis de BroglieIV. Quantized non-radiating stationary states

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The development of atomic physics progressed through distinct physical models and conceptual breakthroughs in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Item Matching
1. J. J. Thomson proposed the plum pudding model in 1898, picturing positive charge uniformly distributed throughout the volume with electrons embedded in it. Thus, A matches II.
2. Ernst Rutherford interpreted large-angle \(\alpha\)-particle scattering in 1911 to discover the atomic nucleus. Thus, B matches I.
3. Niels Bohr introduced quantum postulates in 1913, proposing stationary non-radiating energy states. Thus, C matches IV.
4. Louis de Broglie proposed particle wave nature in 1923, explaining Bohr's angular momentum quantisation via circular standing waves. Thus, D matches III.

Step 3: Application and Final Conclusion
Combining these associations yields A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III as the correct match.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q03 - Bohr model physical quantities scaling dependencies

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Physical Quantity in Bohr Orbit (Column I) Proportionality with \(n\) (Column II)
A. Orbital radius (\(r_n\))I. \(\propto \frac{1}{n^2}\)
B. Orbital speed (\(v_n\))II. \(\propto n^3\)
C. Total energy (\(|E_n|\))III. \(\propto n^2\)
D. Orbital time period (\(T_n\))IV. \(\propto \frac{1}{n}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Bohr's hydrogen atom model, all dynamical orbital properties scale with integer powers of the principal quantum number \(n\).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Item Matching
1. The radius of the \(n^{\text{th}}\) orbit is \(r_n = n^2 a_0 \propto n^2\). Thus, A matches III.
2. The orbital speed of the electron is \(v_n = \frac{v_1}{n} \propto \frac{1}{n}\). Thus, B matches IV.
3. The magnitude of the total bound energy is \(|E_n| = \frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2} \propto \frac{1}{n^2}\). Thus, C matches I.
4. The time period of revolution is \(T_n = \frac{2\pi r_n}{v_n} \propto \frac{n^2}{1/n} = n^3\). Thus, D matches II.

Step 3: Application and Final Conclusion
Combining these power dependencies yields A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II as the correct match.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q04 - Alpha scattering impact parameter collision kinematics

questiontext.text:
Match Column I with Column II:

Scattering Condition / Parameter (Column I) Physical Consequence / Characteristic (Column II)
A. Head-on collision (\(b = 0\))I. Undeviated trajectory with scattering angle \(\theta \approx 0\)
B. Large impact parameter (\(b \gg 10^{-14}\text{ m}\))II. \(\alpha\)-particle rebounds directly backward with \(\theta \approx \pi\)
C. Distance of closest approach (\(d\))III. Kinetic energy converts completely to electrostatic potential energy
D. Intermediate impact parameterIV. Coulomb deflection through an acute or obtuse angle

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In Rutherford's Coulomb scattering framework, an \(\alpha\)-particle follows a hyperbolic trajectory dictated by its impact parameter \(b\) and initial kinetic energy.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Item Matching
1. For a head-on collision, the impact parameter is zero (\(b = 0\)), causing the \(\alpha\)-particle to come to rest and rebound straight back along its path with \(\theta \approx 180^\circ = \pi\). Thus, A matches II.
2. For large impact parameters, the particle stays far from the nucleus where the electric field is weak, passing almost undeviated with \(\theta \approx 0\). Thus, B matches I.
3. At the distance of closest approach in a head-on collision, the incoming particle momentarily stops so that all its initial kinetic energy converts into electrostatic potential energy \(K = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{2Ze^2}{d}\). Thus, C matches III.
4. For moderate intermediate impact parameters, the particle experiences a net Coulomb repulsion deflecting it into an acute or obtuse angle. Thus, D matches IV.

Step 3: Application and Final Conclusion
Combining these geometric and kinetic features yields A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV as the correct match.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q01 - Number of alpha particles deflecting beyond ninety degrees

questiontext.text: In an \(\alpha\)-particle scattering experiment, about \(1\) in \(8000\) incident \(\alpha\)-particles is deflected by more than \(90^\circ\). If \(6.4 \times 10^4\) \(\alpha\)-particles are directed at the gold foil, how many are expected to deflect by more than \(90^\circ\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total number of incident \(\alpha\)-particles: \(N_{\text{total}} = 6.4 \times 10^4 = 64000\). Deflection probability for angles exceeding \(90^\circ\): \(P(\theta > 90^\circ) = \frac{1}{8000}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The expected number of particles scattered by more than \(90^\circ\) is given by:
\[ N = N_{\text{total}} \times P(\theta > 90^\circ) \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute the given values into the formula:
\[ N = 64000 \times \frac{1}{8000} = \frac{64000}{8000} = 8 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The division yields exactly \(8\) particles, which is dimensionally pure and consistent with the observed scattering ratio. The expected count of deflected particles is \(8\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q02 - Alpha particles scattered by more than one degree

questiontext.text: In Rutherford's \(\alpha\)-particle scattering experiment, approximately \(0.14\%\) of the incident \(\alpha\)-particles scatter by more than \(1^\circ\). Out of \(5.0 \times 10^5\) incident \(\alpha\)-particles, how many are scattered by more than \(1^\circ\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total number of incident \(\alpha\)-particles: \(N_{\text{total}} = 5.0 \times 10^5\). Percentage deflected by more than \(1^\circ\): \(0.14\%\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The scattered number is calculated using percentage proportion:
\[ N = N_{\text{total}} \times \frac{0.14}{100} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Perform the arithmetic:
\[ N = (5.0 \times 10^5) \times (1.4 \times 10^{-3}) = 5.0 \times 1.4 \times 10^2 = 7.0 \times 10^2 = 700 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
\(0.14\%\) of \(100,000\) is \(140\), so for \(500,000\) it is \(140 \times 5 = 700\). The number of particles scattered by more than \(1^\circ\) is \(700\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q03 - Ratio of atomic radius to nuclear radius calculation

questiontext.text: Taking the typical radius of an atom as \(1.0 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\) and the radius of its nucleus as \(1.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\), what is the ratio of the volume of the atom to the volume of the nucleus?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of the atom: \(R_{\text{atom}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\). Radius of the nucleus: \(R_{\text{nucleus}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Relevant Formulae
Assuming spherical geometry for both atom and nucleus, the volume is \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3\). The ratio of volumes is:
\[ \frac{V_{\text{atom}}}{V_{\text{nucleus}}} = \left(\frac{R_{\text{atom}}}{R_{\text{nucleus}}}\right)^3 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Compute the linear ratio first:
\[ \frac{R_{\text{atom}}}{R_{\text{nucleus}}} = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}}{1.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}} = 10^4 \]
Cube the linear ratio:
\[ \frac{V_{\text{atom}}}{V_{\text{nucleus}}} = (10^4)^3 = 10^{12} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is a pure dimensionless number of order \(10^{12}\), illustrating that an atom is mostly empty space. The ratio of volumes is \(10^{12}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q04 - Excitation energy required for first excited state

questiontext.text: The ground state energy of a hydrogen atom is \(-13.6\text{ eV}\), and the energy of its first excited state (\(n = 2\)) is \(-3.4\text{ eV}\). What is the minimum excitation energy required to excite the atom from the ground state to the first excited state?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Ground state energy: \(E_1 = -13.6\text{ eV}\). First excited state energy (\(n = 2\)): \(E_2 = -3.4\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Excitation energy \(\Delta E\) is the energy difference between the higher state and the ground state:
\[ \Delta E = E_2 - E_1 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute the energy values:
\[ \Delta E = -3.4\text{ eV} - (-13.6\text{ eV}) = -3.4\text{ eV} + 13.6\text{ eV} = 10.2\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The required excitation energy is positive and equal to \(10.2\text{ eV}\), consistent with standard Bohr transitions. The excitation energy is \(10.2\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q05 - Ratio of second to first Bohr orbit radii

questiontext.text: According to Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, what is the ratio of the radius of the second orbit (\(n = 2\)) to that of the first orbit (\(n = 1\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Principal quantum numbers: \(n_1 = 1\) and \(n_2 = 2\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The radius of the \(n^{\text{th}}\) Bohr orbit in a hydrogen atom is given by:
\[ r_n = n^2 a_0 \implies r_n \propto n^2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Form the ratio of the radii:
\[ \frac{r_2}{r_1} = \left(\frac{2}{1}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{1} = 4 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The radius increases with the square of the quantum number, yielding a ratio of \(4 : 1\). The ratio of the radii is \(4 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q06 - Ratio of electron speeds in Bohr orbits

questiontext.text: In Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, what is the ratio of the electron's speed in the first orbit (\(n = 1\)) to its speed in the third orbit (\(n = 3\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Principal quantum numbers: \(n_1 = 1\) and \(n_3 = 3\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The orbital speed of an electron in the \(n^{\text{th}}\) Bohr orbit is inversely proportional to \(n\):
\[ v_n = \frac{v_1}{n} \implies v_n \propto \frac{1}{n} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Form the ratio of the speeds:
\[ \frac{v_1}{v_3} = \frac{n_3}{n_1} = \frac{3}{1} = 3 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Since an electron moves slower in higher orbits, the ratio \(v_1 : v_3\) must be greater than 1, exactly \(3 : 1\). The ratio of the speeds is \(3 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q07 - Orbital angular momentum value in ground state hydrogen

questiontext.text: According to Bohr's second postulate, what is the magnitude of the orbital angular momentum of an electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom? (Take Planck's constant \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Planck's constant: \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}\). Ground state quantum number: \(n = 1\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Bohr's angular momentum quantisation condition is:
\[ L_n = \frac{nh}{2\pi} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
For \(n = 1\):
\[ L_1 = \frac{1 \times 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}}{2 \times 3.1416} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{6.2832}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s} \approx 1.055 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s} \approx 1.05 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
This value is the reduced Planck constant \(\hbar \approx 1.05 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}\). The angular momentum is \(1.05 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q08 - Calculation of second Bohr orbit radius value

questiontext.text: The radius of the innermost electron orbit of a hydrogen atom is \(5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\). What is the orbital radius of the electron in the \(n = 2\) state?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Innermost radius (first Bohr radius): \(r_1 = 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\). Target principal quantum number: \(n = 2\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
In the Bohr model, the radius of the \(n^{\text{th}}\) orbit is given by:
\[ r_n = n^2 r_1 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
For \(n = 2\):
\[ r_2 = 2^2 \times (5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}) = 4 \times 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m} = 21.2 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m} = 2.12 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Checking the value: \(2.12 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} = 0.212\text{ nm} = 2.12\text{ Å}\), which is physically sound. The radius of the second orbit is \(2.12 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q09 - Calculation of third Bohr orbit radius value

questiontext.text: Given that the radius of the ground state orbit of a hydrogen atom is \(5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\), what is the orbital radius of the electron in the \(n = 3\) state?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Ground state radius: \(r_1 = 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\). Quantum number: \(n = 3\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Bohr radius formula:
\[ r_n = n^2 r_1 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute \(n = 3\):
\[ r_3 = 3^2 \times (5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}) = 9 \times 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m} = 47.7 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m} = 4.77 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The third orbit radius is \(4.77 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} = 0.477\text{ nm}\). The radius of the third orbit is \(4.77 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q10 - Total energy value of third stationary state

questiontext.text: Using Bohr's formula \(E_n = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2}\), what is the total energy of an electron in the \(n = 3\) stationary state of hydrogen?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Principal quantum number: \(n = 3\). Ground state energy: \(E_1 = -13.6\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The energy of the \(n^{\text{th}}\) stationary state is:
\[ E_n = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute \(n = 3\):
\[ E_3 = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{3^2} = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{9} \approx -1.511\text{ eV} \approx -1.51\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The energy is negative and less negative than the ground state, as expected for an excited level. The energy is \(-1.51\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q11 - Total energy value of fourth stationary state

questiontext.text: What is the total energy of an electron in the \(n = 4\) stationary state of a hydrogen atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Principal quantum number: \(n = 4\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Bohr energy expression:
\[ E_n = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{n^2} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute \(n = 4\):
\[ E_4 = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{4^2} = -\frac{13.6\text{ eV}}{16} = -0.85\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Dividing \(13.6\) by \(16\) gives exactly \(0.85\). With the bound state negative sign, the energy is \(-0.85\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q12 - Potential energy of electron in first excited state

questiontext.text: In the first excited state (\(n = 2\)) of a hydrogen atom, the total energy of the electron is \(-3.40\text{ eV}\). What is its electrostatic potential energy in this state?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total energy in the \(n = 2\) state: \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For a Coulomb inverse-square central force orbit, the potential energy \(U\) is related to total energy \(E\) by:
\[ U = 2E \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\):
\[ U_2 = 2 \times (-3.40\text{ eV}) = -6.80\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The kinetic energy is \(K_2 = -E_2 = +3.40\text{ eV}\), so \(E = K + U = 3.40 - 6.80 = -3.40\text{ eV}\), verifying consistency. The potential energy is \(-6.80\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q13 - Kinetic energy of electron in first excited state

questiontext.text: What is the kinetic energy of the electron in the first excited state (\(n = 2\)) of a hydrogen atom, given that its total energy in this state is \(-3.40\text{ eV}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Total energy: \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For an inverse-square attractive potential, kinetic energy \(K\) and total energy \(E\) satisfy:
\[ K = -E \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\):
\[ K_2 = -(-3.40\text{ eV}) = +3.40\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Kinetic energy is positive and equal in magnitude to the total energy. The kinetic energy is \(+3.40\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q14 - Ionisation energy required from first excited state

questiontext.text: What is the minimum energy required to ionise a hydrogen atom that is already in its first excited state (\(n = 2\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial state: \(n = 2\) with total energy \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\). Final ionised state at infinity: \(E_\infty = 0\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The ionisation energy from an excited state \(n\) is the energy required to remove the electron to infinity:
\[ \Delta E_{\text{ionise}} = E_\infty - E_n \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute the values:
\[ \Delta E_{\text{ionise}} = 0\text{ eV} - (-3.40\text{ eV}) = +3.40\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
As \(n\) increases, the binding energy decreases, requiring less energy to ionise the atom. The required ionisation energy is \(3.40\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q15 - Orbital speed of electron in second level

questiontext.text: In a hydrogen atom, the orbital speed of the electron in the ground state is \(2.18 \times 10^6\text{ m/s}\). What is its orbital speed in the \(n = 2\) level?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Speed in the first orbit: \(v_1 = 2.18 \times 10^6\text{ m/s}\). Target state: \(n = 2\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
In the Bohr model, the orbital speed of an electron is inversely proportional to the principal quantum number:
\[ v_n = \frac{v_1}{n} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute \(n = 2\):
\[ v_2 = \frac{2.18 \times 10^6\text{ m/s}}{2} = 1.09 \times 10^6\text{ m/s} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The speed decreases by half, consistent with angular momentum and centripetal force requirements. The orbital speed is \(1.09 \times 10^6\text{ m/s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q16 - Orbital period ratio of second to first orbit

questiontext.text: In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, what is the ratio of the orbital time period of the electron in the \(n = 2\) orbit to that in the \(n = 1\) orbit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Principal quantum numbers: \(n_1 = 1\) and \(n_2 = 2\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The orbital period is \(T_n = \frac{2\pi r_n}{v_n}\). Since \(r_n \propto n^2\) and \(v_n \propto \frac{1}{n}\), the period scales as:
\[ T_n \propto \frac{n^2}{1/n} = n^3 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Take the ratio of periods:
\[ \frac{T_2}{T_1} = \left(\frac{2}{1}\right)^3 = 2^3 = 8 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Kepler's third law applied to Bohr orbits confirms \(T^2 \propto r^3 \implies T \propto r^{3/2} \propto (n^2)^{3/2} = n^3\). The ratio of the orbital periods is \(8 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q17 - Ratio of third to first orbit period values

questiontext.text: What is the ratio of the orbital revolution period of an electron in the \(n = 3\) state of hydrogen to that in the \(n = 1\) state?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Principal quantum numbers: \(n = 1\) and \(n = 3\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The orbital period of revolution in Bohr's model obeys:
\[ T_n \propto n^3 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Compute the ratio:
\[ \frac{T_3}{T_1} = \left(\frac{3}{1}\right)^3 = 3^3 = 27 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The period increases rapidly with quantum number, taking \(27\) times longer to complete a single revolution in the third orbit. The ratio is \(27 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q18 - Closest approach distance for alpha on gold nucleus

questiontext.text: In the Geiger-Marsden experiment, a \(5.5\text{ MeV}\) \(\alpha\)-particle emitted by \(^{214}_{83}\text{Bi}\) heads directly toward a gold nucleus (\(Z = 79\)). Given that a \(7.7\text{ MeV}\) \(\alpha\)-particle has a closest approach of \(3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\), what is the closest approach distance for this \(5.5\text{ MeV}\) particle?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial kinetic energies: \(K_1 = 7.7\text{ MeV}\) with distance \(d_1 = 3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\); \(K_2 = 5.5\text{ MeV}\). Target material is gold (\(Z = 79\)) for both.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The distance of closest approach is inversely proportional to kinetic energy:
\[ d = \frac{2Ze^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K} \implies d \propto \frac{1}{K} \implies \frac{d_2}{d_1} = \frac{K_1}{K_2} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute the given values:
\[ d_2 = d_1 \times \frac{K_1}{K_2} = (3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}) \times \frac{7.7\text{ MeV}}{5.5\text{ MeV}} \]
\[ d_2 = (3.0 \times 10^{-14}) \times 1.40 = 4.2 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m} = 42\text{ fm} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
A particle with lower kinetic energy cannot penetrate as close to the positively charged nucleus, turning back at a greater distance. The distance of closest approach is \(4.2 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q19 - Closest approach distance on silver target foil

questiontext.text: A \(7.7\text{ MeV}\) \(\alpha\)-particle has a distance of closest approach of \(3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\) on a gold nucleus (\(Z = 79\)). What would be the distance of closest approach for the same \(\alpha\)-particle on a silver nucleus (\(Z = 47\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Kinetic energy \(K = 7.7\text{ MeV}\) (constant). Gold atomic number: \(Z_{\text{Au}} = 79\) with \(d_{\text{Au}} = 3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\). Silver atomic number: \(Z_{\text{Ag}} = 47\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For constant kinetic energy, the distance of closest approach is directly proportional to the atomic number \(Z\):
\[ d \propto Z \implies \frac{d_{\text{Ag}}}{d_{\text{Au}}} = \frac{Z_{\text{Ag}}}{Z_{\text{Au}}} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute the values:
\[ d_{\text{Ag}} = d_{\text{Au}} \times \frac{47}{79} = (3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}) \times \frac{47}{79} \approx (3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}) \times 0.5949 \approx 1.78 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m} \approx 1.8 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Because silver has less nuclear positive charge, the repulsive force is weaker, allowing the \(\alpha\)-particle to get closer before coming to rest. The distance of closest approach is \(1.8 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q20 - de Broglie wavelength of electron in ground orbit

questiontext.text: In Louis de Broglie's model, the circumference of the first Bohr orbit (radius \(r_1 = 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\)) accommodates exactly one de Broglie wavelength (\(n = 1\)). What is the de Broglie wavelength of the ground-state electron?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of first orbit: \(r_1 = 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}\). Principal quantum number: \(n = 1\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to de Broglie's standing wave condition on a circular orbit:
\[ 2\pi r_n = n\lambda \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
For \(n = 1\):
\[ \lambda_1 = 2\pi r_1 = 2 \times 3.1416 \times (5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m}) \approx 6.2832 \times 5.3 \times 10^{-11}\text{ m} \approx 3.33 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The de Broglie wavelength is \(0.333\text{ nm} = 3.33\text{ Å}\), which is comparable to atomic spacing. The wavelength is \(3.33 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q21 - Photon energy emitted in hydrogen alpha transition

questiontext.text: In the hydrogen atom spectrum, the \(H_\alpha\) line of the Balmer series corresponds to an electron transition from \(n = 3\) to \(n = 2\). Given \(E_3 = -1.51\text{ eV}\) and \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\), what is the energy of the emitted photon?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial state energy: \(E_3 = -1.51\text{ eV}\). Final state energy: \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By Bohr's third postulate, the photon energy equals the energy difference between the initial and final stationary states:
\[ h\nu = E_i - E_f \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Calculate the energy difference:
\[ h\nu = -1.51\text{ eV} - (-3.40\text{ eV}) = -1.51\text{ eV} + 3.40\text{ eV} = 1.89\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
A photon energy of \(1.89\text{ eV}\) corresponds to red visible light (\(\lambda \approx 656\text{ nm}\)), which matches the \(H_\alpha\) line. The energy of the emitted photon is \(1.89\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q22 - Photon energy emitted in hydrogen beta transition

questiontext.text: In the hydrogen spectrum, what is the energy of the photon emitted in the transition from \(n = 4\) (\(E_4 = -0.85\text{ eV}\)) to \(n = 2\) (\(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial state energy: \(E_4 = -0.85\text{ eV}\). Final state energy: \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Bohr frequency condition:
\[ h\nu = E_4 - E_2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Compute the photon energy:
\[ h\nu = -0.85\text{ eV} - (-3.40\text{ eV}) = 3.40\text{ eV} - 0.85\text{ eV} = 2.55\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
An energy of \(2.55\text{ eV}\) corresponds to blue-green visible light (\(\lambda \approx 486\text{ nm}\)), which is the \(H_\beta\) line. The energy of the emitted photon is \(2.55\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q23 - Maximum photon energy in Balmer emission series

questiontext.text: What is the maximum photon energy (series limit) emitted in the Balmer series of atomic hydrogen, corresponding to a transition from \(n = \infty\) to \(n = 2\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial level: \(n_i = \infty\) with \(E_\infty = 0\text{ eV}\). Final level: \(n_f = 2\) with \(E_2 = -3.40\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The series limit represents the maximum energy difference in the series:
\[ \Delta E_{\max} = E_\infty - E_2 \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Calculate the energy difference:
\[ \Delta E_{\max} = 0\text{ eV} - (-3.40\text{ eV}) = 3.40\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The maximum energy emitted in the Balmer series is \(3.40\text{ eV}\), corresponding to the series limit wavelength of \(365\text{ nm}\). The photon energy is \(3.40\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q24 - Maximum photon energy in Paschen emission series

questiontext.text: In the infrared Paschen series of the hydrogen spectrum, transitions terminate at \(n = 3\) (\(E_3 = -1.51\text{ eV}\)). What is the maximum photon energy corresponding to the series limit (\(n = \infty \to 3\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Final state: \(n_f = 3\) with \(E_3 = -1.51\text{ eV}\). Initial state at the continuum limit: \(n_i = \infty\) with \(E_\infty = 0\text{ eV}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The maximum photon energy in any series terminating at level \(n\) is:
\[ \Delta E_{\max} = E_\infty - E_n = 0 - E_n = |E_n| \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Substitute \(E_3 = -1.51\text{ eV}\):
\[ \Delta E_{\max} = 0\text{ eV} - (-1.51\text{ eV}) = 1.51\text{ eV} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
A photon energy of \(1.51\text{ eV}\) corresponds to the Paschen series limit (\(\lambda \approx 820\text{ nm}\) in the infrared). The maximum photon energy is \(1.51\text{ eV}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q25 - Ratio of Coulomb force between Bohr orbits

questiontext.text: In the hydrogen atom, how does the magnitude of the electrostatic attractive force on the electron in the first Bohr orbit (\(n = 1\)) compare to that in the second Bohr orbit (\(n = 2\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Principal quantum numbers: \(n_1 = 1\) and \(n_2 = 2\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Coulomb's force of attraction is given by \(F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{e^2}{r^2}\). Since \(r_n \propto n^2\), the force scales with \(n\) as:
\[ F_n \propto \frac{1}{r_n^2} \propto \frac{1}{(n^2)^2} = \frac{1}{n^4} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Take the ratio of the forces in the two orbits:
\[ \frac{F_1}{F_2} = \left(\frac{n_2}{n_1}\right)^4 = \left(\frac{2}{1}\right)^4 = 2^4 = 16 \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Because radius doubles squared (factor of 4), the inverse-square force drops by a factor of \(4^2 = 16\). The ratio of the forces is \(16 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q26 - Calculated closest approach for alpha particle collision

questiontext.text: In a Geiger-Marsden experiment, an \(\alpha\)-particle of kinetic energy \(7.7\text{ MeV}\) (\(1.2 \times 10^{-12}\text{ J}\)) undergoes a head-on collision with a gold nucleus (\(Z = 79\)). Given \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\) and \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\), what is the distance of closest approach?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Kinetic energy \(K = 7.7\text{ MeV} = 1.2 \times 10^{-12}\text{ J}\), atomic number of gold \(Z = 79\), charge quantum \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\), Coulomb constant \(\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9.0 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
At the stopping distance \(d\), initial kinetic energy converts entirely into electrostatic potential energy:
\[ K = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{(2e)(Ze)}{d} \implies d = \frac{2Ze^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K} \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Substitution and Calculation
Evaluate the factor independent of \(Z\):
\[ \frac{2 e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K} = \frac{2 \times (9.0 \times 10^9) \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{1.2 \times 10^{-12}} = \frac{18.0 \times 10^9 \times 2.56 \times 10^{-38}}{1.2 \times 10^{-12}} = 3.84 \times 10^{-16}\text{ m} \]
Multiply by \(Z = 79\):
\[ d = 3.84 \times 10^{-16} \times 79 = 3.0336 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m} \approx 3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m} = 30\text{ fm} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The calculated value is \(3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\), which sets an upper limit on the nuclear radius. The distance of closest approach is \(3.0 \times 10^{-14}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ATOMS_MCQ_Q27 - Calculation of hydrogen orbital radius from ground energy

questiontext.text: The ground state energy of hydrogen is \(-13.6\text{ eV}\) (\(-2.18 \times 10^{-18}\text{ J}\)).
